docs.title: 14. Prompt Template Rules
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Prompt templates are in prompts/tutorial/, prompts/advanced/, prompts/api-reference/, and prompts/sdk/. They contain {placeholder} variables that form a CONTRACT with the node code.

  1. NEVER paraphrase, truncate, or summarize prompt templates — copy them byte-for-byte from the originals
  2. The {variable} placeholders are a CONTRACT — nodes MUST pass exactly matching kwargs to .format()
  3. To verify correctness: grep each template for {word} patterns. Every match must appear as a kwarg in the corresponding node's .format() call
  4. Templates use Python .format() syntax — any literal { or } in template text MUST be escaped as {{ or }}
  5. All 4 directories (tutorial/, advanced/, api-reference/, sdk/) have the SAME 6 template files. The tutorial/ and advanced/ directories share identical placeholder names. The api-reference/ and sdk/ templates may have different placeholder sets (e.g., api-reference/draft_chapters.md omits {tone_note}, {chapter_num}, {instruction_lang_note}, {code_comment_note}).

docs.title: Prompt Loading Pattern
docs.text:
# mode is one of: "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"
prompt_dir = mode  # Directly selects the prompt subdirectory
template_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
with open(template_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
    prompt_template = f.read()

docs.title: Common Prompts (prompts/common/)
docs.text: Shared prompts that are NOT mode-specific. Loaded directly by path, not via load_prompt_template().

docs.title: group_modules.md — LLM Nav Grouping
docs.text:
Template variables: | Variable | Source | Description | |---|---|---| | {project_name} | shared["project_name"] | Project display name | | {module_count} | len(chapter_files) | Number of documented modules | | {module_list} | Built from chapter_files + chapter_summaries | - module_name: summary per module | | {directory_tree} | shared["directory_tree"] | Project directory tree string | | {language_note} | Conditional on shared["language"] | "Section names MUST be in {language}." or empty |

Expected YAML response: 

sections:
  - name: "Section Name"
    modules: ["module_name_1", "module_name_2"]
  - name: "Parent Section"
    children:
      - name: "Child Section"
        modules: ["module_name_3"]

docs.title: translate_strings.md — LLM String Translation
docs.text: Template variables: | Variable | Source | Description | |---|---|---| | {language} | --language argument | The target language to translate strings into | | {entries} | Missing translations from utils/strings.csv | List or JSON of strings needing translation |

docs.title: Output Format Conventions
docs.text:
Standardized output formats enforced by prompt instructions to ensure consistency across chapters:

Mode Convention Prompt Instruction api-reference File path header > **Source:** \path/to/file.ext`` (blockquote with bold label)

docs.title: Mandatory Page Skeletons (draft_chapters.md)
docs.text:
Each mode's draft_chapters.md enforces a fixed set of ## headings. Only these headings are allowed at the ## level — the LLM must NOT invent headings like "Pipeline Context", "Key Architectural Capabilities", or "Standalone Execution Block". ### and #### headings are free-form.

Mode Skeleton (## headings) tutorial Motivation & Use Case → Key Concepts → How It Works → Under the Hood → Summary advanced Technical Overview → Implementation Deep-Dive → Data Structures → Error Handling → Practical Notes api-reference Technical Overview → Public API → Internal Helpers → Data Structures → Error Handling → See Also sdk Technical Overview → Public API → Configuration & Options → Data Structures → Error Handling → See Also

All ## skeleton headings MUST be translated to the target {language}.

docs.title: Function Documentation Depth
docs.text:
Depth scales proportionally to the function's logical complexity — NOT by counting lines of code:

Complexity Documentation approach Simple (single responsibility, linear flow) One code block + one explanation paragraph under ### Multi-phase (distinct logical phases) Split into #### sub-sections, one per logical phase. Each gets its own code block + explanation paragraph Very large (many distinct phases) Phase overview, then a #### sub-section per phase. There is NO cap on sub-sections — if a function has 12 logical phases, create 12 #### sub-sections

Phase names must describe the actual phase (e.g., "Tree Traversal", "Response Assembly") — NOT generic labels like "Implementation Walkthrough: Part 1".

Consistency rule: If two chapters cover functions of similar complexity, they MUST get similar documentation depth.

docs.title: Diagram & Mermaid Standards (ABSOLUTE)
docs.text:
NEVER use ASCII art — no +---+, |, -->, box-drawing characters, or plaintext diagrams. ALL diagrams must be fenced ```mermaid blocks using one of: flowchart TD, classDiagram, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram, erDiagram.

Mermaid rendering rules: - All flowcharts use flowchart TD (top-down only; never LR, RL, or BT) - Process nodes use rectangular brackets with quoted labels: nodeId["Label"] - Decision nodes MAY use diamond shape: nodeId{{"Decision?"}} - For 6+ nodes, use subgraph blocks to prevent flat sprawl - Define classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; once at the end, apply to first node of flow and each subgraph - Do NOT use %%{{init}}%% directives — the site handles theming

docs.title: Mandatory Data Structures Section
docs.text:
Required in api-reference, sdk, and advanced modes. Every type, schema, container class, and complex return dictionary shape must be documented with field-by-field tables:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | The abstraction name |
| `files` | `list[int]` | File indices containing this abstraction |

docs.title: Language-Agnostic Grouping (api-reference / sdk)
docs.text: Criteria for categorizing symbols into Public API, Internal Helpers, and Data Structures are language-agnostic. The LLM determines visibility using the language's own conventions — access modifiers, naming conventions, export mechanisms, header declarations, etc. For non-typed languages (HTML, CSS, config files), document structural contracts instead.

docs.title: Code Extraction Rules
docs.text:
• Code fidelity: preserve exact code and original comments without translation inside code fences
  • Block size caps: 30 lines (tutorial), 60 lines (advanced), 50 lines (api-reference/sdk)
  • Minimum 1 full paragraph (3-5 sentences) of technical explanation after every code block
  • Minimum 55-60% prose ratio across chapters

docs.title: Target Chapter Length
docs.text: Mode Word range tutorial 3,000–6,000 advanced 5,000–10,000 api-reference 3,000–8,000 sdk 3,000–6,000

docs.title: 15. Flow Wiring
docs.text:
Notes for AI: This is the EXACT content of flow.py. Reproduce it exactly.

from pocketflow import Flow
from nodes import (
    FetchRepo, ContextRouter, MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions,
    IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters,
    WriteChapters, CombineTutorial, DeterministicFileMapper
)

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

docs.title: 16. Code Organization & DRY Patterns
docs.text: Notes for AI: Always look for repeated code patterns and extract them into helper functions. When building nodes, check if the pattern you're about to write already exists as a helper. These are not optional suggestions — they are REQUIRED patterns.

docs.title: Mindset
docs.text: As you implement nodes, you will notice recurring operations: loading prompts, parsing YAML, counting tokens, resolving provider config. Do NOT copy-paste these inline. These are extracted into purpose-specific utility modules in utils/. This keeps the codebase maintainable and reduces the surface area for bugs.

docs.title: Required Helper Functions
docs.text: These helpers are organized by function across utility modules:

docs.title: load_prompt_template — utils/prompts.py
docs.text:
Loads a prompt template from prompts/{mode}/{template_name}.md. When mode is provided, it directly selects the subdirectory. When mode is None, falls back to legacy advanced_mode boolean. 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode
    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                        "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()
Used by: MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters (6 nodes)

docs.title: parse_yaml_response — utils/prompts.py
docs.text:
Extracts and parses YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks. 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e
Used by: MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, DeterministicFileMapper, CombineTutorial (7 nodes)

docs.title: count_tokens / input_token_budget — utils/token_utils.py
docs.text:
count_tokens(text) is the model-calibrated estimate (tiktoken × get_token_ratio()); input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level) is the prompt budget after reserving room for the response (Section 9). 

safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level)
tokens = count_tokens(entry)
Used by: ContextRouter, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships (budgets); every node (analytics)

docs.title: resolve_thinking_level — utils/thinking.py
docs.text:
Returns the thinking level for one LLM call site from shared["thinking_plan"] (Section 17). 

thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "identify_abstractions")
call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
Used by: every node that calls call_llm() (10 call sites)

docs.title: resolve_max_tokens — utils/token_utils.py
docs.text:
Resolves max_tokens from shared store or auto-detects from provider environment variables. 

def resolve_max_tokens(shared):
    """Resolve max_tokens from shared store or auto-detect from the active provider."""
    max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        return max_tokens
    _, model_name, endpoint, api_key = resolve_llm_settings()
    return get_model_context_length(endpoint, model_name, api_key)
Used by: ContextRouter, IdentifyAbstractions (2 nodes)

docs.title: Anti-Patterns to Avoid
docs.text: ❌ Don't ✅ Do Instead prompt_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", ...) inline in every node prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_abstractions", advanced_mode) yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1]... repeated 5× data = parse_yaml_response(response) try: enc = tiktoken.get_encoding(...) in 3 different methods tokens = count_tokens(text) (model-calibrated) provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER") + if/else in 2 nodes provider, model, endpoint, key = resolve_llm_settings() / max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared) safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95) safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level) thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level") in a node thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "<node_key>") Redefining import re inside functions when it's already imported at the top Use the top-level import

docs.title: When to Create New Helpers
docs.text: If you find yourself writing the same block of code (≥3 lines) in 2+ nodes, extract it as a module-level helper function. Name it descriptively and add a docstring explaining what it does, what it takes, and what it returns.

docs.title: main.py Modular Design
docs.text:
main() is a short orchestrator (~40 lines). All logic is extracted into module-level functions:

Function Signature Returns Description parse_arguments () -> tuple[ArgumentParser, Namespace] (parser, args) All argparse setup; returns parser (for .error()) and parsed args resolve_mode_and_project (args) -> tuple[str, str] (mode, project_name) Handles --advanced legacy flag, derives project name from args build_shared_store (args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name) -> dict shared dict Constructs the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes resolve_thinking_plan (args) -> tuple[str, dict, list[str]] (profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides) Pure (no emit), runs before init_output() so string translation uses the plan's translate_strings level _validate_thinking_args (args, invalid_overrides) -> None — Emits ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE (exit 1), WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED (override names a node not in thinking.MODE_NODES[mode]), and WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE — after init_output() detect_llm_config (args) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int] (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length) resolve_llm_settings() + context length display_config (args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan) -> None — Emits all CFG_* strings to console (startup order) — — parse_arguments → resolve_thinking_plan → init_output(auto_translate=False) → _check_quoting_errors / _validate_thinking_args → standalone --cleanup → check_anthropic_auth() (exit 1 on failure) → translate_missing_strings() → mode/project resolution → flow. Translation is an LLM call, so it runs only after arguments and credentials are checked. _emit_usage_summary () -> None — In finally: one LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY per provider used (llm_common.get_usage_summary(): calls, input/output/thinking/cache tokens, refusals, fallbacks, truncations, est. cost or CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN) _run_cleanup () -> None — Removes llm_cache_v2.json (+ .tmp), legacy llm_cache.json, and the logs/ directory

docs.title: Depth-First File Ordering (api-reference mode)
docs.text:
In DeterministicFileMapper.post(), chapter_order is sorted by directory depth (deepest first, then alphabetical within same depth). This ensures utility/leaf files are processed before orchestration files in WriteChapters, making their summaries available as previous_chapters_summary context when processing higher-level files.

shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
    chapter_order,
    key=lambda idx: (-modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep), modules[idx]["original_path"].lower()),
)

This ordering is language-agnostic — it works for any codebase (Python, C#, C++, Java, etc.) because it exploits the universal convention that utility files live in deeper directories.

docs.title: 17. LLM Providers & Thinking Flows
docs.text: Notes for AI: utils/llm_anthropic.py is the ONLY file that imports the anthropic SDK. utils/thinking.py is the ONLY place that defines per-node effort. Nodes never hard-code a thinking level.

docs.title: Thinking Plan (utils/thinking.py)
docs.text:
Every LLM call site has a NODE key. main.resolve_thinking_plan() builds shared["thinking_plan"] once: --thinking-override NODE=LEVEL > --thinking-level LEVEL (all nodes) > --thinking-profile table (+ per-mode adjustments). Nodes read their level with resolve_thinking_level(shared, "<node_key>") (falls back to shared["thinking_level"] when no plan exists).

NODE key Call site Workload filter_files DeterministicFileMapper Mechanical classification (api-reference) map_abstractions MapAbstractions (per batch) Extraction reduce_abstractions ReduceAbstractions Reasoning-heavy synthesis identify_abstractions IdentifyAbstractions Reasoning-heavy synthesis analyze_relationships AnalyzeRelationships Reasoning-heavy synthesis order_chapters OrderChapters Planning write_chapters WriteChapters (per chapter) Long-form generation chapter_summary WriteChapters (per chapter, summary_thinking_level) Mechanical summary group_modules CombineTutorial → write_mkdocs_output nav grouping Light structuring translate_strings utils/i18n.auto_translate (via init_output) Mechanical translation

Profiles (auto = balanced on ANTHROPIC, GEMINI and OPENROUTER (thinking.PROFILED_PROVIDERS), off elsewhere; off = every node None → model default):

NODE economy balanced quality max filter_files low low medium medium map_abstractions low medium high xhigh reduce_abstractions medium high high max identify_abstractions medium high high max analyze_relationships low medium high xhigh order_chapters low medium high high write_chapters low medium high xhigh chapter_summary low low medium medium group_modules low medium high high translate_strings low low medium medium

Rationale: reasoning-heavy synthesis (identify/reduce) gets the most effort; relationship analysis only feeds the summary, diagram and ordering; chapter writing runs N times (hundreds in api-reference), so shipped profiles stop at high — Opus 5.5 at medium already beats Opus 5 at high on knowledge work. xhigh/max only in the explicit max profile (use when a gain has been measured).

Per-mode adjustments: economy → write_chapters=medium for advanced (design-rationale chapters, at most max_abstraction_num calls). MODE_NODES lists which nodes can run per mode (api-reference: filter_files, write_chapters, chapter_summary, group_modules, translate_strings; other modes: the analysis nodes + write_chapters, chapter_summary, translate_strings) — used for the config display and WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED.

Provider mapping of a level: ANTHROPIC → output_config.effort (xhigh → high on the 4.6 family; pre-4.6 models such as Haiku 4.5 → budget_tokens 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 24,576 / 32,000); GEMINI 3.x → thinking_level (per-model set, llm_config.GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS), Gemini 2.5 → thinking_budget (GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS clamped to GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES); OPENROUTER → reasoning.effort clamped to the catalog's supported_efforts, or reasoning.max_tokens for budget-only models; OLLAMA → low/medium/high. The startup display shows it as CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT (llm_config.describe_thinking_support).

docs.title: call_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_anthropic.py)
docs.text:
• Model: ANTHROPIC_MODEL, default claude-opus-5-5 (1M context, 128K output). Limits from the Models API (client.models.retrieve(model) → max_input_tokens, max_tokens), cached per process; offline fallback 1M/128K (Haiku 4.5: 200K/64K) with WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP.
  • Thinking: adaptive-thinking models (Opus 5.x, Sonnet 5, Fable/Mythos, Opus 4.6–4.8, Sonnet 4.6) get thinking={"type": "adaptive"} and, when a level is set, output_config={"effort": level} (minimal → low). With no level (model default), thinking is omitted on Opus/Sonnet 4.6–4.8, where omission means no thinking; Opus/Sonnet 5.x, Fable and Mythos think adaptively either way. Claude Opus 5.5 cannot disable thinking and defaults to medium, so the plan sets effort explicitly. With --debug, display="summarized" and the summaries are written to the log file only.
  • Never sent: temperature/top_p/top_k, assistant prefill, budget_tokens on adaptive models (all 400 on Opus 5.5).
  • max_tokens (thinking counts toward it): llm_config.anthropic_planned_output(model, level) — adaptive models: ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT (minimal/low 32K, medium/high/None 64K, xhigh 96K, max 128K); Haiku 4.5 and older: ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL + 16K for the reply. input_token_budget reserves the same value. Level → effort normalization (llm_config.anthropic_effort) is shared too. ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is a hard cap: planned max_tokens = min(table, cap), and the truncation retry never exceeds it. Ceiling = min(model output cap, context − count_tokens(prompt) − ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN (2,000), cap), min 4,096; WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED only when the ceiling is < 90% of the plan. The prompt is tokenized once per call.
  • Streaming: every request uses messages.stream(...) + get_final_message() (large max_tokens never hit HTTP timeouts).
  • Refusal fallbacks: ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS=default (Opus 5.x and Fable 5.x only) → beta server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 + extra_body={"fallbacks": "default"} on client.beta.messages.stream; a comma-separated model list (any model, e.g. Mythos 5.1) → beta server-side-fallback-2026-06-01 + [{"model": ...}]; off disables. A fallback-served answer emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED. Cost with fallbacks sums usage.iterations, each at its own model's price; an attempt with 0 output tokens (declined before output) is unbilled.
  • Prompt caching: ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE=on adds top-level cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"}. Off by default: templates start with per-call content (chapter name, batch files), so only exact retries share a prefix — the 1.25× write cost is not repaid on single-shot calls.
  • Response: text = concatenated text blocks (thinking/fallback blocks ignored). A reply that ends with max_tokens / model_context_window_exceeded is returned as TruncatedResponse (a str subclass with truncated = True), which call_llm never caches. Refusal / truncation handling: Section 13.
  • Usage: per call, ANTHROPIC USAGE | ... (tokens, cache, est. cost, observed_token_ratio = billed input ÷ tiktoken count — use it to tune ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO) goes to the log; totals are emitted after the flow as LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY. Prices (USD/MTok in/out/cache-read) live in _PRICING; 5-minute cache writes = 1.25× input.

docs.title: Credentials & preflight (utils/llm_config.check_anthropic_auth)
docs.text:
The anthropic SDK (zero-arg anthropic.Anthropic()) resolves credentials itself: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY → ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN → the ant auth login profile (ANTHROPIC_PROFILE or the active one, stored under ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR, default %APPDATA%\Anthropic on Windows / ~/.config/anthropic elsewhere) → Workload Identity Federation. Empty variables count as unset. For OAuth profiles the SDK merges its oauth-2025-04-20 beta header with ours (fallback beta), so betas=[...] is safe.

check_anthropic_auth() -> bool (SDK-free; returns True for every other provider) runs before any LLM call in both entry points — main() (after argument validation, before translate_missing_strings() and the flow) and the utils/call_llm.py self-test (after init_output):

Step Condition Result 1 anthropic package not importable ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING (pip install -r requirements.txt) → False 2 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN non-empty (both → WARN_ANTHROPIC_KEY_AND_TOKEN) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK → True 3 Federation vars (ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, _ORGANIZATION_ID, _SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID + _IDENTITY_TOKEN[_FILE]) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK → True 4 ant on PATH run ant auth status (30 s timeout, empty key vars removed from its env). Its exit code is not a health signal, so parse_ant_auth_status() reads the (active) rows of the Credentials / Workspace sections (token prefixes redacted). Active credential → ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK (source + workspace) → True; none → ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN + the (redacted) status output + help → False; subprocess error/timeout → WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED → True 5 ant not on PATH stored credentials/*.json in the config dir → WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND → True; otherwise ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS + help (incl. OS-specific ANTHROPIC_AUTH_HELP_INSTALL_ANT_{WIN,MAC,LINUX}: winget install Anthropic.Ant / brew install anthropics/tap/ant / release packages, each with a go install or zip fallback) → False

Help lines: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_HELP_HEADER, _KEY (API key from platform.claude.com/settings/keys), _INSTALL_ANT_* (only when ant is missing), _LOGIN (ant auth login / ant auth status), _NOTE (leave the key unset; billed to the API org, not a Claude.ai plan). Interactive login is for your own machine; CI uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or federation.

utils/call_llm.py adds the repo root to sys.path when run as a script, so the self-test works as both python utils/call_llm.py and python -m utils.call_llm.

docs.title: call_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_gemini.py)
docs.text:
The only module that imports google-genai (>= 1.56: thinking_level MINIMAL/MEDIUM; 1.51 had LOW/HIGH only; older SDKs reject the field).

Model (prefix, longest wins) Thinking control Levels Default when omitted gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.7-flash thinking_level low, medium, high (MINIMAL errors) medium gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash(-lite) thinking_level minimal, low, medium, high medium (Flash-Lite: minimal) gemini-3.1-pro(-preview) thinking_level low, medium, high (cannot turn off) high gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash thinking_level minimal, low, medium, high minimal / high other gemini-3.x, gemini-flash-latest / gemini-pro-latest, newer families thinking_level low, medium, high — gemini-2.5-pro / -flash / -flash-lite thinking_budget 128-32,768 / 1-24,576 / 512-24,576 dynamic gemini-1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants, non-Gemini ids none (WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED) — —

Model ids are normalized first (llm_config.gemini_model_id: models/… and publishers/google/models/… prefixes stripped, lower-cased).

  • thinking_level and thinking_budget are never sent together (400). Levels outside the set clamp (WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED, once per model+level); xhigh/max → high. No level → no thinking_config (model default). include_thoughts=True only with --debug (summaries go to the log).
  • max_output_tokens = llm_config.gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit): minimal/low 32,768, else 65,536 (the 3.x / 2.5 output limit, thinking included), capped by GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Gemini's input and output limits are separate, so output is not reduced for large prompts and input_token_budget reserves only CONTEXT_MARGIN.
  • Limits: models.get (input_token_limit, output_token_limit) on AI Studio, cached; Vertex AI (SDK maps no limits) and failures → GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS (1,048,576 / 65,536; WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP).
  • One client per process: HttpOptions(timeout=GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS×1000 ms (default 1800 s, total deadline), retry_options=HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, 408/429/5xx)); Vertex via vertexai=True, project, location=GEMINI_LOCATION (default global — Gemini 3.x is not served from us-central1); AI Studio via vertexai=False, api_key.
  • Requests stream (generate_content_stream): text = non-thought parts; prompt_feedback from the first chunk; the last usage_metadata and finish_reason win. Never sends temperature/top_p/top_k (deprecated on 3.x).
  • Usage: input = prompt_token_count (incl. cached), output = candidates + thoughts (thinking is billed as output), cost from _PRICING (standard prices, AI Studio = Vertex global; >200K-prompt tier for Pro; 3.6–3.8 Flash at the introductory _INTRO_PRICING through 2026-12-31; Vertex regional endpoints +10%; unknown models → cost n/a).
  • Retired ids (GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS: id → (replacement, still aliased on AI Studio)): gemini-3-pro-preview on AI Studio → WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (served by 3.1 Pro Preview); on Vertex, and gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview anywhere → ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (preflight fails).
  • Vertex locations per model (GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS, longest prefix): 3.1 Pro / 3 Flash / 3 Pro → global; 3.8 Flash Cyber → global, us; 3.5 Flash → any (also single regions); other 3.x → global, us, eu. us / eu use the aiplatform.{us|eu}.rep.googleapis.com endpoints.

docs.title: call_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_openrouter.py)
docs.text:
Catalog-driven (llm_config.openrouter_model_info: exact id, canonical_slug, a dated canonical slug only (anthropic/claude-4.6-opus → …-20260205; looser prefixes are not matched), routing suffixes :nitro/:floor/:online/…, ~…-latest aliases via alias_target). The catalog is fetched from {OPENROUTER_BASE_URL}/v1/models and cached on success; after a failure callers get None and the fetch is retried after a 60 s cooldown (WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE once). Family checks (rejects_sampling_params, get_token_ratio) resolve aliases through the catalog, and _normalize_claude_id maps version-first ids (claude-4.7-opus → claude-opus-4-7).

Catalog reasoning Request supported_efforts list reasoning.effort = level clamped to the list (never none; WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED once) supported_efforts key missing + supports_max_tokens (e.g. Qwen 3.8 Flash) reasoning.max_tokens = 1,024 / 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 24,576 / 32,000 for minimal…max (kept below max_tokens) supported_efforts null / key missing otherwise (e.g. Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5) reasoning.effort = level (OpenRouter converts to a budget) no reasoning and not in supported_parameters no reasoning (WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED once) model not in catalog / catalog unavailable reasoning.effort = level (unverified)
  • reasoning.exclude = not --debug (reasoning is billed either way; with --debug it is logged).
  • max_tokens: openrouter_output_budget(model, level) (shared per-effort table capped by top_provider.max_completion_tokens, 32K when that is unknown, and OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), clamped to context − prompt − CONTEXT_MARGIN (min 4,096). Omitted for a model missing from the catalog unless OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is set.
  • temperature (OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE, default 0.7) only when: no reasoning requested, not rejects_sampling_params(model) (Claude 4.7+/5.x, Gemini 3.x), temperature in supported_parameters, and the model is neither mandatory nor default_enabled reasoning.
  • SSE streaming (stream: true; lines split as bytes and decoded per line — str.splitlines() would break JSON containing U+2028; :-prefixed keep-alive lines skipped; read timeout OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS between events). A proxy that answers with one application/json body is parsed as a single chunk. Headers Authorization: Bearer (when a key is set). App attribution is opt-in (llm_openrouter._attribution_headers()): only when OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set are HTTP-Referer (that URL), X-OpenRouter-Title and legacy X-Title ("Codebase Knowledge Builder") sent; unset → no attribution headers.
  • Usage from the final chunk: prompt / completion (incl. reasoning) / completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens / prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens/cache_write_tokens / cost (USD, authoritative; with BYOK, cost_details.upstream_inference_cost is added).
  • Claude 4.6+ through OpenRouter: effort → Anthropic output_config.effort (xhigh → high on 4.6, minimal → low); Gemini 3.x: effort → thinkingLevel.

Success → LLM_AUTH_OK. - Other providers → True.

docs.title: flow.py
docs.text:
Source: flow.py

Following the token sizing, context budgeting, and calibration mechanics implemented in token_utils.py, the flow.py module establishes the high-level execution topology for the entire documentation generation pipeline. While token budgeting utilities operate at the granular prompt and payload level, flow.py defines the macro-architectural orchestration layer, determining how codebase data flows between computational nodes, when conditional branching occurs, and how processing paths converge to produce structured technical documentation.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The flow.py module serves as the central workflow definition engine for Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. Built on top of the lightweight PocketFlow graph orchestration framework, it declaratively defines the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) that executes repository crawling, abstraction extraction, relational architecture analysis, chapter ordering, drafting, and static-site synthesis. The module encapsulates the entire end-to-end lifecycle into a single factory function, create_tutorial_flow(), abstracting away graph instantiation and wiring from the application entry point in main.py.

At runtime, the flow coordinates ten discrete task nodes imported from nodes.py. It handles three distinct structural pathways through dynamic routing: 1. Direct Path ("direct"): Sized for repositories whose code files fit comfortably within the LLM's active context window, routing directly through global abstraction identification (IdentifyAbstractions). 2. Batch Path ("batch"): Sized for massive codebases that exceed single-prompt context limits, breaking files into chunked sub-groups for parallel abstraction mapping (MapAbstractions) followed by an LLM-driven hierarchical reduction phase (ReduceAbstractions). 3. Deterministic Path ("deterministic"): Bypasses AI abstraction mapping entirely when configured for mode-specific direct file documentation (such as per-file API reference generators), dispatching directly to DeterministicFileMapper and bypassing intermediary relational analysis to feed raw file mappings directly into chapter drafting.

The following top-down workflow diagram illustrates the structural routing, node dependencies, and graph convergence constructed by flow.py:

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Constructs, configures, and returns the executable PocketFlow.Flow instance containing the full codebase documentation pipeline. The function manages the instantiation of all underlying execution nodes from nodes.py, configures fault-tolerant retry parameters across inference-backed stages, links execution dependencies via operator overloading (>> and -), logs graph generation telemetry via output.py, and designates FetchRepo as the root entry point.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * Flow: A fully wired PocketFlow.Flow execution graph initialized with FetchRepo as the starting node (start=fetch_repo).

Raises: * This function does not raise runtime exceptions directly during construction; graph validation or node initialization errors are delegated to the underlying pocketflow library or node constructors.

Implementation Phases:

docs.title: Node Instantiation and Parameter Configuration
docs.text:
fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

During this initial phase, the function instantiates ten node objects. Distinct operational requirements are reflected in their initialization arguments: purely deterministic or filesystem-bound nodes (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) are instantiated with default retry parameters because their execution relies on deterministic local logic or terminal disk I/O. Conversely, all nodes interfacing with remote LLM provider APIs (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper) are explicitly injected with max_retries=5 and wait=20. This ensures that downstream transient network anomalies, remote provider HTTP 429 rate limits, and JSON/YAML deserialization issues are retried with 20-second backoffs before failing the flow.

docs.title: Graph Topology and Routing Definition
docs.text:
fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

This phase uses PocketFlow domain-specific operators to wire the pipeline's execution topology. Unconditional sequential steps are defined using the shift operator (>>), such that fetch_repo >> context_router ensures filesystem harvesting completes before evaluation starts. The conditional branching operator (- action >> target) splits execution from ContextRouter along three discrete paths based on repository size and mode ("direct", "batch", and "deterministic"). The graph then reconverges: both the "direct" and "batch" pipelines merge at AnalyzeRelationships, flow through OrderChapters, and reach WriteChapters. Concurrently, the "deterministic" path bypasses structural analysis entirely and links directly from DeterministicFileMapper to WriteChapters. Finally, chapter authoring unconditionally transitions to CombineTutorial for final site and file compilation.

docs.title: Telemetry Logging and Flow Encapsulation
docs.text:
emit_raw("DEBUG", "create_tutorial_flow | constructed PocketFlow execution graph", dest="LOG")
    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The final phase logs the graph creation event directly to disk logs using emit_raw() from utils/output.py. The call routes to dest="LOG" to prevent diagnostic noise from polluting standard interactive console streams. Once logged, the function wraps the complete execution topology into a pocketflow.Flow instance by binding fetch_repo as the designated root node, returning the flow object for downstream execution by main.py.

Example: 

# Call site extracted from main.py:
from flow import create_tutorial_flow

# ...
flow = create_tutorial_flow()
shared_context = {
    "repo_path": repo_path,
    # ... runtime parameters
}
flow.run(shared_context)

docs.text: The flow.py module defines the structural integration between the underlying PocketFlow engine and the node implementations in nodes.py. It operates over the following structural contracts:

docs.text:
The nodes instantiated within flow.py adhere to specific configuration profiles depending on whether they perform deterministic operations or remote inference:

Node Variable Target Node Class Execution Category Configured Retries (max_retries) Backoff (wait) Upstream Dependencies Downstream Targets fetch_repo FetchRepo Deterministic I/O Default (0) Default (0) None (Start Node) context_router context_router ContextRouter Evaluation / Routing Default (0) Default (0) fetch_repo identify_abstractions, map_abstractions, deterministic_mapper identify_abstractions IdentifyAbstractions LLM Inference 5 20s context_router ("direct") analyze_relationships map_abstractions MapAbstractions LLM Inference 5 20s context_router ("batch") reduce_abstractions reduce_abstractions ReduceAbstractions LLM Inference 5 20s map_abstractions analyze_relationships deterministic_mapper DeterministicFileMapper LLM / Fallback 5 20s context_router ("deterministic") write_chapters analyze_relationships AnalyzeRelationships LLM Inference 5 20s identify_abstractions, reduce_abstractions order_chapters order_chapters OrderChapters LLM Inference 5 20s analyze_relationships write_chapters write_chapters WriteChapters LLM Inference 5 20s order_chapters, deterministic_mapper combine_tutorial combine_tutorial CombineTutorial Deterministic I/O Default (0) Default (0) write_chapters None (End Node)

docs.title: Branch Action Routing Contract
docs.text:
The context_router node outputs string action tokens that determine edge traversal across the conditional branches:

Action Identifier Trigger Condition Activated Node Skipped Subgraphs "direct" Single-prompt codebase token size below context ceiling. IdentifyAbstractions map_abstractions, reduce_abstractions, deterministic_mapper "batch" Large codebase token size exceeding context ceiling; requires batching. MapAbstractions identify_abstractions, deterministic_mapper "deterministic" Operational mode specifies 1:1 file-to-chapter documentation. DeterministicFileMapper identify_abstractions, map_abstractions, reduce_abstractions, analyze_relationships, order_chapters

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The flow.py file delegates runtime exception handling to PocketFlow and the internal retry logic of individual nodes. However, it implements proactive fault tolerance through constructor parameter injection:

  • Inference Rate Limiting & Transient Flakiness: All nodes interacting with external LLMs (map_abstractions, reduce_abstractions, identify_abstractions, analyze_relationships, order_chapters, write_chapters, and deterministic_mapper) are configured with max_retries=5 and wait=20. When an underlying node encounters an API error, rate limit (HTTP 429), or malformed response format, PocketFlow intercepts the failure and sleeps for 20 seconds before retrying the node's prep -> exec -> post cycle, up to 5 times.
  • Deterministic Isolation: Nodes executing deterministic operations (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) omit max_retries and wait. Failures within these stages (e.g., repository path not found, disk full, or write permission denied) are treated as fatal configuration or environmental errors and bubble up immediately to main.py without delaying the user with redundant retry cycles.

docs.title: main.py
docs.text: Source: main.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Serving as the primary runtime entry point for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder toolchain, main.py bridges user-specified command-line configurations with the execution graph declared in flow.py. While flow.py defines the macro-architectural Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) and data dependencies across discrete analysis nodes, main.py orchestrates the system's operational lifecycle: initializing environment parameters, validating inputs defensively, verifying remote API credentials, constructing the centralized mutable blackboard context (shared), dispatching workflow execution, and finalizing telemetry.

The module executes a disciplined multi-stage bootstrapping procedure. It begins by loading local environment definitions through python-dotenv and compiling command-line arguments using argparse. Before delegating work to LLM nodes, main.py executes preflight validations: verifying that shell glob patterns did not inadvertently swallow other CLI flags, evaluating provider authentication credentials through utils/llm_config.py, configuring localized string registries via utils/output.py, and synthesizing a per-node reasoning effort plan through utils/thinking.py. Once preflight criteria are satisfied, the script builds a unified shared dictionary that encapsulates configuration parameters, input sources, filtering sets, and placeholder output references.

During the execution phase, main.py instantiates the PocketFlow graph via create_tutorial_flow() and executes it against the shared state dictionary. A critical architectural invariant of this orchestrator is robust session durability: the pipeline execution is enclosed within a comprehensive try...finally block. Regardless of whether processing succeeds, halts on interruption, or crashes due to upstream rate limits, main.py guarantees the invocation of _emit_usage_summary() and shutdown(), ensuring that session costs, token usage metrics, and audit log file handles from utils/llm_common.py and utils/output.py are flushed to disk and displayed to the user.

docs.title: parse_arguments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_arguments() -> tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]:

Description: Configures the command-line argument schema, binds positional and keyword flags, defines custom argument validation types, and parses invocation parameters into an argparse.Namespace object. It handles mutual exclusivity between --repo and --dir, sets pipeline defaults, and registers flags across ingestion limits, documentation generation modes, static site generation, incremental build caching, and cognitive reasoning tiers.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]: A two-element tuple containing the active ArgumentParser instance (retained for contextual error formatting and introspection) and the populated Namespace encapsulating all parsed CLI options.

Raises: * SystemExit: Implicitly raised by argparse when arguments violate declared constraints, unexpected flags are encountered, or required options are absent.

Example: 

# Extracted from main.py: main() orchestrator entry point
parser, args = parse_arguments()
# Resolved silently before init_output(): string translation itself uses the plan's translate_strings level.
thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)

The function defines flags for repository sources (--repo, --dir, --cleanup), project identifiers (-n, --name, -t, --token, -o, --output), and path filters (-i, --include, -e, --exclude, -s, --max-size). It exposes documentation generation profiles through --mode (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), --mkdocs, --incremental, and --force-rebuild. Additionally, it binds granular LLM reasoning parameters (--thinking-level, --thinking-profile, --thinking-override) and batching configurations (--batch, --force-batch).

docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str]:

Description: Normalizes the active documentation mode and derives the target project name from input sources. It arbitrates between the legacy --advanced boolean flag and explicit --mode selections, warning the user if conflicting flags are supplied. If an explicit project name is omitted from CLI arguments, it dynamically computes a fallback identifier using the directory name of local paths or the trailing slug of a Git repository URL (stripping .git suffixes).

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Populated CLI options container.

Returns: * tuple[str, str]: A tuple of (mode, project_name) where mode is one of 'tutorial', 'advanced', 'api-reference', or 'sdk', and project_name is the resolved canonical project directory name.

Example: 

def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name

The function first checks if args.advanced was toggled. If true, it enforces mode = "advanced" and emits WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE if --mode had also been configured to something other than 'tutorial'. For project name resolution, it prioritizes args.name; otherwise, it extracts the basename of the absolute local path for --dir, strips trailing slashes and Git extensions from remote URLs for --repo, or defaults conservatively to "project".

docs.title: build_shared_store()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_shared_store(args: argparse.Namespace, github_token: str | None, mode: str, thinking_plan: dict[str, str | None], project_name: str) -> dict[str, any]:

Description: Assembles the master blackboard context (shared) utilized by all PocketFlow execution nodes. It transforms CLI arguments, authentication tokens, normalized patterns, and resolved reasoning strategies into a single mutable state dictionary. Furthermore, it initializes empty payload slots for ingestion assets, identified abstractions, relational maps, chapter orderings, drafted Markdown contents, and final disk locations.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line arguments. * github_token (str | None): Authenticated GitHub API token, or None if unauthenticated. * mode (str): Resolved documentation mode string. * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Mapping of individual workflow node identifiers to assigned thinking effort levels. * project_name (str): Resolved canonical project name.

Returns: * dict[str, any]: The centralized state dictionary consumed by nodes.py and flow.py.

Example: 

def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": project_name,  # Resolved once in main so logs, --force-rebuild and output agree
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities: global level (legacy) + per-node plan (utils/thinking.py)
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        "thinking_plan": thinking_plan,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }

This constructor ensures that file exclusion sets merge the repository's internal rules with the static baseline catalog DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS from utils/exclude_patterns.py. It records operational controls, such as use_cache (the inverse of args.no_cache) and advanced_mode (derived from mode == "advanced"), guaranteeing downstream compatibility across heterogeneous node implementations.

docs.title: detect_llm_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def detect_llm_config(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int]:

Description: Discovers the active LLM provider identity, target model name, base API endpoint URL, and effective context window limit from the runtime environment and CLI overrides. It delegates provider discovery to resolve_llm_settings() and resolves maximum token context length by either respecting args.max_tokens or querying get_model_context_length() from utils/llm_config.py.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Populated CLI options container containing optional max_tokens constraints.

Returns: * tuple[str, str, str, str, int]: A 5-tuple representing: 1. provider (str): Resolved vendor string ("anthropic", "gemini", or "openrouter"). 2. model_name (str): Model family or deployment name. 3. endpoint_url (str): Target HTTP(S) completion endpoint. 4. api_key (str): Active API key retrieved from environment variables. 5. context_length (int): Input token context window ceiling.

Example: 

def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.llm_config import get_model_context_length

    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key = resolve_llm_settings()
    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length

The function utilizes deferred local imports of get_model_context_length from utils/llm_config.py to preserve fast initialization. By allowing args.max_tokens to short-circuit dynamic context discovery, developers can manually bound pipeline memory footprints when operating on constrained tiers or non-standard models.

docs.title: resolve_thinking_plan()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_thinking_plan(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]:

Description: Constructs the per-node reasoning effort plan based on --thinking-override, --thinking-level, and --thinking-profile. This function is strictly pure and performs no console emissions, enabling it to execute before utils/output.py is initialized. This early resolution ensures that string localization tasks executed during output bootstrapping can query their assigned thinking level.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line options.

Returns: * tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]: A 3-tuple containing: 1. resolved_profile (str): Name of the resolved thinking profile ("global", "auto", "balanced", etc.). 2. thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Mapping of node key strings (e.g., 'identify_abstractions', 'write_chapters') to normalized reasoning tiers or None. 3. invalid_overrides (list[str]): List of unrecognized or malformed CLI override strings for subsequent diagnostic validation.

Example: 

def resolve_thinking_plan(args):
    """Build the per-node thinking plan from --thinking-override / --thinking-level / --thinking-profile.

    Pure (no emit): runs before init_output(). Validation messages come from _validate_thinking_args().

    Returns:
        tuple[str, dict, list[str]]: (resolved profile name, {node_key: level | None}, invalid override strings)
    """
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, invalid = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    profile = "global" if args.thinking_level else resolve_profile_name(args.thinking_profile, resolve_llm_settings()[0])
    return profile, build_thinking_plan(profile, mode, args.thinking_level, overrides), invalid

The function leverages utils/thinking.py utilities. It maps the operational mode, evaluates CLI override tokens into a valid mapping and an invalid tracking list, checks whether a global thinking effort level overrides the active profile, resolves the profile against the detected LLM provider, and outputs the final per-node execution plan dictionary.

docs.title: display_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def display_config(args: argparse.Namespace, mode: str, provider: str, model_name: str, endpoint_url: str, context_length: int, log_file: str, thinking_profile: str, thinking_plan: dict[str, str | None]) -> None:

Description: Emits a formatted operational summary to the console and session log files before repository analysis begins. It outputs the source target, active language, AI provider details, endpoint addresses, model context ceilings, reasoning effort matrices, batch thresholds, caching flags, and filesystem log locations using localized UI message keys.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): The active CLI namespace. * mode (str): Documentation generation mode. * provider (str): Active LLM vendor identifier. * model_name (str): Model deployment identifier. * endpoint_url (str): Active API endpoint. * context_length (int): Token context window size. * log_file (str): Absolute path to the active disk log file. * thinking_profile (str): Resolved thinking effort profile name. * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Node-to-level reasoning assignment dictionary.

Returns: * None

Example: 

def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_PROFILE", value=thinking_profile)
    if any(thinking_plan.values()):
        emit("CFG_THINKING_PLAN", value=describe_plan(thinking_plan, mode))
    emit("CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT", value=describe_thinking_support(provider, model_name))
    emit("CFG_BATCH_SIZE", value=f"{args.batch}")
// ...
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block

The function standardizes boolean representation by querying translated string tokens (CFG_VALUE_ENABLED and CFG_VALUE_DISABLED) from utils/output.py. If incremental caching is enabled, it notes whether a forced rebuild was requested. For api-reference mode, it replaces numeric abstraction ceilings with the localized key CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX.

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: The primary procedural orchestrator of the entire CLI application. It coordinates argument parsing, reasoning plan resolution, logging configuration, quote error checks, preflight authentication, string translation, incremental cache invalidation, shared store construction, pipeline graph instantiation, error-resilient execution, and teardown telemetry.

Due to its orchestration responsibilities, its implementation is divided into five distinct logical phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: CLI and Thinking Plan Initialization
docs.text:
Parses command-line inputs and calculates the per-node reasoning plan before initializing the console presentation layer.

    parser, args = parse_arguments()
    # Resolved silently before init_output(): string translation itself uses the plan's translate_strings level.
    thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)
    # Translation of missing strings is an LLM call: deferred until arguments and credentials are checked.
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=thinking_plan["translate_strings"],
        debug=args.debug,
        auto_translate=False,
    )
    _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)
    _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)

In this initial phase, the reasoning effort plan is computed in total isolation without emitting console logs. This ensures that when init_output is invoked, it can configure the translation subsystem with the precise reasoning budget allocated for translate_strings. Following output initialization, the CLI flags undergo defensive inspection for shell quoting mistakes and invalid override tokens.

docs.title: Phase 2: Preflight Validation and Internationalization
docs.text:
Evaluates standalone cleanup requests, source availability, LLM provider credentials, and missing translation entries.

    # Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return

    # Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

    # Fail fast (with setup instructions) before crawling if Claude cannot authenticate
    if not check_llm_auth():
        sys.exit(1)
    translate_missing_strings()

If the invocation is a standalone cleanup task (--cleanup without --dir or --repo), cache stores and log directories are purged immediately, terminating the process early. For pipeline generation runs, the orchestrator asserts that at least one repository target was provided. It then invokes check_llm_auth() to verify provider credentials and SDK compatibility. Once authentication is confirmed, translate_missing_strings() processes missing target language entries.

docs.title: Phase 3: Project Identity and Cache Validation
docs.text:
Resolves repository metadata, verifies documentation mode constraints, and arbitrates cache invalidation.

    # Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
    elif args.token:
        emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

    mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
        emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
        args.incremental = False

    # --force-rebuild requires --incremental
    if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        output_base = args.output or "output"
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            os.remove(manifest_path)
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED", path=manifest_path)
        else:
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_NO_MANIFEST", path=manifest_path)

    # Warn about args ignored in api-reference mode
    if mode == "api-reference" and args.force_batch:
        emit("WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF")
        args.force_batch = False

This phase resolves GitHub personal access tokens, warns when tokens are supplied without remote repositories, and computes canonical project basenames. It validates the constraints of the incremental cache engine, ensuring that incremental compilation is applied exclusively to api-reference documentation modes. If --force-rebuild is requested alongside --incremental, the on-disk cache manifest .doc_cache_manifest.json is located and unlinked.

docs.title: Phase 4: Context Store Assembly and Logging Initialization
docs.text:
Constructs the central shared context dictionary, inspects LLM limits, initializes disk logs, and prints configuration telemetry.

    shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
    display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)

The phase compiles all runtime state into the shared dictionary, inspects runtime LLM context length boundaries via detect_llm_config(), opens a dedicated run log file via configure_logging() (e.g., in logs/<project_name>_<mode>_<timestamp>.log), and outputs the finalized configuration block to standard output.

docs.title: Phase 5: Flow Execution and Lifecycle Teardown
docs.text:
Compiles the PocketFlow execution graph, executes all nodes sequentially or concurrently, runs post-execution cleanups, and guarantees resource finalization in a finally block.

    # Create and run the flow
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
    try:
        tutorial_flow.run(shared)

        # Cleanup after run if requested
        if args.cleanup:
            _run_cleanup()
    finally:
        from utils.output import shutdown

        # Report spend even when the run fails — failed runs are often the expensive ones.
        try:
            _emit_usage_summary()
        except Exception as e:
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")
        shutdown()

The execution phase instantiates the workflow via create_tutorial_flow() from flow.py and executes it synchronously against shared. If --cleanup was specified alongside generation flags, _run_cleanup() purges intermediate caches upon completion. Crucially, the enclosing finally block ensures that even if an unhandled exception or SIGINT aborts pipeline processing, _emit_usage_summary() tabulates and logs cumulative token costs, and shutdown() flushes and closes active logging file handles.

docs.title: _thinking_level_arg()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Signature: def _thinking_level_arg(value: str) -> str | None:

Description: Type validation and normalization callable passed to argparse for the --thinking-level CLI parameter. It trims whitespace, lowercases input strings, maps empty inputs or the literal "default" to None (representing the LLM's native default behavior), and verifies that explicit levels belong to THINKING_LEVELS from utils/thinking.py.

Parameters: * value (str): The raw string value passed via command-line arguments.

Returns: * str | None: A normalized reasoning tier string ('minimal', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max'), or None.

Raises: * argparse.ArgumentTypeError: Raised if the string does not match allowed choices.

Example: 

def _thinking_level_arg(value):
    """argparse type for --thinking-level: a level from THINKING_LEVELS; '' or 'default' → None (model default)."""
    level = value.strip().lower()
    if level in ("", "default"):
        return None
    if level not in THINKING_LEVELS:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"invalid choice: {value!r} (choose from {', '.join(THINKING_LEVELS)}, default)")
    return level

This helper guarantees that invalid thinking tiers are intercepted during argument parsing before any subsystem initialization occurs. By transforming empty strings and "default" into None, it allows upstream callers to distinguish between explicit user overrides and fallback model defaults.

docs.title: _check_quoting_errors()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Signature: def _check_quoting_errors(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser, args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

Description: Detects shell argument quoting mistakes where missing closing quotes in --exclude or --include arrays accidentally swallow subsequent command-line flags. Because shells treat unbalanced strings as continuous literal arguments, subsequent CLI flags (e.g., --language) are frequently merged into pattern lists, causing them to be silently ignored. This defensive validator inspects all extracted pattern strings against registered parser flags and terminates execution if an embedded flag is detected.

Parameters: * parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The active CLI argument parser used to extract registered options dynamically. * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed argument namespace containing evaluated exclude and include lists.

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Invokes sys.exit(1) upon identifying an embedded flag in any glob pattern.

Example: 

def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):
    """Detect shell quoting errors where --exclude/--include values accidentally swallowed other CLI flags."""
    # Extract all registered flags (both --long and -short) from the parser
    known_flags = set()
    for action in parser._actions:
        for opt in action.option_strings:
            known_flags.add(opt)

    for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
        if not pattern_list:
            continue
        for pattern in pattern_list:
            for known_flag in known_flags:
                if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                    emit(
                        "ERROR_QUOTING",
                        flag=flag_name,
                        pattern=pattern[:120],
                        embedded=known_flag,
                    )
                    sys.exit(1)

The function queries parser._actions to extract all valid option strings (-n, --repo, --mode, etc.). It iterates over each pattern provided to --exclude and --include, checking whether an option string appears with leading whitespace (f" {known_flag} " or trailing f" {known_flag}"). If found, it emits a localized ERROR_QUOTING diagnostic and immediately halts execution, preventing confusing downstream crawl errors.

docs.title: _validate_thinking_args()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Signature: def _validate_thinking_args(args: argparse.Namespace, invalid_overrides: list[str]) -> None:

Description: Audits the validity of cognitive effort configurations. It raises fatal errors for malformed override syntax, warns when users configure overrides for nodes not executed in the active --mode, and warns when a global --thinking-level overrides a specified --thinking-profile.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line argument namespace. * invalid_overrides (list[str]): List of malformed NODE=LEVEL override strings returned by resolve_thinking_plan().

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Invokes sys.exit(1) if invalid_overrides contains any malformed strings.

Example: 

def _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides):
    """Report malformed --thinking-override values (fatal), overrides for nodes the mode never runs,
    and --thinking-level/--thinking-profile conflicts."""
    if invalid_overrides:
        emit("ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE", value=", ".join(invalid_overrides), nodes=", ".join(NODE_KEYS), levels=", ".join(THINKING_LEVELS))
        sys.exit(1)
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, _ = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    unused = [node for node in overrides if node not in MODE_NODES[mode]]
    if unused:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED", nodes=", ".join(unused), mode=mode, active=", ".join(MODE_NODES[mode]))
    if args.thinking_level and args.thinking_profile != "auto":
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE", level=args.thinking_level, profile=args.thinking_profile)

The validator first halts execution via sys.exit(1) if any override fails parsing. It then compares specified override nodes against MODE_NODES[mode] from utils/thinking.py; if an override is provided for a stage not present in the active mode's DAG, it alerts the operator via WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED. Finally, it warns if both a global effort level and a non-default profile are specified concurrently.

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Signature: def _run_cleanup() -> None:

Description: Purges disk-based cache artifacts and execution log directories. It unlinks persistent JSON response caches (llm_cache_v2.json, llm_cache_v2.json.tmp, llm_cache.json) and removes the active logging directory (resolved from LOG_DIR or defaulting to "logs").

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None. Internal file operations trap and log exceptions via CLEANUP_FAILED without aborting cleanup passes.

Example: 

def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in ["llm_cache_v2.json", "llm_cache_v2.json.tmp", "llm_cache.json"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)

The cleanup helper is designed for defensive execution. It checks for file and directory existence before unlinking assets. Individual deletion failures (e.g., due to file system locks or permission restrictions) are trapped and reported through CLEANUP_FAILED, allowing the remaining files to be processed.

docs.title: _emit_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Signature: def _emit_usage_summary() -> None:

Description: Queries the cumulative session usage ledger from utils/llm_common.py and displays a formatted summary across all active providers. For each vendor, it reports unique model identifiers, total network requests, input tokens, output tokens, internal thinking tokens, prompt cache metrics, total estimated financial cost, and recorded operational events (refusals, fallbacks, truncations).

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None. Exceptions occurring inside this helper during final teardown are trapped by the caller.

Example: 

def _emit_usage_summary():
    """Emit accumulated token usage and estimated cost for every provider used this run."""
    from utils.llm_common import get_usage_summary

    for name, usage in get_usage_summary().items():
        emit(
            "LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY",
            provider=name,
            models=", ".join(usage["models"]) or "-",
            calls=f"{usage['calls']:,}",
            input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
            output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
            thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
            cache_read=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
            cache_write=f"{usage['cache_write']:,}",
            cost=f"${usage['cost']:.2f}" if usage["cost_known"] else get("CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN"),
            refusals=usage["refusals"],
            fallbacks=usage["fallbacks"],
            truncations=usage["truncations"],
        )

The function consumes data from get_usage_summary(). It iterates through each provider ledger, formatting token counts with comma separators and currency values to two decimal places. If any model in the ledger lacked authoritative pricing metadata, it sets the cost string to the localized CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN fallback to prevent misleading accounting figures.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
main.py enforces a defensive, fail-fast strategy across early validation phases, paired with a reliable teardown pattern in the workflow execution phase:

  • Quoting Error Interception (_check_quoting_errors): Catches shell quoting mistakes (e.g., passing unescaped globs that merge subsequent flags like --language into --exclude) by inspecting argument patterns against registered CLI flags. It displays ERROR_QUOTING and exits via sys.exit(1).
  • Argument Conflict and Override Validation (_validate_thinking_args): Detects malformed thinking overrides and terminates execution immediately (sys.exit(1)). It also emits non-fatal warnings if a global --thinking-level overrides a designated --thinking-profile, or if an override targets a node not used by the active --mode.
  • Credential Verification Preflight (check_llm_auth): Verifies provider credentials and required SDK installations before executing repository crawls or remote API calls. If authentication fails, the process exits with status code 1.
  • Incremental Mode Constraints: Ensures incremental caching is only used where supported. It disables incremental mode with a warning if used outside --mode api-reference, and rejects --force-rebuild when --incremental is absent.
  • Teardown and Exception Handling: Encloses the primary pipeline call tutorial_flow.run(shared) in a try...finally block. If node processing raises an unhandled exception or terminates early, the finally block traps internal errors, reports token usage via _emit_usage_summary(), and invokes shutdown() to flush logging buffers cleanly.

docs.title: nodes.py
docs.text:
Source: nodes.py

Following the orchestration flow constructed in flow.py and initialized at application startup by main.py, nodes.py implements the concrete execution stages of the documentation pipeline. Each class in this module inherits from PocketFlow.Node or PocketFlow.BatchNode, encapsulating a lifecycle divided into preparation (prep), execution (exec), and state publishing (post).

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
nodes.py serves as the operational engine for repository ingestion, abstraction extraction, topological relationship modeling, pedagogical sequencing, chapter synthesis, and documentation serialization. The module interacts with the central runtime blackboard dictionary (shared) to pass state between decoupled execution nodes. Depending on the volume of source code, repository structure, and user configuration, nodes dynamically adapt their behavior—switching between direct in-context analysis, batch chunking, and 1:1 deterministic file mapping.

The architectural lifecycle consists of four functional phases: 1. Ingestion & Context Evaluation: FetchRepo retrieves source code trees from remote GitHub repositories or local directories via crawl_github_files.py or crawl_local_files.py. ContextRouter evaluates the token size of the source files against the model's effective context ceiling, subtracting prompt template overhead and reserved completion headroom. It then routes execution through a single direct prompt (direct), directory-bounded chunks (batch), or an isolated 1:1 module breakdown (deterministic). 2. Abstraction Extraction: Depending on the selected route, IdentifyAbstractions extracts core concepts from full codebase listings in a single inference pass; MapAbstractions processes directory-bound file batches in parallel, followed by ReduceAbstractions to consolidate partial abstractions into a unified architecture; or DeterministicFileMapper strips non-code files via LLM classification and maps remaining files directly to individual documentation chapters sorted by directory depth. 3. Relational Analysis & Sequencing: AnalyzeRelationships distributes prompt token budgets across abstractions to provide code context, prompts the model to infer architectural dependencies, and builds an indexed relationship graph. OrderChapters analyzes this dependency graph to establish a pedagogical reading order from foundational utility layers to high-level orchestration controllers. 4. Drafting & Final Emission: WriteChapters processes ordered abstractions sequentially, maintaining an in-memory sliding window of preceding chapter summaries to provide context while avoiding quadratic context token growth ($O(n^2)$). It also incorporates MD5-based incremental disk caching to bypass previously synthesized chapters. Finally, CombineTutorial synthesizes static HTML websites via MkDocs Material or emits standalone Markdown packages using mkdocs.py.
