docs.title: uses_adaptive_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def uses_adaptive_thinking(model: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a specified Claude model supports Anthropic's adaptive thinking protocol. Under the hood, it performs prefix matching against _ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES (sourced from ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES in llm_config.py), which designates models like Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable that dynamically modulate internal reasoning depth.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier string to evaluate.

Returns: * bool: True if the model utilizes adaptive thinking; False if it relies on static budget_tokens or does not support reasoning blocks.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def uses_adaptive_thinking(model: str) -> bool:
    return _matches(model, _ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES)
This function serves as a feature switch during request compilation. When this returns True, parameter assembly logic attaches {"type": "adaptive"} along with output_config.effort mappings. Conversely, when it returns False, older models such as Haiku 4.5 fall back to explicit token-budget structures (budget_tokens).

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Determines the maximum input context window and maximum allowable output tokens for a given model. It queries an in-memory memoization cache _model_limits_cache to avoid repeated remote network roundtrips. On a cache miss, it contacts the Anthropic Models API via _get_client().models.retrieve(model) to read remote limits. If the API lookup encounters an anthropic.APIError (e.g., during offline operation or permission limitations), it logs a warning and falls back to pre-configured bounds from _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier string whose limits are requested.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A two-element tuple consisting of (context_window, max_output_tokens).

Raises: * None (API errors are trapped internally and resolved using offline fallbacks).

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (context_window, max_output_tokens) from the Models API, with offline fallback."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    fallback = next((v for k, v in _MODEL_LIMITS.items() if model.startswith(k)), _DEFAULT_LIMITS)
    try:
        info = _get_client().models.retrieve(model)
        limits = (getattr(info, "max_input_tokens", None) or fallback[0], getattr(info, "max_tokens", None) or fallback[1])
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Anthropic Models API | model={model} | context={limits[0]:,} | max_output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
    except anthropic.APIError as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e))
        limits = fallback
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits
The function combines API-driven limit discovery with defensive offline resilience. By caching limits in the module-level dictionary _model_limits_cache, it ensures that the overhead of querying the Anthropic Models API occurs at most once per model ID per process execution. When the network is unavailable or the credentials lack permission to call the Models endpoint, the system seamlessly applies predefined defaults (such as 200,000 / 64,000 tokens for Haiku 4.5 or 1,000,000 / 128,000 tokens as the global default).

docs.title: normalize_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Normalizes an abstract or user-specified thinking effort level to an effort value supported by the specified Anthropic model. It invokes anthropic_effort() from llm_config.py to map values (such as translating "minimal" to "low", or downscaling "xhigh" to "high" on 4.6 family models). If an invalid or unsupported effort string is provided, it logs a warning via emit() and returns None.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier string. * level (str | None): The requested effort level string or None.

Returns: * str | None: The validated effort string ("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", or "max"), or None if unconfigured or unsupported.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Map a thinking level to an effort value the model accepts (None = model default)."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, level)  # minimal → low; xhigh → high on the 4.6 family
    if level and effort is None:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_INVALID", level=level.lower(), model=model, supported=str(list(EFFORT_LEVELS)))
    return effort
This function serves as an input validation and sanitization bridge between abstract thinking configurations and concrete API parameters. Because different Claude releases accept different subsets of reasoning effort values, the normalization logic guarantees that invalid payload configurations are caught early before network dispatch, avoiding API validation rejections.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public (Re-exported) Signature: class LLMRefusalError(Exception):

Description: Domain exception re-exported from llm_common.py. Raised when the model's safety classifiers reject generation (stop_reason == "refusal"). It contains the model identifier, provider name, and refusal category.

Example: 

# Usage inside call_anthropic:
if message.stop_reason == "refusal":
    count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals")
    details = getattr(message, "stop_details", None)
    category = getattr(details, "category", None) if details else None
    emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL", model=model, category=category or "unknown")
    raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public (Re-exported) Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: Domain string wrapper re-exported from llm_common.py. Represents a model output that terminated due to token length exhaustion (stop_reason == "max_tokens" or "model_context_window_exceeded"). Downstream caching modules detect this type and intentionally bypass response caching.

Example: 

# Usage inside call_anthropic:
text = _extract_text(message)
if message.stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS:
    count_event("ANTHROPIC", "truncations")
    emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED", max_tokens=f"{params['max_tokens']:,}")
    return TruncatedResponse(text)

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_client() -> anthropic.Anthropic:

Description: Lazily initializes and returns the shared singleton instance of anthropic.Anthropic. The client is configured with max_retries=3 to handle transient network issues (HTTP 408, 409, 429, and 5xx) with exponential backoff beneath the orchestration layer.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * anthropic.Anthropic: The initialized Anthropic client singleton.

Raises: * anthropic.AnthropicError: If client instantiation fails due to missing or invalid credentials.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        # SDK resolves credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / AUTH_TOKEN / ant profile) and
        # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL itself. SDK retries 408/409/429/5xx with backoff;
        # PocketFlow node retries sit on top of this.
        _client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=3)
    return _client
By deferring client instantiation until the first API request is dispatched, the module prevents import-time failures in environments where Anthropic credentials are absent. The underlying SDK manages authentication token discovery across environment variables and profile stores, while the retry policy guarantees localized resilience against transient provider throttling.

docs.title: _matches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _matches(model: str, prefixes: tuple[str, ...] | list[str]) -> bool:

Description: Helper predicate that checks whether a model identifier string begins with any prefix in the provided collection.

Parameters: * model (str): The target model string. * prefixes (tuple[str, ...] | list[str]): A sequence of string prefixes to match against.

Returns: * bool: True if model.startswith(p) is true for any prefix p; otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:
    return any(model.startswith(p) for p in prefixes)
This utility centralizes prefix-based matching throughout the module. It evaluates whether a model belongs to specific capability categories, such as adaptive thinking, default reasoning, or safety fallback eligibility.

docs.title: _fallback_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:

Description: Evaluates the ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS environment variable and returns the appropriate beta header list and extra_body payload dictionary for server-side refusal fallbacks. If fallbacks have been globally disabled for the run (due to prior 400 Bad Request rejections) or explicitly set to "off", it returns empty structures.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier string.

Returns: * tuple[list[str], dict]: A tuple of (betas, extra_body). For default fallbacks, returns ([_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}). For custom model lists, returns ([_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m}, ...]}).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (betas, extra_body) for server-side refusal fallbacks, or empty when disabled."""
    setting = (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS") or "default").strip()
    if _fallbacks_disabled or setting.lower() == "off":
        return [], {}
    if setting.lower() == "default":
        if not _matches(model, _FALLBACK_PREFIXES):
            return [], {}
        return [_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}
    targets = [m.strip() for m in setting.split(",") if m.strip()]
    return [_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m} for m in targets]}
This helper structures server-side safety fallback configurations. When models encounter policy classifiers (such as Claude Opus 5.x and Fable 5.x), enabling Anthropic's fallback beta directs the Anthropic edge proxy to automatically redirect queries to secondary models rather than returning terminal refusal errors.

docs.title: _build_request()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:

Description: Constructs the parameters dictionary and beta header list required for the Anthropic Messages API. It configures the user prompt message, assigns max_tokens, attaches adaptive thinking parameters (or budget tokens for non-adaptive architectures), injects ephemeral prompt cache controls when enabled, and includes fallback headers.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The input user prompt text. * model (str): The target model ID. * effort (str | None): The normalized thinking effort level. * max_tokens (int): Maximum allowed output tokens.

Returns: * tuple[dict, list[str]]: A tuple containing (params, betas) where params is the request keyword arguments dictionary and betas is a list of active Anthropic beta feature strings.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    params = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    }
    if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
        if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
            thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
            if is_debug():
                # Readable reasoning summaries go to the log file (never to stdout).
                thinking["display"] = "summarized"
            params["thinking"] = thinking
        if effort:
            params["output_config"] = {"effort": effort}
    elif effort:
        budget = min(_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL[effort], max_tokens - 1_024)
        if budget >= 1_024:
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget}

    if (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE") or "off").strip().lower() == "on":
        params["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}

    betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
    if extra_body:
        params["extra_body"] = extra_body
    return params, betas
This function isolates API parameter assembly across diverse Claude generations. For adaptive models, it configures thinking: {"type": "adaptive"} along with output_config: {"effort": effort}, enabling debug summaries if debug logging is enabled. For pre-adaptive models, it translates effort levels to explicit budget_tokens, ensuring token margins remain valid (budget >= 1024).

docs.title: _resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Computes the optimal planned max_tokens budget and the absolute ceiling allowed by context limits and configuration overrides. It retrieves model limits via get_model_limits(), calculates available context room after subtracting prompt tokens and safety margins (ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN), and clamps output budgets to prevent context window overflow.

Parameters: * prompt_tokens (int): Estimated prompt token count (scaled by token multiplier). * model (str): Target model identifier string. * effort (str | None): Normalized thinking effort level.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A tuple of (wanted, ceiling) representing the allocated budget and the maximum context ceiling.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)  # same value input_token_budget reserved

    room = max(context_window - prompt_tokens - ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096)
    ceiling = min(output_cap, room, cap) if cap else min(output_cap, room)
    if ceiling < wanted:
        # Small shortfalls (template overhead on a budget-packed prompt) are expected; only report real cuts.
        if ceiling < wanted * 0.9:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED", wanted=f"{wanted:,}", available=f"{ceiling:,}")
        wanted = ceiling
    return wanted, ceiling
The allocation algorithm balances token capacity across generation requirements. It reserves headroom defined by ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN to ensure prompt expansion or internal reasoning tokens do not trigger API context window errors. If the available room falls significantly short of the requested budget (ceiling < wanted * 0.9), it issues a warning before clamping the allocation.

docs.title: _stream_message()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Invokes either client.beta.messages.stream() (if beta headers are provided) or standard client.messages.stream() using context managers, returning the final accumulated message object upon stream completion.

Parameters: * params (dict): Keyword arguments passed directly to the Anthropic Messages streaming endpoint. * betas (list[str]): List of Anthropic beta feature strings.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The fully accumulated message object returned by stream.get_final_message().

Raises: * anthropic.APIError: If network failure or API validation errors occur during streaming.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    client = _get_client()
    if betas:
        with client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params) as stream:
            return stream.get_final_message()
    with client.messages.stream(**params) as stream:
        return stream.get_final_message()
By encapsulating streaming transport within context managers, this helper ensures that HTTP stream connections are cleanly consumed and terminated without socket leaks. Streaming prevents standard HTTP connection timeouts on generations that produce tens of thousands of reasoning and content tokens.

docs.title: _fallback_rejected()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether an HTTP 400 Bad Request error from Anthropic was specifically caused by the refusal fallback feature itself (e.g., unsupported beta header, or accounts where default fallbacks are unavailable), rather than an invalid prompt or schema error.

Parameters: * error_text (str): The error message text from the caught BadRequestError. * params (dict): The parameter dictionary used in the rejected request.

Returns: * bool: True if the error indicates that server-side fallback headers caused the rejection; otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:
    """True when a 400 rejects the fallback feature itself (beta header not enabled, or
    `fallbacks: "default"` unsupported for this model/account) — not a user config error."""
    text = error_text.lower()
    if "anthropic-beta" in text and "server-side-fallback" in text:
        return True
    return params.get("extra_body", {}).get("fallbacks") == "default" and "fallbacks" in text
This heuristic inspects error payloads to distinguish between genuine user configuration issues and server-side beta compatibility limitations. It searches for specific signatures indicating that beta fallback routing is not provisioned for the current API tier or model.

docs.title: _send()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Executes a streamed request via _stream_message(). If a BadRequestError occurs and _fallback_rejected() confirms that server-side fallbacks caused the failure, it permanently sets _fallbacks_disabled = True, logs a warning, removes fallback configurations from the payload, and retries the request without fallback headers.

Parameters: * params (dict): Request parameter dictionary. * betas (list[str]): Active beta header list.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The completed response message.

Raises: * anthropic.BadRequestError: If the 400 error is unrelated to fallback feature rejection. * anthropic.APIError: For other unrecoverable API errors.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    """Send one streamed request; disable fallbacks for the run if the feature is unavailable."""
    global _fallbacks_disabled
    try:
        return _stream_message(params, betas)
    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise
This function implements an automated recovery loop. When an account or model rejects fallback headers, modifying the module global _fallbacks_disabled ensures that subsequent requests throughout the process skip fallback negotiation entirely, preventing repetitive failed calls.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated USD cost of an API call based on token consumption metrics and prefix-matched pricing rates from _PRICING. Cache write operations are billed at 1.25× the base input token price.

Parameters: * model (str): Model identifier used to match pricing tiers. * tokens_in (int): Count of non-cached input tokens. * tokens_out (int): Count of generated output tokens. * cache_read (int): Count of input tokens read from prompt cache. * cache_write (int): Count of input tokens written to prompt cache.

Returns: * float | None: Total estimated cost in USD, or None if the model does not match any prefix in _PRICING.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:
    price = next((_PRICING[k] for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if (model or "").startswith(k)), None)
    if price is None:
        return None
    p_in, p_out, p_read = price
    return (tokens_in * p_in + tokens_out * p_out + cache_read * p_read + cache_write * p_in * 1.25) / 1_000_000
Pricing calculations sort model prefixes by descending string length to ensure specific versions (such as claude-fable-5-1) match before broader family prefixes (claude-fable-5). Costs are calculated on a per-million token basis, incorporating cached read discounts and write surcharges.

docs.title: _tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:

Description: Extracts input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation token counts from an Anthropic message usage container, defaulting missing fields to 0.

Parameters: * usage (Any): SDK usage object containing token metric attributes.

Returns: * tuple[int, int, int, int]: A tuple of (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    return (
        getattr(usage, "input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
    )
This defensive helper extracts token counts across varying response payloads. Using getattr() with fallback zeros protects against schema differences across SDK minor versions or beta response formats.

docs.title: _message_cost()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated USD cost of an entire message response. When server-side fallbacks occur, it processes per-attempt usage records stored in usage.iterations, billing each attempt at its corresponding model's rate while skipping attempts declined before output generation. For un-iterated responses, it bills according to the served model's rates.

Parameters: * message (Any): The Anthropic message object. * served_model (str): The model ID that served the final response.

Returns: * float | None: Aggregated USD cost, or None if any consumed model's pricing rates are unrecognized.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        total, known = 0.0, True
        for entry in iterations:
            tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(entry)
            if tokens_out == 0:
                continue  # declined before any output (primary or fallback attempt): not billed
            cost = _price(getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write)
            known = known and cost is not None
            total += cost or 0.0
        return total if known else None
    if message.stop_reason == "refusal" and not _extract_text(message):
        return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
    return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))
This calculation accurately accounts for costs in multi-model fallback sequences. When Anthropic routes a request through multiple candidate models before completing, top-level usage covers only the final attempt, while usage.iterations tracks all intermediate executions. Declined requests that yielded zero output tokens are excluded from billing calculations.

docs.title: _record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float) -> None:

Description: Extracts usage metrics from a message, calculates costs, updates global session ledgers via record_usage(), and logs granular debugging telemetry (including elapsed time and observed token ratios).

Parameters: * message (Any): The completed Anthropic message object. * raw_prompt_tokens (int): Unscaled prompt token count measured by count_tokens_raw(). * effort (str | None): Normalized effort level string. * elapsed (float): Request duration in seconds.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float) -> None:
    served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
    tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(message.usage)
    cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)
    record_usage(
        "ANTHROPIC", served_model, input_tokens=tokens_in, output_tokens=tokens_out, cache_read=cache_read, cache_write=cache_write, cost=cost
    )

    # Observed Claude/tiktoken ratio helps tune ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO for this codebase.
    ratio = (tokens_in + cache_read + cache_write) / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"ANTHROPIC USAGE | model={served_model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | stop={message.stop_reason} | "
        f"in={tokens_in:,} | out={tokens_out:,} | cache_read={cache_read:,} | cache_write={cache_write:,} | "
        f"est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
This function logs operational telemetry for cost tracking and tokenizer calibration. Comparing actual Anthropic input tokens against raw tiktoken counts computes the observed_token_ratio, providing visibility into token expansion for the repository's source code mix.

docs.title: _log_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _log_thinking(message) -> None:

Description: Iterates through message content blocks, detects blocks with type == "thinking", and outputs reasoning summaries to the debug log stream.

Parameters: * message (Any): The message object containing parsed content blocks.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _log_thinking(message) -> None:
    for block in message.content:
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "thinking" and getattr(block, "thinking", ""):
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{block.thinking}", dest="LOG")
Anthropic models utilizing adaptive thinking return their chain-of-thought blocks separately from final answer text. This function routes those reasoning traces to the debug log file (dest="LOG") without polluting standard terminal outputs.

docs.title: _served_by_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:

Description: Inspects content blocks and usage iterations to determine whether the request was fulfilled by a fallback model rather than the primary target.

Parameters: * message (Any): The message object to inspect.

Returns: * bool: True if fallback indicators are detected in content blocks or iteration metadata; otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:
    if any(getattr(block, "type", None) == "fallback" for block in message.content):
        return True
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    return any(getattr(entry, "type", None) == "fallback_message" for entry in iterations)
This predicate detects whether server-side fallback handling was activated during execution. It inspects both content block structures and iteration event types to surface automated reroutes.

docs.title: _extract_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _extract_text(message) -> str:

Description: Extracts and concatenates text from all message content blocks that have type == "text".

Parameters: * message (Any): The message object returned by the Anthropic SDK.

Returns: * str: The concatenated text string.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sourced directly from utils/llm_anthropic.py
def _extract_text(message) -> str:
    return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text")
Because the Anthropic Messages API returns structured content blocks (interleaving text, reasoning, tool use, and fallback metadata), this helper strips non-text blocks and extracts the synthesized textual content.

docs.title: Pricing Directory Schema (_PRICING)
docs.text:
The _PRICING dictionary maps model prefix substrings to pricing tuples. Rates are defined in USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Prompt cache writes are billed dynamically at 1.25× the base input token price.

docs.text:
Defines offline token limit fallback configurations when the Models API cannot be reached. Represented as a tuple[int, int] corresponding to (context_window, max_output_tokens).

docs.text:
The internal payload tuple returned by _build_request() and consumed by _send().

Parameter Field Type Description model str Model identifier string. max_tokens int Clamped maximum generation output budget. messages list[dict[str, str]] Single-turn message list: [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. thinking dict[str, Any] (optional) Reasoning configuration: {"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"} or {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": int}. output_config dict[str, str] (optional) Effort configuration for adaptive models: {"effort": effort}. cache_control dict[str, str] (optional) Set to {"type": "ephemeral"} when prompt caching is enabled. extra_body dict[str, Any] (optional) Contains fallback configurations (e.g., {"fallbacks": "default"}). betas list[str] Active Anthropic beta headers (e.g., ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]).

docs.text:
The standard 4-integer tuple returned by the _tokens() helper.

Index Name Type Description 0 tokens_in int Count of un-cached input tokens processed by the API. 1 tokens_out int Count of generated output and thinking tokens. 2 cache_read int Count of prompt tokens matched and read from Anthropic prompt cache. 3 cache_write int Count of prompt tokens written to Anthropic prompt cache.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module provides defensive exception handling and recovery workflows across API interactions:

  • Remote Models API Failures (anthropic.APIError): When checking model context limits in get_model_limits(), network or authentication errors are caught. The driver logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP and falls back to offline boundaries from _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS without crashing.
  • Server-Side Fallback Feature Rejection (anthropic.BadRequestError): When Anthropic's API returns an HTTP 400 rejecting fallback beta headers (detected via _fallback_rejected()), the module isolates the failure. It sets _fallbacks_disabled = True, logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED, strips extra_body and beta headers from the parameters, and immediately retries the request natively.
  • Context Budget Shortfalls & Output Clamping: In _resolve_max_tokens(), if available context room is below 90% of the planned output allocation (ceiling < wanted * 0.9), the module issues WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED and clamps output tokens to the context boundary.
  • Premature Token Truncation Retry Escalation: In call_anthropic(), when a response ends with stop_reason == "max_tokens" and max_tokens < ceiling, the driver issues WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY, records the intermediate attempt's metrics, recalculates parameters using the context ceiling, and executes a one-time retry.
  • Terminal Truncation Handling (_TRUNCATION_STOPS): If a response terminates due to "max_tokens" or "model_context_window_exceeded" after retry escalation, the driver logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED and returns the generated text wrapped in a TruncatedResponse instance. This prevents upstream caching layers in call_llm.py from storing incomplete output.
  • Safety Classifications and Refusals (stop_reason == "refusal"): When Claude refuses a prompt, the driver extracts classification categories from message.stop_details, increments failure counters via count_event(), issues WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL, and raises LLMRefusalError. This signals to call_llm.py and upstream workflow nodes that the request failed due to content boundaries and should not be retried.

docs.title: llm_common.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_common.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the vendor-specific transport and parsing mechanics established in llm_anthropic.py, the llm_common.py module defines the shared, provider-agnostic domain layer for the entire inference pipeline. It operates as a zero-dependency foundational component that explicitly avoids importing third-party provider SDKs (anthropic, google-genai, openai). By establishing uniform domain representations for incomplete generations, provider rejections, runtime deduplication, and financial telemetry, it isolates the high-level orchestration workflows in call_llm.py from the underlying provider implementations.

The primary architectural role of llm_common.py is to manage stateful inference invariants across multi-step execution graphs. It provides a circuit-breaking refusal memoization mechanism (_refused) that prevents wasteful network retries against models that deterministically decline prompts due to safety, moderation, or policy violations. Furthermore, it defines custom string subtype semantics (TruncatedResponse) to intercept length-truncated completions before they can contaminate the disk-backed cache in call_llm.py, while simultaneously offering a centralized session ledger (_usage) to record token volumes, thinking token allocations, prompt cache interactions, and accumulated operational costs.

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: A specialized string subclass that tags model responses truncated by output token limits or context window boundaries. It preserves standard string behavior across serialization and downstream logging operations while exposing a sentinel truncated = True attribute. Higher-level orchestration layers, specifically call_llm and parse_yaml_response, inspect this boolean attribute to bypass persistent disk caching and signal upstream node retries.

Attributes: * truncated (bool): Sentinel flag, always set to True, identifying the output buffer as incomplete.

Example: 

class TruncatedResponse(str):
    """Response text from a reply that was cut off; call_llm returns it but never caches it."""

    truncated = True
The implementation derives directly from native str without mutating base string memory layouts. Because instances pass standard string type checks throughout the Python runtime, intermediate formatters can safely inspect, print, or measure the truncated payload without raising type errors. Upstream orchestrators use getattr(response, "truncated", False) to selectively invalidate the run from the persistence cache, ensuring that defective, half-formed YAML blocks or code generations are forced through subsequent re-sampling passes.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError): def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):

Description: Domain exception raised when an LLM provider declines to generate a completion due to content moderation filters, safety guardrails, or recitation protections. It encapsulates the originating provider, model identifier, refusal classification category, and a criticality flag (retryable). This flag differentiates between deterministic prompt declines (such as system-level policy blocks that must never be re-sent) and stochastic candidate blocks (such as mid-generation recitation triggers that may succeed upon re-sampling).

Parameters: * model (str): The specific model identifier that issued the refusal (e.g., "claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219"). * category (str | None): The provider's safety category code or rejection reason (e.g., "safety", "recitation", "content_filter"). * provider (str): The identifier of the rejecting vendor platform. Defaults to "ANTHROPIC". * retryable (bool): Indicates whether repeating the inference request with alternative sampling parameters could succeed. Defaults to False.

Returns: * LLMRefusalError: Instantiated exception object with formatted diagnostic details.

Raises: * N/A: Instantiation does not raise errors.

Example: 

class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the provider (and any configured fallback) declines a request.

    retryable=False: the same request is declined again (Claude refusal, blocked prompt,
    prohibited content) — call_llm remembers it and does not re-send it on node retries.
    retryable=True: an output-side block that a new sample can pass (Gemini RECITATION / OTHER /
    SAFETY on the candidate, OpenRouter content_filter) — node retries re-sample normally.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
        self.model = model
        self.category = category
        self.provider = provider
        self.retryable = retryable
        super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")
The constructor structures diagnostic messages uniformly across diverse provider payloads, converting ambiguous vendor error codes into a standardized runtime exception. Downstream dispatchers evaluate the instance's retryable property to modulate retry loops. If retryable evaluates to False, the refusal is committed to the module's internal lookup table, short-circuiting identical subsequent requests before invoking network sockets.

docs.title: request_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:

Description: Generates a deterministic SHA-256 hexadecimal hash identifying an inference request. The key is composed of a scoped header containing the provider name, the model string, and the normalized reasoning effort level, followed by the exact prompt payload. This hash serves as the primary indexing key for refusal tracking and cache deduplication.

Parameters: * provider (str): The upstream inference provider (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER"). * model (str): The target model name string. * thinking_level (str | None): The configured reasoning intensity (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"), or None if operating without reasoning tokens. * prompt (str): The complete serialized prompt string passed to the driver.

Returns: * str: A 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal digest representing the request signature.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
The implementation uses a delimiter-separated scope prefix (provider|model|thinking_level\n) to ensure that identical prompt strings routed to different models or distinct reasoning budgets yield collision-free digests. The resulting string is encoded into UTF-8 before being passed to hashlib.sha256. This mechanism provides an identical hash output across diverse operating systems and process lifecycles.

docs.title: remember_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:

Description: Registers an encountered non-retryable LLMRefusalError into the module-level refusal registry (_refused), binding the error object to the request's deterministic SHA-256 hash.

Parameters: * key (str): The hexadecimal request digest computed via request_key(). * error (LLMRefusalError): The refusal error instance capturing the failure context.

Returns: * None

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:
    _refused[key] = error
This function populates the private global dictionary _refused to provide process-level memorization of declined inference attempts. When synthesis nodes attempt retries following a fatal safety refusal, registering the error through this function allows the caller to break out of cascading execution cycles immediately. The stored error retains its original stack context, failure model, and safety categories for subsequent inspection.

docs.title: previous_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:

Description: Queries the module-level refusal registry for a previously recorded LLMRefusalError matching the provided request hash.

Parameters: * key (str): The hexadecimal request digest computed via request_key().

Returns: * LLMRefusalError | None: The cached refusal error if previously recorded; otherwise None.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:
    return _refused.get(key)
The retrieval helper executes an $O(1)$ dictionary lookup against the _refused table. Orchestrators in call_llm evaluate this lookup before calculating token bounds or initiating network requests. If an error is returned, the orchestrator immediately raises the memorized exception, preventing unnecessary network traffic, API quota consumption, and unneeded billing on inputs that will reliably trigger safety filters.

docs.title: record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def record_usage(provider: str, model: str, *, input_tokens: int = 0, output_tokens: int = 0, thinking_tokens: int = 0, cache_read: int = 0, cache_write: int = 0, cost: float | None = None) -> None:

Description: Records token volumes, prompt cache mechanics, and operational expenses for a completed inference call into the global usage ledger (_usage). It aggregates metrics per provider, tracks unique models utilized, and updates cost flags based on pricing availability.

Parameters: * provider (str): The provider identifier (e.g., "GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC"). * model (str): The specific model used for the completion. * input_tokens (int): Count of prompt/input tokens processed. Defaults to 0. * output_tokens (int): Count of total output tokens generated, including thinking tokens. Defaults to 0. * thinking_tokens (int): Subset of output tokens dedicated to internal model reasoning. Defaults to 0. * cache_read (int): Count of input tokens read from the provider's prompt cache. Defaults to 0. * cache_write (int): Count of input tokens written to create new prompt cache entries. Defaults to 0. * cost (float | None): Financial cost in USD for the transaction. If passed as None, marks the provider's overall cost as uncomputable. Defaults to None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Accumulate one call. `output_tokens` includes thinking; `thinking_tokens` is the reported subset.
    `cost` is USD; None means the price is unknown for this model (summary shows n/a)."""
    entry = _usage.setdefault(
        provider,
        {
            "models": set(),
            "calls": 0,
            "input": 0,
            "output": 0,
            "thinking": 0,
            "cache_read": 0,
            "cache_write": 0,
            "cost": 0.0,
            "cost_known": True,
            "refusals": 0,
            "fallbacks": 0,
            "truncations": 0,
        },
    )
    if model:
        entry["models"].add(model)
    entry["calls"] += 1
    entry["input"] += input_tokens or 0
    entry["output"] += output_tokens or 0
    entry["thinking"] += thinking_tokens or 0
    entry["cache_read"] += cache_read or 0
    entry["cache_write"] += cache_write or 0
    if cost is None:
        entry["cost_known"] = False
    else:
        entry["cost"] += cost
The implementation uses dict.setdefault to initialize zeroed usage buckets on the first call for a given provider. Integer token metrics defensively fall back to 0 if passed falsy or None values. When tracking costs, if any call for a model lacks price metadata (cost is None), the ledger sets cost_known to False, signaling downstream reporting routines in output.py to render costs as unknown (n/a) rather than misleadingly incomplete figures.

docs.title: count_event()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:

Description: Increments discrete operational anomaly counters ("refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations") for a specified provider entry within the global usage ledger.

Parameters: * provider (str): The target provider key in the usage ledger. * event (str): The metric counter to increment; expected to be one of "refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations".

Returns: * None

Raises: * KeyError: If event does not match an existing key in the ledger entry template.

Example: 

def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:
    """Increment 'refusals' | 'fallbacks' | 'truncations' for a provider."""
    entry = _usage.setdefault(
        provider,
        {
            "models": set(),
            "calls": 0,
            "input": 0,
            "output": 0,
            "thinking": 0,
            "cache_read": 0,
            "cache_write": 0,
            "cost": 0.0,
            "cost_known": True,
            "refusals": 0,
            "fallbacks": 0,
            "truncations": 0,
        },
    )
    entry[event] += 1
This function maintains parity between token volume reporting and pipeline operational health. By sharing the initialization structure with record_usage(), it allows events to be recorded before any tokens have been successfully generated—such as during immediate prompt rejections or connection fallback events. Upstream adapters call this helper whenever fallback headers are disabled, responses are truncated at context limits, or refusals are intercepted.

docs.title: get_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_usage_summary() -> dict:

Description: Generates a consolidated summary of token allocations, costs, and operational events for all providers that processed at least one call during the execution run. Transforms internal sets of model names into lexicographically sorted lists.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping provider names to shallow-copied usage records with sorted "models" lists, omitting inactive providers.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def get_usage_summary() -> dict:
    """{provider: totals} for every provider that made at least one call this run."""
    return {provider: dict(entry, models=sorted(entry["models"])) for provider, entry in _usage.items() if entry["calls"]}
The summary pipeline uses a dictionary comprehension that filters out uncalled providers (if entry["calls"]). It creates a decoupled copy of the internal accumulator using dict(entry, ...), explicitly converting the internal set of model names into a deterministically sorted list. This transformation guarantees stable rendering when generating tables or serialized CLI output summaries.

docs.title: reset_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def reset_usage() -> None:

Description: Resets all in-memory usage ledgers and refusal caches, returning the module to an uninitialized state. Primarily intended for automated test suites and isolated execution resets.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def reset_usage() -> None:
    _usage.clear()
    _refused.clear()
The helper invokes .clear() on both the _usage ledger and _refused map in-place. This guarantees that subsequent pipeline executions within the same Python process boundary do not retain dirty telemetry or memorized refusals from previous test runs.

docs.title: warn_once()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a warning signature has already been displayed during the active process run, tracking compound keys to prevent noisy CLI log duplication.

Parameters: * key (str): The primary category or message identifier. * *parts (Any): Optional additional hashable values (such as model names or HTTP status codes) forming a composite warning key.

Returns: * bool: True if this specific warning marker is encountered for the first time; False if it has already been registered.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:
    """True the first time a (key, parts) combination is seen this run."""
    marker = (key, *parts)
    if marker in _warned:
        return False
    _warned.add(marker)
    return True
The helper constructs a tuple (key, *parts) to serve as a composite hash in the private _warned set. If the marker is already present, the function returns False, allowing caller logging blocks to exit early. When a new marker is encountered, it is recorded in the set and returns True, ensuring that identical warnings (e.g., deprecated parameters, unsupported reasoning flags) are emitted only once per session.

docs.title: Internal Helpers
docs.text:
The utils/llm_common.py module maintains three internal, process-scoped data containers to track runtime state without exposing mutable data structures directly to external modules.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refused-request memo: a declined prompt is declined again, so PocketFlow retries
# must not re-send it (wasted rate limit, and billed partial output on mid-stream declines).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_refused = {}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Usage ledger (one per process; a run is sequential)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_usage = {}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# De-duplicated warnings
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_warned = set()

docs.title: _refused
docs.text: A process-level dictionary (dict[str, LLMRefusalError]) that maps SHA-256 request signatures generated by request_key() to their corresponding LLMRefusalError instances. It acts as an in-memory cache to prevent repetitive, non-retryable API calls. External modules access this dictionary exclusively through remember_refusal(), previous_refusal(), and reset_usage().

docs.title: _usage
docs.text: A process-level dictionary (dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) that aggregates operational statistics and token accounting across all active LLM providers. Each entry stores call counts, token usage, cost data, and error metrics. State modifications and reads are restricted to record_usage(), count_event(), get_usage_summary(), and reset_usage().

docs.title: _warned
docs.text: A process-level set (set[tuple[str, ...]]) containing composite warning markers. It records unique tuples passed to warn_once() to deduplicate warning messages in CLI logs throughout the life of the process.

docs.title: UsageRecord Schema
docs.text:
The internal dictionary structure maintained for each provider inside the _usage ledger, and exposed in shallow-copied form via get_usage_summary().

Field Type Description models set[str] (internal) / list[str] (summary) Unique model identifiers invoked for this provider during the run. calls int Total number of attempted inference calls dispatched. input int Total count of input/prompt tokens processed. output int Total count of output tokens generated (including thinking tokens). thinking int Subset of output tokens dedicated to model reasoning/thinking. cache_read int Prompt tokens retrieved directly from provider-side caches. cache_write int Prompt tokens written to create new provider-side cache entries. cost float Cumulative calculated cost in USD across all calls. cost_known bool Flag indicating whether all models used have known pricing metadata (False if any model cost was None). refusals int Count of declined requests encountered for this provider. fallbacks int Count of times the provider dropped down to secondary models or disabled fallback beta headers. truncations int Count of model completions cut off by context or token limits.

docs.title: RefusalMemo Schema
docs.text:
The schema mapping maintained by the _refused dictionary for recording declined requests.

Key Value Type Description SHA-256 digest string (64 characters) LLMRefusalError The captured refusal error instance, preserving model, category, provider, and retryability semantics.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module provides the foundation for error handling across the system's inference layers:

  • Refusal Classification: LLMRefusalError introduces a structured categorization for declined prompts. By dividing errors into retryable=False (fatal declines, policy triggers, deterministic refusals) and retryable=True (transient safety blocks, recitation checks on output candidates), it provides the decision logic necessary for upstream graph nodes to either resample or abandon execution paths.
  • Truncation Signatures: Rather than raising an unhandled exception upon encountering context window limits or maximum token exhaustion, the module provides TruncatedResponse. This string subtype allows pipelines to inspect partial completions, bypass the disk-based cache, and trigger controlled retries via higher-level handlers (such as YAML parsers).
  • Cost Incompleteness Guard: If an invoked model does not have pricing metrics available, record_usage() flags cost_known = False. This prevents the pipeline from displaying inaccurate or partially calculated cost summaries in terminal logs.

docs.text:

  • llm_anthropic.py — Anthropic integration driver that translates API response metrics into record_usage and handles LLMRefusalError and TruncatedResponse.
  • llm_gemini.py — Google Gemini adapter that reports token usage and converts candidate safety blocks into LLMRefusalError.
  • llm_openrouter.py — OpenRouter integration layer that reports multi-provider costs and usage to record_usage.
  • output.py — Telemetry and console formatting layer that processes get_usage_summary() to render final execution tables.

docs.title: llm_config.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/llm_config.py

Following the vendor-neutral state management and telemetry primitives established in llm_common.py, llm_config.py acts as the single source of truth for runtime provider resolution, model capability negotiation, token ratio calibration, output budgeting, and preflight authentication checks across the entire system. It was extracted directly from call_llm.py to break a circular import dependency between execution dispatching and prompt budgeting in token_utils.py. Both inference drivers and context-sizing utilities now import settings and token limits from this module without reciprocal couplings.

The module manages execution policies across three primary inference ecosystems: Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and OpenRouter. It resolves target provider environments, negotiates model-specific features—such as adaptive reasoning budgets versus explicit token limits, and flags models that reject standard sampling controls (e.g., temperature, top_p, top_k). It also provides tokenizer calibration multipliers to reconcile discrepancies between native BPE tokenizers and the cl100k_base encoding used by tiktoken, preventing context window overflow during high-density code analysis.

In addition to static configuration resolution, the module implements lightweight credential preflights and runtime catalog discovery. It validates environment variables, SDK installations, Google Vertex AI Application Default Credentials (ADC), and Anthropic CLI (ant auth status) profiles before expensive graph traversal passes begin. For OpenRouter endpoints, it features an in-memory cached model catalog fetcher with automatic cooldown backoff to dynamically determine remote context windows and provider-specific parameter capabilities.

flowchart TD
    startCheck["check_llm_auth()"] --> resolveProv["get_llm_provider()"]
    resolveProv --> checkProv{"Provider?"}

    subgraph AnthropicPreflight ["Anthropic Preflight"]
        anthCheck["check_anthropic_auth()"] --> sdkAnth{"anthropic SDK installed?"}
        sdkAnth -- No --> errAnthSdk["Emit ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING"]
        sdkAnth -- Yes --> checkAnthKeys{"API Key or Auth Token set?"}

        checkAnthKeys -- No --> checkAntCli{"ant CLI available?"}
        checkAntCli -- Yes --> runAnt["subprocess: ant auth status"]
        runAnt --> parseAnt["parse_ant_auth_status()"]
        parseAnt --> evalAnt{"Credential found?"}
        evalAnt -- Yes --> okAntLogin["Emit ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK"]
        evalAnt -- No --> errAntLogin["Emit ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN"]
        checkAntCli -- No --> checkDiskProfiles{"Stored ~/.config/anthropic credentials?"}
        checkDiskProfiles -- Yes --> warnDisk["Emit WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND"]
        checkDiskProfiles -- No --> errAnthCreds["Emit ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS"]
