docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves and returns the normalized Gemini model identifier configured for the current runtime. It inspects the GEMINI_MODEL environment variable, falling back to DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL (from utils.llm_config) if unset. The raw model string is stripped of leading resource path prefixes such as models/ or publishers/google/models/ via gemini_model_id to ensure compatibility with both AI Studio and Vertex AI SDK client calls.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * str: The sanitized model name (e.g., "gemini-3.7-flash").

Raises: None.

Example: 

def get_model() -> str:
    """GEMINI_MODEL without a 'models/' or 'publishers/google/models/' resource prefix."""
    return gemini_model_id(os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL)

The get_model function acts as the single entry point for model name normalization within the driver. Upstream dispatchers and internal helper functions use this sanitized ID to ensure cache consistency, pricing lookups, and SDK request formatting without redundant regex parsing.

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the maximum input and output token boundaries for a given Gemini model identifier. The function implements an in-memory caching mechanism via _model_limits_cache to minimize network overhead. When querying Google AI Studio (when GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is absent), the function attempts to fetch dynamic limits via client.models.get(model=model). If Vertex AI is active, or if the API query fails, the function falls back to static defaults defined in GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS (from utils.llm_config).

Parameters: * model (str): The normalized model identifier string.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A 2-element tuple representing (input_token_limit, output_token_limit).

Raises: None (internal exceptions during lookup are trapped, logged as warnings via emit(), and resolved to default limits).

Example: 

def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(input_token_limit, output_token_limit). AI Studio reports them via models.get; Vertex does
    not (the SDK maps no limits there), so the static Gemini 3.x / 2.5 table applies."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    limits = GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS
    if not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        try:
            info = _get_client().models.get(model=model)
            limits = (getattr(info, "input_token_limit", None) or limits[0], getattr(info, "output_token_limit", None) or limits[1])
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Gemini models.get | model={model} | input={limits[0]:,} | output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
        except Exception as e:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits

The implementation prevents repetitive remote lookups by memoizing results in _model_limits_cache. When running against Vertex AI endpoints, Google does not expose token ceilings via the standard models.get endpoint; the driver handles this discrepancy by bypassing the network lookup entirely and applying local static limits.

docs.title: call_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches a single-turn completion request to Google Gemini using streaming transport and returns the synthesized response text. It coordinates token estimation, thinking parameter selection, function calling suppression, stream processing, error recovery, operational logging, and finish reason classification.

Because this function implements the central workflow of the module, its internal logic is broken down into four distinct execution phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Configuration Preparation and Model Parameter Resolution
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw

    model = get_model()
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
    max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)
    thinking, level_desc = _thinking_config(model, thinking_level)
    # No tools are passed, so automatic function calling is off (google-genai warns on streams otherwise).
    no_afc = types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True)
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=thinking, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Gemini request | model={model} | {level_desc} | max_output_tokens={max_output:,} | location={gemini_location() if os.getenv('GEMINI_PROJECT_ID') else 'ai-studio'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

The initial phase resolves the model ID and calculates the baseline token count of the prompt using count_tokens_raw. It determines the output token ceiling by invoking _max_output_tokens and configures the reasoning behavior using _thinking_config. Automatic function calling is explicitly disabled using types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True) to prevent the SDK from emitting runtime stream warnings when no tool schemas are supplied.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution and Dynamic Thinking Fallback
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    try:
        result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
    except genai_errors.ClientError as e:
        # A model that rejects our thinking control (unknown future model, level set changed):
        # warn once and resend without it for the rest of the run.
        if getattr(e, "code", None) == 400 and thinking is not None and "think" in str(e).lower():
            _thinking_rejected.add(model)
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
            config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=None, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
            result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
        else:
            raise
    elapsed = time.time() - start

Execution delegates to the private _stream helper inside a timed block. If the endpoint rejects the thinking parameter by returning an HTTP 400 ClientError containing the string "think", the driver catches the exception, registers the model into _thinking_rejected to bypass thinking parameters on future calls, emits a warning, strips thinking_config, and immediately retries the request.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry Recording and Thought Logging
docs.text:
if result["usage"] is not None:
        _record(model, result["usage"], raw_tokens, level_desc, result["finish"], elapsed)
    else:
        record_usage("GEMINI", model, cost=None)
    if is_debug() and result["thoughts"]:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{result['thoughts']}", dest="LOG")

Once the stream completes, telemetry is written to the global usage ledger via _record(). If the response omitted usage metadata, record_usage() is called with cost=None to mark cost tracking as unverified. When CLI debugging is enabled via is_debug(), extracted reasoning traces (result["thoughts"]) are written to the persistent log file.

docs.title: Phase 4: Block and Truncation Post-Processing
docs.text:
if result["block_reason"] or result["finish"] in _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS:
        category = result["block_reason"] or result["finish"]
        # A blocked prompt repeats for the same input; a stop on the candidate may pass on resampling.
        retryable = not result["block_reason"] and result["finish"] in _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS
        count_event("GEMINI", "refusals")
        emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="Gemini", model=model, category=category)
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="GEMINI", retryable=retryable)
    if result["finish"] in _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS:
        count_event("GEMINI", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="Gemini", max_tokens=f"{max_output:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
    if not result["text"]:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Gemini response contained no text (finish_reason={result['finish'] or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
    return result["text"]

The final phase inspects candidate finish states and prompt feedback blocks. If the request was halted by safety mechanisms, terms-of-service violations, or content blocks (_BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS), it increments the refusal counter, logs a warning, and raises LLMRefusalError. It differentiates between permanent prompt refusals (retryable=False) and transient candidate stops (retryable=True). If the generation was halted due to context or budget exhaustion (MAX_TOKENS), it logs the truncation and returns a TruncatedResponse instance. Otherwise, it returns the generated text.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The full text prompt to be completed by the model. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): The requested reasoning intensity ("low", "medium", "high", etc.), or None to adopt the model default.

Returns: * str: The generated completion text, or an instance of TruncatedResponse (which subclasses str) if generation exceeded output token limits.

Raises: * LLMRefusalError: If the prompt or generated response was blocked by safety filters, recitation checks, or policy restrictions. * google.genai.errors.ClientError: For unhandled 4xx client errors that are not related to thinking parameter rejection. * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment.

Example: 

# Real usage pattern from utils/call_llm.py delegating to call_gemini
from utils.llm_gemini import call_gemini

response_text = call_gemini(
    prompt="Generate an architecture summary for the authentication subsystem.",
    thinking_level="high",
)

docs.title: _timeout_ms()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _timeout_ms() -> int:

Description: Parses the GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable to compute the global request timeout in milliseconds for the google-genai SDK. Because the SDK applies this deadline to the entire streamed response rather than individual socket read intervals, the timeout must accommodate extended reasoning cycles. The value is clamped to a minimum of 30.0 seconds (30,000 ms), defaulting to 1,800.0 seconds (1,800,000 ms or 30 minutes).

Parameters: None.

Returns: * int: Total per-request deadline in milliseconds.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _timeout_ms() -> int:
    """Total per-request deadline (the SDK applies it to the whole streamed response)."""
    try:
        seconds = float(os.getenv("GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "1800"))
    except ValueError:
        seconds = 1800.0
    return int(max(seconds, 30.0) * 1000)

The function incorporates defensive parsing of the environment variable. If an invalid or non-numeric string is configured, the ValueError exception handler reverts the value to the 1,800-second baseline. Clamping with max(seconds, 30.0) guarantees that aggressive user configurations do not drop connections during standard network handshakes.

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Initializes and returns the process-wide google.genai.Client singleton. The client is configured with HTTP deadline options derived from _timeout_ms() and automated retry parameters (HttpRetryOptions) for status codes 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504. The helper evaluates the execution environment to configure either Vertex AI (via GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and gemini_location()) or Google AI Studio (via GEMINI_API_KEY). When using AI Studio, vertexai=False is passed explicitly to prevent ambient environment variables such as GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI from rerouting requests.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * genai.Client: The configured Google GenAI client instance.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment.

Example: 

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        http_options = types.HttpOptions(
            timeout=_timeout_ms(),  # milliseconds; with no timeout a stalled connection hangs forever
            # One SDK retry for transient errors; PocketFlow node retries (5 x 20 s) sit on top.
            retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, http_status_codes=[408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]),
        )
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=gemini_location(), http_options=http_options)
        elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            # vertexai=False explicitly: GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true in the environment would otherwise
            # route the API key to Vertex AI.
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=False, api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"), http_options=http_options)
        else:
            raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    return _client

This helper manages client lifecycle state through the global _client reference. The SDK's built-in HTTP retry policy is constrained to two attempts, operating underneath the higher-level workflow retry loops in the pipeline's execution graph.

docs.title: _thinking_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None) -> tuple[types.ThinkingConfig | None, str]:

Description: Constructs the vendor-specific reasoning configuration object (types.ThinkingConfig) based on the target model's supported mode ("level" vs "budget"). If the model previously rejected thinking parameters (tracked in _thinking_rejected), the function bypasses configuration and returns None. For Gemini 3.x models (mode == "level"), it clamps the requested level to the model's supported enumeration via clamp_level, warning the user via warn_once if clamping occurs. For Gemini 2.5 models (mode == "budget"), it clamps the budget to the allowed integer range. The two modes are never mixed.

Parameters: * model (str): Normalized Gemini model name. * level (str | None): Desired reasoning intensity level.

Returns: * tuple[types.ThinkingConfig | None, str]: A tuple containing the initialized SDK thinking configuration (or None) and a human-readable telemetry description string.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None):
    """(ThinkingConfig | None, description). Never mixes thinking_level with thinking_budget."""
    mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
    include = True if is_debug() else None  # thought summaries only for the debug log
    if model in _thinking_rejected:
        return None, "default (thinking config rejected by model)"
    if not level:
        # Model default thinking; with --debug still ask for summaries so they can be logged.
        return (types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True) if include and mode != "none" else None), "default"
    if mode == "level":
        effective = clamp_level(level.lower(), spec) or spec[-1]
        if effective != level.lower() and warn_once("gemini_level", model, level):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effective, model=model)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=effective, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_level={effective}"
    if mode == "budget":
        low, high, _can_disable = spec
        budget = min(max(GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS.get(level.lower(), 4096), low), high)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=budget, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_budget={budget}"
    if warn_once("gemini_no_thinking", model):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
    return None, "unsupported"

The function coordinates with utils.llm_config.gemini_thinking_mode to determine whether the target model supports categorical thinking levels or integer token budgets. The include_thoughts flag is enabled only when debug logging is active (is_debug()), avoiding transport overhead and log bloat during standard execution.

docs.title: _max_output_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Resolves the maximum generation limit for output tokens based on the active model and reasoning intensity. It retrieves the model's static or queried token limit using get_model_limits(), and delegates budget calculation to gemini_output_budget from utils.llm_config. Because Google Gemini maintains separate input and output token quotas, the output budget is not dynamically reduced for large prompts.

Parameters: * model (str): Normalized model name. * level (str | None): Desired thinking level string.

Returns: * int: The maximum allowed output tokens for the completion request.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-level budget capped by the model's output limit. Gemini documents separate input and
    output limits, so output is not reduced for large prompts (input_token_budget still reserves it)."""
    _input_limit, output_limit = get_model_limits(model)
    return gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit)

This helper ensures that downstream requests do not exceed the architectural limits of the model while allocating sufficient headroom for internal reasoning steps, which share the max_output_tokens allocation on Gemini 3.x and 2.5 architectures.

docs.title: _name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _name(value) -> str:

Description: Normalizes enum members, status objects, or dynamic error types into a standardized uppercase string. In the google-genai SDK, unexpected or newly introduced finish reasons may arrive as raw strings or dynamically generated enum instances. This helper safely extracts the .name attribute if present, splits by dot notation, and transforms the resulting identifier to uppercase.

Parameters: * value (Any): An enum instance, string, or arbitrary object representing a finish or block reason.

Returns: * str: Standardized uppercase string identifier.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _name(value) -> str:
    """Enum → 'NAME' (unknown enum members arrive as dynamic values; compare by name)."""
    return (getattr(value, "name", None) or str(value or "")).split(".")[-1].upper()

By decoupling finish reason evaluation from static SDK enum classes, _name prevents AttributeError exceptions when newer API releases introduce unmapped finish conditions.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated financial cost (in USD) for an inference request based on token consumption, prompt caching, long-context thresholds, promotional pricing calendars, and deployment locations. It performs a longest-prefix match against the _PRICING table. If the model qualifies for introductory rates (_INTRO_PRICING) and the current date is before _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL (December 31, 2026), discounted rates are applied. If the input exceeds _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD (200,000 tokens) and the model defines dual-tier pricing, Tier-2 rates are evaluated. Finally, a 10% regional uplift (_REGIONAL_UPLIFT = 1.10) is applied if the request was routed through Vertex AI outside the global region.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model name. * prompt_tokens (int): Total input prompt tokens. * cached (int): Tokens read from explicit or implicit prompt context caches. * output_tokens (int): Total output tokens (including reasoning tokens). * today (datetime.date | None, optional): Explicit date override used for testing pricing cutoffs. Defaults to datetime.date.today().

Returns: * float | None: Estimated cost in USD, or None if the model pricing is unmapped.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:
    key = next((k for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if model.lower().startswith(k)), None)
    if key is None:
        return None
    row = _PRICING[key]
    if key in _INTRO_PRICING and (today or datetime.date.today()) <= _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL:
        row = _INTRO_PRICING[key]
    p_in, p_out, p_cache = row[3:6] if len(row) == 6 and prompt_tokens > _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD else row[:3]
    uncached = max(prompt_tokens - cached, 0)
    cost = (uncached * p_in + cached * p_cache + output_tokens * p_out) / 1_000_000
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") and gemini_location().lower() != "global":
        cost *= _REGIONAL_UPLIFT
    return cost

The algorithm splits input tokens into cached and uncached portions, applying differential rates to each. If a model identifier does not match any prefix in _PRICING, the function safely returns None, signaling downstream telemetry engines that costs could not be computed.

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:

Description: Extracts token metrics from the SDK's usage_metadata object, invokes _price() to estimate request expense, and writes operational metrics into the centralized session ledger using record_usage(). It calculates the observed tokenization ratio between Gemini's native tokenizer and the pipeline's offline estimator (raw_prompt_tokens), outputting detailed diagnostics to the debug log.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier. * usage (types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata): The usage container returned in the final stream chunk. * raw_prompt_tokens (int): The offline baseline token count computed prior to transmission. * level_desc (str): Telemetry description of the applied thinking configuration. * finish (str): Resolved finish reason identifier. * elapsed (float): Request duration in seconds.

Returns: None.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:
    prompt = getattr(usage, "prompt_token_count", 0) or 0
    candidates = getattr(usage, "candidates_token_count", 0) or 0
    thoughts = getattr(usage, "thoughts_token_count", 0) or 0
    cached = getattr(usage, "cached_content_token_count", 0) or 0
    output = candidates + thoughts  # thinking is billed as output
    cost = _price(model, prompt, cached, output)
    record_usage("GEMINI", model, input_tokens=prompt, output_tokens=output, thinking_tokens=thoughts, cache_read=cached, cost=cost)
    ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"GEMINI USAGE | model={model} | {level_desc} | finish={finish or 'n/a'} | in={prompt:,} | out={candidates:,} | thinking={thoughts:,} | "
        f"cached={cached:,} | est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

The function handles reasoning tokens by consolidating candidate tokens and thought tokens into total output volume, matching Google's billing architecture. The ratio of actual prompt tokens to raw offline estimates is tracked to assist in calibrating tokenizer multiplier settings.

docs.title: _stream()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config: types.GenerateContentConfig) -> dict:

Description: Consumes the generator returned by client.models.generate_content_stream. It iterates through streaming response chunks, accumulating text content, separating internal thoughts from candidate output, capturing prompt blocks, monitoring finish reasons, and saving the final usage metadata.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model identifier. * prompt (str): Raw prompt text. * config (types.GenerateContentConfig): Fully populated generation configuration schema.

Returns: * dict: An aggregation dictionary containing: * "text" (str): Concatenated output text. * "thoughts" (str): Concatenated thinking traces. * "finish" (str): Uppercase finish reason. * "block_reason" (str): Uppercase prompt block reason. * "usage" (types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata | None): Token usage metadata.

Raises: * google.genai.errors.ClientError: If network or authentication errors occur during stream consumption.

Example: 

def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config) -> dict:
    """Consume generate_content_stream; returns text, thoughts, finish, block_reason, usage."""
    text, thoughts = [], []
    finish, block_reason, usage = "", "", None
    for chunk in _get_client().models.generate_content_stream(model=model, contents=[prompt], config=config):
        feedback = getattr(chunk, "prompt_feedback", None)
        if feedback is not None and getattr(feedback, "block_reason", None):
            block_reason = _name(feedback.block_reason)
        if getattr(chunk, "usage_metadata", None) is not None:
            usage = chunk.usage_metadata
        for candidate in getattr(chunk, "candidates", None) or []:
            if getattr(candidate, "finish_reason", None):
                finish = _name(candidate.finish_reason)
            content = getattr(candidate, "content", None)
            for part in (getattr(content, "parts", None) or []) if content is not None else []:
                if getattr(part, "text", None):
                    (thoughts if getattr(part, "thought", False) else text).append(part.text)
            break  # candidate_count is 1
    return {"text": "".join(text), "thoughts": "".join(thoughts), "finish": finish, "block_reason": block_reason, "usage": usage}

The streaming loop evaluates candidate parts individually, appending content to thoughts if part.thought evaluates to True, and to text otherwise. It restricts candidate parsing to the first candidate (candidate_count is 1), matching the single-turn design of the pipeline.

docs.title: Stream Result Payload
docs.text:
Returned internally by _stream() to consolidate stream accumulation data:

Key Type Description "text" str Full synthesized response text from candidate parts where thought is false. "thoughts" str Internal reasoning traces extracted when include_thoughts=True. "finish" str Normalized finish reason name (e.g., "STOP", "MAX_TOKENS", "SAFETY"). "block_reason" str Normalized prompt feedback block reason (e.g., "SAFETY", "PROHIBITED_CONTENT"), or empty if unblocked. "usage" types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata \| None Google GenAI SDK token usage object containing prompt, candidate, and cached counts.

docs.text:
Module-level dictionary storing USD rates per million tokens. Entries follow the tuple format: (input_rate, output_rate, cached_input_rate[, input_rate_over_200k, output_rate_over_200k, cached_rate_over_200k])

docs.title: Environment Configuration Schema
docs.text:
The driver behavior is controlled through the following environment variables:

Variable Type Default Operational Impact GEMINI_API_KEY str "" Google AI Studio authentication key. Enables AI Studio transport mode. GEMINI_PROJECT_ID str "" Google Cloud project ID. Triggers Vertex AI transport mode (vertexai=True). GEMINI_LOCATION str "global" Google Cloud region for Vertex AI. Regional endpoints incur a 10% cost uplift. GEMINI_MODEL str DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL Target Gemini model identifier. GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS float 1800 Total stream execution deadline in seconds (clamped to a minimum of 30.0).

docs.title: Thinking Parameter Rejection Recovery
docs.text:
Certain experimental or future Gemini models may reject structured reasoning configurations via HTTP 400 Client Errors. The module catches these errors dynamically during stream execution:

    except genai_errors.ClientError as e:
        # A model that rejects our thinking control (unknown future model, level set changed):
        # warn once and resend without it for the rest of the run.
        if getattr(e, "code", None) == 400 and thinking is not None and "think" in str(e).lower():
            _thinking_rejected.add(model)
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
            config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=None, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
            result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
        else:
            raise

When an HTTP 400 error occurs and the error payload contains the substring "think", the model is permanently added to the _thinking_rejected set. The current request is immediately re-executed with thinking_config=None, ensuring the pipeline continues without failing the active workflow step.

docs.title: Safety Refusals and Policy Blocks
docs.text:
The driver standardizes vendor-specific safety classifications into LLMRefusalError (defined in utils.llm_common). It categorizes finish states into two distinct groups:

  1. Deterministic Refusals (retryable=False): Blocks triggered on the prompt itself (via block_reason) or finish reasons matching explicit policy violations:
  2. PROHIBITED_CONTENT, BLOCKLIST, SPII

  3. IMAGE_SAFETY, IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT, IMAGE_RECITATION, IMAGE_OTHER These errors indicate content that Google's filters will deterministically decline for the same input. They are not retried.

  4. Retryable Refusals (retryable=True): Blocks occurring on candidate generation where alternate sampling trajectories might succeed:

  5. SAFETY, RECITATION, LANGUAGE, OTHER These errors are flagged with retryable=True, allowing upstream execution graphs to attempt re-generation with altered sampling conditions.

docs.title: Response Truncation
docs.text: When generation terminates due to output budget limits, the SDK emits a finish_reason of MAX_TOKENS. The driver records the event using count_event("GEMINI", "truncations") and wraps the accumulated text in a TruncatedResponse instance. Upstream caching layers (in call_llm.py) identify this type and bypass disk caching to ensure partial outputs are not permanently stored.

docs.text:
• call_llm.py — Central inference facade and caching dispatcher that invokes call_gemini.
  • llm_config.py — Source of truth for model defaults, thinking mode definitions, output budgets, and credential validation.
  • llm_common.py — Shared types (LLMRefusalError, TruncatedResponse) and usage ledger functions (record_usage, count_event).
  • thinking.py — Utility functions for reasoning level validation and clamping (clamp_level).
  • token_utils.py — Offline token counting utilities used to compute prompt sizing ratios.
  • output.py — Centralized UI emitting and structured debug logging subsystem.

docs.title: llm_openrouter.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/llm_openrouter.py

Following the vendor-specific driver implementation for Google Gemini in llm_gemini.py, this module provides a catalog-driven integration layer for OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible API gateway. While llm_gemini.py and llm_anthropic.py interact directly with proprietary vendor SDKs, llm_openrouter.py acts as a polymorphic client capable of orchestrating requests across hundreds of upstream model architectures through a single standardized transport interface.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The primary responsibility of llm_openrouter.py is to execute single-turn chat completions against the OpenRouter gateway without hardcoding model capabilities. Instead of maintaining static parameter lookup tables for each upstream provider, the module queries metadata dynamically from the OpenRouter model catalog via llm_config.py (openrouter_model_info). This metadata dictates reasoning parameters, token constraints, context boundaries, and parameter eligibility (such as temperature filtering) for any arbitrary model identifier at runtime.

To maintain transport resilience during long-running generative passes and extended reasoning traces, all interactions are executed via Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming using requests.post(..., stream=True). This architecture prevents transport-layer socket timeouts by continually consuming SSE events while discarding gateway-specific keep-alive pulses (: OPENROUTER PROCESSING). The module transparently manages transient network anomalies and upstream rate limiting using exponential backoff aligned with server-supplied Retry-After headers.

The module standardizes downstream error handling by classifying diverse gateway responses into shared domain abstractions defined in llm_common.py. Generation outputs halted due to token ceilings are wrapped in TruncatedResponse to prevent corrupting local cache stores in call_llm.py. Upstream policy violations, moderation triggers, and safety guardrails are mapped to LLMRefusalError, explicitly differentiating between deterministic prompt rejections and transient sampling filter halts. Additionally, token telemetry and financial ledger entries—including Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) upstream inference surcharges—are recorded into session analytics via record_usage.

docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Retrieves and normalizes the target model identifier configured for the OpenRouter provider. The function inspects the OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable, stripping surrounding whitespace. If the variable is unset or empty, it returns an empty string, prompting downstream validation routines in call_openrouter() to halt execution.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: The stripped OpenRouter model identifier (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet", "deepseek/deepseek-r1"), or an empty string if unset.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

model = get_model()
if not model:
    raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")

docs.title: build_payload()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_payload(prompt: str, model: str, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, str]:

Description: Compiles the OpenAI-compatible JSON request payload tailored to the capabilities of the specified model. It queries catalog metadata using openrouter_model_info(model) to resolve output token ceilings, reasoning constraints, and parameter compatibility. The function dynamically sets stream mode, caps completion limits within available context windows, shapes the reasoning block, and evaluates whether temperature controls must be injected or suppressed.

docs.title: Phase 1: Context Resolution & Token Sizing
docs.text:
info = openrouter_model_info(model)
    max_tokens = _max_tokens(model, info, level, prompt_tokens)
    reasoning, desc = _reasoning(model, info, level, max_tokens)
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "stream": True,
    }
During the initial sizing phase, the function queries openrouter_model_info(model) to retrieve provider boundaries and upstream architectural limits. It invokes _max_tokens() to determine the maximum generation ceiling, clamping planned output against residual context space while accounting for prompt_tokens and internal headroom margins. It then delegates to _reasoning() to translate the abstract level string into vendor-specific reasoning structures. Finally, it initializes the baseline request dictionary with user messages and explicitly sets "stream": True to mandate Server-Sent Events from the gateway.

docs.title: Phase 2: Parameter Shaping & Temperature Policy
docs.text:
if max_tokens:
        payload["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
    if reasoning is not None:
        payload["reasoning"] = reasoning
    if _sends_temperature(model, info, reasoning):
        try:
            payload["temperature"] = float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE", "0.7"))
        except ValueError:
            payload["temperature"] = 0.7
    return payload, desc
In the parameter shaping phase, optional attributes are conditionally bound to the request dictionary. If max_tokens was successfully derived, it is injected into the payload; otherwise, it is omitted to allow unconstrained upstream execution. If structured reasoning was generated, the dictionary is attached under the "reasoning" key. The function then evaluates _sends_temperature(): if the model allows sampling parameters and is not engaged in extended reasoning, it parses OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE (defaulting to 0.7), falling back defensively if the environment variable cannot be parsed as a float.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw text prompt destined for model evaluation. * model (str): The OpenRouter model slug (e.g., "google/gemini-2.5-pro"). * level (str | None): The requested reasoning intensity level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"), or None for baseline generation. * prompt_tokens (int): Estimated token count of the prompt payload, scaled by tokenizer ratio multipliers.

Returns: * tuple[dict, str]: A 2-tuple containing: 1. dict: The serialized JSON request payload ready for HTTP transmission. 2. str: A human-readable diagnostic description of the applied reasoning configuration (e.g., "effort=medium" or "unsupported").

Raises: * None.

Example: 

raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
payload, desc = build_payload(prompt, model, thinking_level, int(raw_tokens * get_token_ratio()))
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", **_attribution_headers()}

docs.title: call_openrouter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_openrouter(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Coordinates the complete single-turn inference lifecycle over the OpenRouter gateway. It validates local environment settings, estimates input token footprints, constructs the catalog-adapted payload, and dispatches the streaming HTTP request. Upon receiving the stream, it accumulates chunks, handles keep-alive pulses, records comprehensive token and billing usage metrics, evaluates termination conditions (distinguishing between length-based truncations, fatal safety blocks, and transient moderation flags), and returns the final synthesized output.

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment Validation & Token Analysis
docs.text:
from utils.llm_config import get_token_ratio
    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw

    model = get_model()
    if not model:
        raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")
    api_key = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "").strip()
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
    payload, desc = build_payload(prompt, model, thinking_level, int(raw_tokens * get_token_ratio()))
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", **_attribution_headers()}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"
    max_tokens = payload.get("max_tokens")
The execution begins by performing local lazy imports to avoid circular dependency chains with configuration and tokenizer modules. It inspects get_model(), raising a ValueError immediately if the target model string is undefined. It calculates raw prompt tokens via count_tokens_raw(prompt) and scales the estimate by get_token_ratio() to account for cross-tokenizer variance before assembling the request payload. Headers are initialized with application/json, optional attribution metadata from _attribution_headers(), and bearer token authorization if OPENROUTER_API_KEY is present.

docs.title: Phase 2: Diagnostics & HTTP Dispatch
docs.text:
emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"OpenRouter request | model={model} | {desc} | max_tokens={f'{max_tokens:,}' if max_tokens else 'omitted'} | "
        f"temperature={payload.get('temperature', 'omitted')} | catalog={'yes' if openrouter_catalog() else 'no'} | "
        f"attribution={'on' if 'HTTP-Referer' in headers else 'off'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

    start = time.time()
    resp = _post(f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/chat/completions", headers, payload)
    generation_id = resp.headers.get("X-Generation-Id")
    result = _consume(resp)
Before network transport commences, detailed execution metadata is emitted to the diagnostic logger, tracing the resolved token caps, temperature values, and catalog availability. The system records the start timestamp and initiates the HTTP request via _post(), targeting /v1/chat/completions under the resolved base URL. Upon opening the HTTP socket, it extracts the gateway generation identifier (X-Generation-Id) from response headers and immediately streams the body through _consume(resp) to parse SSE lines into an in-memory aggregation dictionary.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry Recording & Debug Trace
docs.text:
_record(model, result, raw_tokens, desc, time.time() - start, generation_id)
    if is_debug() and result["reasoning"]:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"REASONING:\n{result['reasoning']}", dest="LOG")

    finish, native = (result["finish"] or ""), (result["native"] or "")
    if finish == "error":
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter generation ended with an error (native_finish_reason={native or 'n/a'})")
Once the stream concludes, the execution elapsed time is computed, and _record() updates internal session ledgers with token counts, cache hits, and calculated financial costs. If runtime debugging is enabled via is_debug() and reasoning traces were gathered from upstream models, the thought trace is written to the diagnostic log stream. The method then checks whether the generation terminated with a finish status of "error", raising a RuntimeError immediately to alert upstream pipeline coordinators.

docs.title: Phase 4: Termination Analysis & Output Classification
docs.text:
if finish == "content_filter" or result["refusal"] or native.lower() in _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS:
        category = native or finish or "refusal"
        # Filters on sampled output (safety, recitation, content_filter) may pass on another attempt.
        retryable = not result["refusal"] and native.lower() not in _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS
        count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
        emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER", retryable=retryable)
    if not finish:
        # No data at all, or the connection dropped mid-answer: never return a partial reply.
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"OpenRouter stream ended without a finish_reason after {result['events']} events ({len(result['text']):,} characters received)"
        )
    if finish == "length":
        count_event("OPENROUTER", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="OpenRouter", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}" if max_tokens else "default")
        return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
    if not result["text"]:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter response contained no text (finish_reason={finish or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
    return result["text"]
In the final evaluation phase, the termination metadata is verified against policy blocks and length exhaustion. If the stream encountered a content filter, an explicit refusal string, or a native safety flag, the method determines retryability: deterministic triggers (like prohibited_content or spii) raise non-retryable LLMRefusalError exceptions, whereas stochastic output filters raise retryable variants. If the stream terminated abruptly without a finish reason (signifying dropped TCP sockets), a RuntimeError prevents returning incomplete outputs. If execution halted due to "length", output is returned wrapped in a TruncatedResponse instance; otherwise, the accumulated plain text string is returned.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete synthesized prompt text destined for model execution. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning intensity level ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The model's complete generated completion string, or a TruncatedResponse subclass if execution hit token ceilings.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if OPENROUTER_MODEL is not defined in the process environment. * LLMRefusalError: Raised when upstream safety policies, moderation filters, or content blocks reject the prompt. * RuntimeError: Raised on non-retryable HTTP failures, gateway stream errors, or abruptly terminated connections.

Example: 

# Real invocation from utils/call_llm.py
from utils.llm_openrouter import call_openrouter

response = call_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level="medium")

docs.title: _read_timeout()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _read_timeout() -> float:

Description: Resolves the maximum socket read timeout allowed between successive SSE streaming events. It inspects the OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable, defaulting to 300.0 seconds if unset or invalid. To avoid premature connection termination during deep reasoning pauses, the returned value is clamped to a lower boundary of 30.0 seconds.

def _read_timeout() -> float:
    try:
        return max(float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "300")), 30.0)
    except ValueError:
        return 300.0

The helper safely wraps the environment lookup inside a try-except block targeting ValueError. If a non-numeric string is provided, it falls back to the 300.0-second default. When a valid float is parsed, max(..., 30.0) prevents misconfigurations from setting dangerously low read timeouts that would abort valid model reasoning pauses.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * float: The resolved timeout threshold in seconds (minimum 30.0).

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _reasoning()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _reasoning(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, max_tokens: int | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:

Description: Assembles the "reasoning" configuration block based on the requested level and catalog capabilities. It inspects whether the model supports explicit effort tiers ("supported_efforts") or raw token allocations ("supports_max_tokens"). In the absence of catalog metadata, it constructs an unverified effort payload, relying on server-side clamping.

docs.title: Phase 1: Level Validation & Unverified Model Fallback
docs.text:
if not level:
        return None, "default"
    level = level.lower()
    exclude = not is_debug()
    if info is None:
        # Catalog unavailable or model unknown: send the level; OpenRouter clamps server-side.
        return {"effort": level, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={level} (unverified)"
    reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
    if not isinstance(reasoning, dict) and "reasoning" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
        if warn_once("openrouter_no_reasoning", model):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
        return None, "unsupported"
The method begins by returning early if no reasoning level was requested. It forces the level string to lowercase and determines the exclude flag: reasoning text is stripped from the completion unless is_debug() is active. If the model catalog is unavailable or the model is unrecognized, it generates an unverified effort payload. If catalog data is present but indicates that reasoning is unsupported by parameters or metadata, it issues a single warning via warn_once and returns None.

docs.title: Phase 2: Budget-Only Reasoning Configuration
docs.text:
meta = reasoning if isinstance(reasoning, dict) else {}
    if "supported_efforts" not in meta and meta.get("supports_max_tokens"):
        # Budget-only model: an explicit thinking budget (OpenRouter's effort ratio of a large
        # max_tokens would over-spend). It must stay below max_tokens.
        budget = _REASONING_BUDGETS.get(level, _REASONING_BUDGETS["medium"])
        if max_tokens:
            budget = max(min(budget, max_tokens - 1_024), 1_024)
        return {"max_tokens": budget, "exclude": exclude}, f"reasoning.max_tokens={budget}"
If the model metadata lacks supported_efforts but contains supports_max_tokens, the model requires an explicit numeric token budget rather than an abstract effort string. The helper resolves the budget against _REASONING_BUDGETS (defaulting to the "medium" allocation of 8,192 tokens). If an upper completion limit (max_tokens) is active, it constrains the thinking allocation to leave at least 1,024 completion tokens free, clamping the budget floor at 1,024 tokens.

docs.title: Phase 3: Effort Clamping & Unsupported Guard
docs.text:
efforts = meta.get("supported_efforts")
    effort = level
    if efforts:
        effort = clamp_level(level, [e for e in efforts if e != "none"]) or level
        if effort != level and warn_once("openrouter_level", model, level):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effort, model=model)
    return {"effort": effort, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={effort}"
When supported_efforts is defined, the helper extracts the allowed tiers, explicitly stripping "none" to prevent HTTP 400 validation rejections on architectures with mandatory reasoning. It leverages clamp_level() from thinking.py to locate the closest compatible tier. If clamping alters the requested intensity, a deduplicated warning is logged. The final dictionary contains the resolved effort and the exclusion flag.

Parameters: * model (str): The OpenRouter model slug. * info (dict | None): The model catalog entry, or None if unknown. * level (str | None): The requested reasoning intensity. * max_tokens (int | None, optional): The calculated maximum generation ceiling. Defaults to None.

Returns: * tuple[dict | None, str]: A 2-tuple containing: 1. dict | None: The serialized payload for the "reasoning" key, or None if unsupported. 2. str: Diagnostic description of the applied configuration.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _sends_temperature()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the temperature parameter should be included in the request payload. Sampling parameters are suppressed if reasoning is active, if the model architecture belongs to a family that rejects sampling controls, or if catalog metadata flags temperature as unsupported or overridden by default reasoning.

def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:
    if reasoning is not None or rejects_sampling_params(model):
        return False
    if info is None:
        return True
    if "temperature" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
        return False
    meta = info.get("reasoning") if isinstance(info.get("reasoning"), dict) else {}
    return not (meta.get("mandatory") or meta.get("default_enabled"))

The function checks if reasoning is active or if rejects_sampling_params(model) (from llm_config.py) matches the model identifier, returning False immediately. If catalog information is unavailable, it permits temperature by default. If catalog metadata exists, it verifies that "temperature" is declared under supported_parameters, and confirms that reasoning is neither mandatory nor enabled by default on the upstream model.

Parameters: * model (str): The target model identifier. * info (dict | None): The OpenRouter catalog metadata dictionary. * reasoning (dict | None): The active reasoning payload structure, if any.

Returns: * bool: True if temperature should be sent; otherwise, False.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:

Description: Computes the output token budget for the request, clamping planned reservations against residual context space. It queries openrouter_output_budget(model, level) and subtracts input prompt tokens and safety margins (CONTEXT_MARGIN) from the context window length reported by OpenRouter's catalog.

def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:
    """Planned max_tokens clamped to the context left after the prompt; None = omit (unknown model)."""
    planned = openrouter_output_budget(model, level)
    context = ((info or {}).get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or (info or {}).get("context_length")
    if planned and context:
        planned = min(planned, max(context - prompt_tokens - CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096))
    return planned

The implementation first resolves the planned output budget via openrouter_output_budget(). It inspects catalog metadata, preferring top_provider.context_length before falling back to top-level context_length. If both a planned budget and a context ceiling exist, it clamps the planned allocation so it does not exceed the remaining capacity (context - prompt_tokens - CONTEXT_MARGIN), maintaining a guaranteed baseline floor of 4,096 tokens.

Parameters: * model (str): The target model identifier. * info (dict | None): The catalog metadata dictionary. * level (str | None): The active reasoning intensity level. * prompt_tokens (int): Scaled token count of the prompt payload.

Returns: * int | None: Clamped token ceiling, or None if the model or its limits are unrecognized.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _attribution_headers()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _attribution_headers() -> dict:

Description: Generates opt-in HTTP headers to attribute API traffic to the Codebase Knowledge Builder application on OpenRouter's activity boards and leaderboards. Attribution is strictly opt-in and is only activated when OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set in the environment.

def _attribution_headers() -> dict:
    """OpenRouter app attribution (rankings / activity page), opt-in: nothing identifying the tool is
    sent unless OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set. OpenRouter attributes by HTTP-Referer; the title needs it."""
    url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_APP_URL", "").strip()
    if not url:
        return {}
    return {"HTTP-Referer": url, "X-OpenRouter-Title": _APP_TITLE, "X-Title": _APP_TITLE}  # X-Title: legacy name

The helper reads OPENROUTER_APP_URL from the process environment. If empty or absent, it returns an empty dictionary, ensuring no identifying metadata is transmitted. If configured, it populates HTTP-Referer alongside the primary X-OpenRouter-Title header and legacy X-Title header with the constant _APP_TITLE ("Codebase Knowledge Builder").

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: Dictionary containing attribution headers, or an empty dictionary if disabled.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _retry_after()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:

Description: Extracts and parses the standard Retry-After HTTP header from an incoming response object.

def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:
    value = resp.headers.get("Retry-After")
    try:
        return float(value) if value else None
    except ValueError:
        return None

The function reads the header string and attempts to convert it to a floating-point number representing seconds. If the header is missing, empty, or cannot be parsed as a float (such as an HTTP-date string), it returns None.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response received from the gateway.

Returns: * float | None: Wait time in seconds, or None if unparseable or absent.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _error_body()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _error_body(resp) -> dict:

Description: Safely deserializes the JSON error payload from a failed HTTP response, handling nested error dictionaries and malformed non-JSON error pages.

def _error_body(resp) -> dict:
    try:
        body = resp.json()
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    err = body.get("error", body) if isinstance(body, dict) else body
    return err if isinstance(err, dict) else {"message": str(err)}

The function executes resp.json() inside a try-except block. If parsing fails, it returns an empty dictionary. When JSON is parsed, it unwraps the nested "error" sub-dictionary if present. If the resulting structure is not a dictionary, it wraps the raw primitive in a {"message": str(err)} container to ensure downstream consumers always receive a dictionary.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response object.

Returns: * dict: Deserialized error dictionary.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _error_detail()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _error_detail(resp) -> str:

Description: Extracts a formatted diagnostic summary string from an error response, incorporating upstream provider metadata where available.

def _error_detail(resp) -> str:
    err = _error_body(resp)
    if not err:
        return resp.text[:300].strip()
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    raw = meta.get("raw") or meta.get("provider_name") or ""
    return f"{err.get('message', err)}" + (f" ({raw})" if raw else "")

The function obtains the error dictionary via _error_body(). If empty, it returns the first 300 characters of the raw response text. If structured error data exists, it reads error metadata to identify upstream provider names or raw gateway diagnostics, appending them in parentheses after the main error message.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The HTTP error response.

Returns: * str: Formatted error description.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _refusal_category()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:

Description: Inspects an HTTP 403 Forbidden response to determine if it represents a content moderation refusal, safety guardrail halt, or upstream policy violation.

def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:
    """Category when an HTTP 403 is a moderation / guardrail / upstream refusal, else None."""
    if resp.status_code != 403:
        return None
    err = _error_body(resp)
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    kind = str(err.get("type") or err.get("error_type") or meta.get("error_type") or "").lower()
    if kind in _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES:
        return kind
    if meta.get("reasons") or meta.get("flagged_input"):
        reasons = meta.get("reasons") or ["moderation"]
        return ",".join(map(str, reasons)) if isinstance(reasons, list) else str(reasons)
    return None

The helper returns None immediately if status_code != 403. It then evaluates the error payload: if the error type matches _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES ("refusal", "content_policy_violation", "moderation"), it returns the normalized type string. If the metadata indicates flagged inputs or explicit moderation reason codes, it flattens the reasons list into a comma-separated string.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response to inspect.

Returns: * str | None: The identified refusal category string, or None if the 403 status is an unrelated authorization failure.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: _post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _post(url: str, headers: dict, payload: dict):

Description: Executes an HTTP POST request with streaming enabled, managing bounded retry loops against transient network dropouts and gateway rate limits.

docs.title: Phase 1: Connection & Timeout Exception Handling
docs.text:
for attempt in range(1, _MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, stream=True, timeout=(15, _read_timeout()))
        except (requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout) as e:
            if attempt == _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter request failed after {attempt} attempts: {e}") from e
            time.sleep(2**attempt)
            continue
The helper iterates across a loop bounded by _MAX_ATTEMPTS (3 attempts). It executes requests.post() configured with a 15-second connect timeout and a dynamic read timeout from _read_timeout(). Low-level transport exceptions (ConnectionError, Timeout) are caught: if the retry threshold is reached, a RuntimeError is raised; otherwise, the thread sleeps for an exponentially increasing delay ($2^{\text{attempt}}$ seconds) before retrying.

docs.title: Phase 2: Transient Status Code Evaluation & Backoff
docs.text:
if resp.status_code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS and attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
            wait = min(_retry_after(resp) or 2**attempt * 2, 60)
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}; retrying in {wait:.0f}s ({_error_detail(resp)})", dest="LOG")
            resp.close()
            time.sleep(wait)
            continue
If the server returns a retryable status code defined in _RETRYABLE_STATUS ({408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529}) and attempts remain, the function evaluates the backoff delay. It checks _retry_after(resp), falling back to exponential backoff ($2^{\text{attempt}} \times 2$) capped at 60 seconds. It emits a warning to the diagnostic logger, explicitly closes the active response connection, and sleeps for the computed duration.

docs.title: Phase 3: Error Classification & Refusal Resolution
docs.text:
if resp.status_code >= 400:
            detail, category = _error_detail(resp), _refusal_category(resp)
            resp.close()
            if category:
                model = payload.get("model", "")
                count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
                emit("WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
                emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP 403 refusal: {detail}", dest="LOG")
                raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER")
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}: {detail}")
        return resp
    raise RuntimeError("OpenRouter request failed")  # unreachable
For non-retryable status codes ($\ge 400$), the helper closes the socket immediately. It invokes _refusal_category(resp): if an HTTP 403 is categorized as a moderation or content violation, it updates refusal event metrics via count_event(), logs localized and raw warnings, and raises an LLMRefusalError. Any other status code raises a fatal RuntimeError containing the detailed error string. If the status is $200$, the open response stream is returned.

Parameters: * url (str): Target completions endpoint URL. * headers (dict): HTTP headers including authorization and attribution. * payload (dict): Serialized request dictionary.

Returns: * requests.Response: The active, open streaming HTTP response.

Raises: * LLMRefusalError: When an HTTP 403 response represents an upstream moderation or refusal block. * RuntimeError: When all retry attempts fail or a fatal HTTP status code is encountered.

docs.title: _consume()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _consume(resp) -> dict:

Description: Parses the incoming Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream line-by-line, isolating content deltas, reasoning traces, refusal states, and usage objects.

docs.title: Phase 1: Direct JSON Detection
docs.text:
out = {"text": [], "reasoning": [], "finish": None, "native": None, "refusal": None, "usage": None, "events": 0}
    try:
        if "application/json" in (resp.headers.get("Content-Type") or "").lower():
            # An OpenAI-compatible proxy that ignores stream=true answers with one JSON body.
            _apply_chunk(out, resp.json())
The method initializes the accumulator dictionary out with empty lists for text and reasoning buffers. It inspects the Content-Type header: if an upstream gateway or proxy ignores stream=True and delivers a static application/json response, it decodes the entire body via resp.json() and passes it directly to _apply_chunk(), bypassing SSE stream iteration entirely.

docs.title: Phase 2: SSE Byte Decoding & Keep-Alive Filtering
docs.text:
else:
            for raw_line in resp.iter_lines():
                line = raw_line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if isinstance(raw_line, bytes) else raw_line
                if not line or line.startswith(":") or not line.startswith("data:"):
                    continue  # blank separators and ': OPENROUTER PROCESSING' keep-alives
                data = line[5:].strip()
                if data == "[DONE]":
                    break
                try:
                    chunk = json.loads(data)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                _apply_chunk(out, chunk)
    finally:
        resp.close()
For standard SSE streams, lines are consumed via resp.iter_lines(). Bytes are decoded individually using UTF-8 with errors="replace", avoiding standard line splitters that mistakenly break on characters like U+2028 or U+0085 embedded in JSON payloads. It filters out empty lines, comments (such as : OPENROUTER PROCESSING keep-alive pulses), and lines lacking the data: prefix. It strips the prefix, terminates parsing on the sentinel [DONE], parses the JSON chunk safely, and folds it into the result via _apply_chunk(). The socket is guaranteed to close via the finally block.

docs.title: Phase 3: Buffer Aggregation
docs.text:
out["text"] = "".join(out["text"])
    out["reasoning"] = "".join(out["reasoning"])
    return out
Once stream iteration completes, the list of text fragments and reasoning deltas are concatenated into consolidated strings using "".join(). The consolidated out dictionary is then returned for post-processing and evaluation.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The open streaming response object.

Returns: * dict: Aggregated stream results (see ParsedStreamResult in Data Structures).

Raises: * RuntimeError: If an individual chunk contains an embedded error object.

docs.title: _apply_chunk()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:

Description: Updates the running stream accumulator dictionary with delta fragments extracted from a single SSE event or non-streamed response chunk.

def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:
    """Fold one stream chunk (or a whole non-streamed completion) into the _consume result."""
    out["events"] += 1
    if chunk.get("error"):
        err = chunk["error"]
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter stream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")
    if chunk.get("usage"):
        out["usage"] = chunk["usage"]
    for choice in chunk.get("choices") or []:
        delta = choice.get("delta") or choice.get("message") or {}
        if delta.get("content"):
            out["text"].append(delta["content"])
        if delta.get("reasoning"):
            out["reasoning"].append(delta["reasoning"])
        if delta.get("refusal"):
            out["refusal"] = delta["refusal"]
        if choice.get("finish_reason"):
            out["finish"] = choice["finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("native_finish_reason"):
            out["native"] = choice["native_finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("error"):
            err = choice["error"]
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter upstream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")

The function increments the event counter and checks for mid-stream error payloads, raising a RuntimeError immediately if one is detected. It records usage metadata when provided in the chunk. It then iterates through choices, extracting fragments from either delta (in streaming mode) or message (in non-streaming fallback mode), appending content and reasoning strings, and capturing refusal, finish_reason, and native_finish_reason attributes.

Parameters: * out (dict): The mutable result dictionary being assembled by _consume(). * chunk (dict): Deserialized JSON payload representing a single chunk.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * RuntimeError: If chunk or choice contains an error payload from OpenRouter or upstream providers.

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:

Description: Computes token usage, applies BYOK cost corrections, logs structured diagnostics, and records metrics in the central ledger via record_usage().

def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:
    usage = result["usage"] or {}
    prompt = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
    completion = usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0  # includes reasoning tokens
    reasoning_tokens = (usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0
    details = usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}
    cached = details.get("cached_tokens") or 0
    cache_write = details.get("cache_write_tokens") or 0
    cost = usage.get("cost")
    upstream = (usage.get("cost_details") or {}).get("upstream_inference_cost")
    if usage.get("is_byok") and isinstance(upstream, int | float):
        # BYOK: `cost` is only OpenRouter's fee; the provider bills upstream_inference_cost to your key.
        cost = (cost if isinstance(cost, int | float) else 0.0) + upstream
    record_usage(
        "OPENROUTER",
        model,
        input_tokens=prompt,
        output_tokens=completion,
        thinking_tokens=reasoning_tokens,
        cache_read=cached,
        cache_write=cache_write,
        cost=float(cost) if isinstance(cost, int | float) else None,
    )
    ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | {desc} | finish={result['finish']} (native={result['native']}) | in={prompt:,} | out={completion:,} | "
        f"reasoning={reasoning_tokens:,} | cached={cached:,} | cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if isinstance(cost, int | float) else 'n/a'} | "
        f"elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f} | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

The function extracts token metrics from result["usage"], distinguishing between prompt tokens, completion tokens, thinking tokens, and cache hits. If the request was executed under Bring-Your-Own-Key (is_byok), OpenRouter's cost field reflects only gateway routing fees; the function therefore adds upstream_inference_cost from cost_details to determine true total expenditure. It calls record_usage() from llm_common.py and logs full usage telemetry via emit_raw().

Parameters: * model (str): The OpenRouter model slug. * result (dict): Stream output dictionary assembled by _consume(). * raw_prompt_tokens (int): Baseline token count from tokenizer estimation. * desc (str): Diagnostic reasoning configuration description. * elapsed (float): Total wall-clock execution time in seconds. * generation_id (str | None): OpenRouter generation tracking ID from the X-Generation-Id header.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: ParsedStreamResult
docs.text:
The dictionary structure constructed and populated by _consume() and _apply_chunk(), aggregating fragments received over the Server-Sent Events stream.

Field Type Description text str Complete accumulated text output generated by the model. reasoning str Accumulated thought/reasoning trace text emitted prior to the final response. finish str \| None Standardized finish reason (e.g., "stop", "length", "content_filter"). native str \| None Upstream provider finish reason string (e.g., "MAX_TOKENS", "SAFETY"). refusal str \| None Explicit model refusal message if provided in delta payloads. usage dict \| None Raw usage metadata dictionary returned in the final stream chunk. events int Total count of SSE chunk events processed during the stream.

Example Value: 

{
    "text": "# Module Architecture\n\nThis component handles...",
    "reasoning": "Analyzing requirements: need to document methods...",
    "finish": "stop",
    "native": "stop",
    "refusal": None,
    "usage": {
        "prompt_tokens": 1240,
        "completion_tokens": 450,
        "total_tokens": 1690,
        "cost": 0.00342,
        "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 128}
    },
    "events": 42
}

docs.title: ReasoningPayload
docs.text:
The configuration dictionary generated by _reasoning() and attached under the "reasoning" key in OpenRouter chat completion payloads.

Field Type Description effort str Optional effort intensity level ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "max"). max_tokens int Optional explicit thinking token budget for models lacking effort tier support. exclude bool Flag indicating whether reasoning text should be omitted from output (True unless in debug mode).

Example Values: 

# Effort-based model configuration:
{"effort": "medium", "exclude": True}

# Budget-based model configuration:
{"max_tokens": 8192, "exclude": True}

docs.title: ChatCompletionPayload
docs.text:
The primary request body structure constructed by build_payload() for transmission to OpenRouter's /v1/chat/completions endpoint.

Field Type Description model str Target model identifier on OpenRouter. messages list[dict] Message history list containing the single user prompt dictionary. stream bool Always True, enforcing Server-Sent Events streaming. max_tokens int (optional) Upper bound on generation tokens, clamped to residual context space. reasoning dict (optional) Structured reasoning parameters (ReasoningPayload). temperature float (optional) Sampling temperature, omitted when reasoning is active or models reject sampling.

Example Value: 

{
    "model": "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write module documentation..."}],
    "stream": True,
    "max_tokens": 16384,
    "reasoning": {"effort": "medium", "exclude": True}
}

docs.title: AppAttributionHeaders
docs.text:
The HTTP request headers generated by _attribution_headers() when attribution is enabled.

Field Type Description HTTP-Referer str The application URL configured via OPENROUTER_APP_URL. X-OpenRouter-Title str Application identification title ("Codebase Knowledge Builder"). X-Title str Legacy identification title header matching _APP_TITLE.

Example Value: 

{
    "HTTP-Referer": "https://github.com/example/codebase-knowledge-builder",
    "X-OpenRouter-Title": "Codebase Knowledge Builder",
    "X-Title": "Codebase Knowledge Builder"
}

docs.title: Transient HTTP Status Handling
docs.text: Network communication over OpenRouter is safeguarded against transient upstream disconnections and traffic spikes. The driver automatically intercepts status codes defined in _RETRYABLE_STATUS (408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529): * Up to _MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) tries are performed. * Delays honor server-supplied Retry-After headers if present and parseable as floats. * In the absence of Retry-After, an exponential backoff formula ($2^{\text{attempt}} \times 2$) is evaluated, capped at 60.0 seconds.

docs.title: Policy Violations, Moderation & Refusal Classification
docs.text: The module differentiates between deterministic rejections and transient content moderation filters: * HTTP 403 Inspection: _refusal_category() inspects the error payload of HTTP 403 responses. If the error matches _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES ("refusal", "content_policy_violation", "moderation") or metadata flags, an LLMRefusalError(retryable=False) is raised. * Native Finish Reason Mapping: During stream analysis, _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS ({"refusal", "safety", "prohibited_content", "recitation", "blocklist", "spii", "content_filter"}) are flagged as refusals. * Deterministic vs. Retryable: If the stop reason is contained in _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS ({"refusal", "prohibited_content", "blocklist", "spii"}), it indicates an unrecoverable policy failure. Conversely, stochastic generation filters (such as recitation or content_filter) raise LLMRefusalError(retryable=True), signaling upstream graph controllers in nodes.py that resampling with different parameters may succeed.

docs.title: Stream Integrity & Truncation Handling
docs.text:
• Dropped Connections: If the SSE stream completes without delivering a finish_reason, the module assumes a socket disconnect occurred mid-generation. It raises a RuntimeError rather than returning a corrupt partial string.
  • Length Exhaustion: If finish == "length", generation stopped due to token budget depletion. The module wraps the accumulated text in TruncatedResponse(result["text"]) and increments truncation event counters via count_event(). The upstream cache engine in call_llm.py detects the TruncatedResponse type and bypasses disk persistence.

docs.text:

  • llm_common.py — Shared domain layer defining LLMRefusalError, TruncatedResponse, and telemetry registries.
  • llm_config.py — Source of truth for OpenRouter model catalogs, token ratios, and sampling parameter rules.
  • thinking.py — Clamping logic that matches requested thinking levels to supported model tiers.
  • token_utils.py — Token counting utilities used to estimate prompt sizing before request compilation.

  • llm_anthropic.py — Native driver for Anthropic Claude models.

docs.title: mkdocs.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/mkdocs.py

Following the OpenRouter client implementation in llm_openrouter.py, which serves as an inference transport driver, utils/mkdocs.py acts as the document compilation and static-site generation engine of the repository. It consolidates all structural formatting, configuration synthesis, cross-chapter link normalization, and filesystem emission routines required to serialize abstract syntax trees and LLM-drafted documentation into navigable static documentation websites or standalone Markdown bundles.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/mkdocs.py module orchestrates the final serialization phase of the synthesis pipeline. When downstream synthesis nodes complete chapter drafting and module mapping, this module transforms raw markdown text, metadata dictionaries, and hierarchical relationship structures into a fully functional MkDocs Material documentation site or an integrated standalone Markdown distribution. It handles site configuration generation, navigation tree layout, responsive diagram initialization, landing page synthesis, and cross-document hyperlink resolution.

A primary technical challenge resolved by this module is cross-chapter link consistency. Because LLMs synthesize chapter documentation independently, relative markdown links generated between files often contain invalid directory offsets or assume a flat hierarchy. The module implements a two-pass deterministic link normalizer that maps base filenames and paths to canonical output locations, disambiguates colliding basenames across nested directories, and rewrites markdown hyperlinks using exact filesystem relative offsets. Furthermore, for large codebases documented in API reference mode, the module provides automated navigation grouping: when module counts exceed configurable thresholds, it dispatches prompts to an LLM to categorize files logically, falls back gracefully to directory structures upon failure, and auto-sub-groups subdirectories deterministically.
