Additionally, utils/mkdocs.py bridges the visual rendering gap between MkDocs Material and Mermaid diagrams. By default, the Material theme overrides Mermaid styles, altering diagram geometries and contrast. This module generates a specialized javascripts/mermaid-init.js bootstrap script paired with custom superfences configurations (mermaid-raw) that strips intermediate wrapping elements rendered by pymdownx.superfences and invokes the native Mermaid rendering engine with interactive Panzoom support.

docs.title: yaml_str()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def yaml_str(value) -> str:

Description: Safely quotes and escapes scalar values (such as navigation labels, chapter titles, and filesystem paths) for insertion into hand-built YAML configuration blocks and Markdown frontmatter. Under the hood, the function delegates serialization to json.dumps(str(value).strip(), ensure_ascii=False). Because valid JSON string literals conform strictly to YAML double-quoted scalar grammar, this strategy guarantees that arbitrary strings containing reserved YAML control characters (such as colons :, brackets [], braces {}, quotes ', leading dashes -, or @ symbols) will not corrupt configuration syntax.

Parameters: * value (Any): The scalar object or string to be escaped.

Returns: * str: A valid, double-quoted, escaped YAML string representation.

Example: 

# Escaping arbitrary module labels and directory paths for YAML navigation lines
lines.append(f"{pad}  - {yaml_str(dir_path)}:")
for mod_name, match in dir_groups[dir_path]:
    lines.append(f"{pad}    - {yaml_str(mod_name)}: {yaml_str('api/' + match['filename'])}")


def yaml_str(value) -> str:
    """Quote a scalar for hand-built YAML (nav labels, section names, titles).

    JSON string literals are valid YAML double-quoted scalars, so names containing
    apostrophes, colons, brackets or a leading @ never break mkdocs.yml or frontmatter.
    """
    return json.dumps(str(value).strip(), ensure_ascii=False)
The implementation converts input values to strings, trims surrounding whitespace, and serializes them using json.dumps. The flag ensure_ascii=False is enforced so that Unicode characters (such as Asian logograms, accented Cyrillic, or Latin script diacritics) remain unescaped, ensuring readability in generated configuration files while remaining fully compliant with YAML parsers.

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:

Description: Assembles the complete textual contents of a production-ready mkdocs.yml configuration file configured for the MkDocs Material theme. It integrates syntax highlighting via pymdownx.highlight, inline code highlighting via pymdownx.inlinehilite, copy-to-clipboard code block buttons, pan-and-zoom controls via the panzoom plugin, custom Mermaid diagram fences via pymdownx.superfences, dark/light palette toggles, localized theme strings, and structured navigation trees.

Parameters: * site_name (str): Display title of the documentation website. * nav_yaml (str): Serialized YAML string defining the navigation structure. * include_home (bool): When True, prepends a root Home: index.md navigation entry. Defaults to True. * lang_code (str): Optional ISO language code (e.g., "vi", "zh", "fr") to configure MkDocs Material UI localization.

Returns: * str: Formatted mkdocs.yml configuration file ready for disk emission.

Example: 

# Assembling configuration inside write_mkdocs_output()
mkdocs_config = build_mkdocs_config(site_title, nav_snippet, include_home=True, lang_code=lang_code)
mkdocs_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "mkdocs.yml")
with open(mkdocs_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(mkdocs_config)


def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:
    # Extract nav items from nav_snippet (strip the "nav:" header line)
    nav_lines = nav_yaml.split("\n")
    nav_body = "\n".join(nav_lines[1:]) if nav_lines else ""

    # Conditional Home nav entry (CI has root index.md, local mkdocs doesn't)
    home_line = "  - Home: index.md\n" if include_home else ""

    # Optional Material theme language (e.g. "vi", "zh", "ja", "ko")
    lang_line = f"  language: {lang_code}\n" if lang_code else ""

    return (
        f"site_name: {yaml_str(site_name)}\n"
        f"theme:\n"
        f"  name: material\n"
        f"{lang_line}"
        f"  features:\n"
        f"    - content.code.copy\n"
        f"    - navigation.indexes\n"
        f"  palette:\n"
        f"    - scheme: default\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-7\n"
        f"        name: Switch to dark mode\n"
        f"    - scheme: slate\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-4\n"
        f"        name: Switch to light mode\n"
        f"plugins:\n"
        f"  - search\n"
        f"  - panzoom:\n"
        f"      include_selectors:\n"
        f"        - '.mermaid-raw'\n"
        f"markdown_extensions:\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.highlight:\n"
        f"      anchor_linenums: true\n"
        f"      use_pygments: true\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.superfences:\n"
        f"      custom_fences:\n"
        f"        - name: mermaid\n"
        f"          class: mermaid-raw\n"
        f"          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.inlinehilite\n"
        f"extra_javascript:\n"
        f"  - https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.min.js\n"
        f"  - javascripts/mermaid-init.js\n"
        f"nav:\n"
        f"{home_line}"
        f"{nav_body}\n"
    )
The constructor dynamically parses nav_yaml by stripping redundant top-level nav: declarations, preventing invalid duplicate YAML keys when embedding user-defined sub-navigation hierarchies. It configures the pymdownx.superfences custom fence to attach the CSS class mermaid-raw instead of standard mermaid. This class binding works in tandem with the Panzoom plugin selector include_selectors: - '.mermaid-raw', which routes diagram panning and zooming events to pure Mermaid renderings rather than Material-styled containers.

docs.title: build_mermaid_init_js()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mermaid_init_js() -> str:

Description: Returns the runtime JavaScript source code that initializes the Mermaid client library within MkDocs Material. The returned script coordinates lifecycle execution during DOMContentLoaded, bypasses Material's default Mermaid stylesheet overrides, unwraps the nested HTML structure generated by pymdownx.superfences, and executes client-side rendering.

Returns: * str: Complete JavaScript script buffer conforming to browser execution standards.

Example: 

# Emitting the initialization asset to the docs build directory
js_dir = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "javascripts")
os.makedirs(js_dir, exist_ok=True)
js_filepath = os.path.join(js_dir, "mermaid-init.js")
with open(js_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(build_mermaid_init_js())


MERMAID_INIT_JS = """\
// Mermaid initialization for MkDocs Material.
//
// Material for MkDocs targets .mermaid class for its own color overrides.
// By using .mermaid-raw, diagrams render with Mermaid's default theme:
// yellow subgraph backgrounds, lavender nodes, clean rectangles.
//
// pymdownx.superfences fence_code_format wraps content as:
//   <pre class="mermaid-raw"><code>flowchart TD ...</code></pre>
// Mermaid expects the diagram text directly in the target element,
// so we unwrap the <code> child before calling mermaid.run().
(function() {
  function initMermaid() {
    if (typeof mermaid === 'undefined') return;
    try {
      // Unwrap: move <code> text content up to <pre> and remove <code>
      document.querySelectorAll('pre.mermaid-raw > code').forEach(function(code) {
        var pre = code.parentElement;
        pre.textContent = code.textContent;
      });
      mermaid.initialize({
        startOnLoad: false,
        theme: 'default',
        securityLevel: 'loose'
      });
      mermaid.run({ querySelector: '.mermaid-raw' }).catch(function(err) {
        console.warn('Mermaid render error:', err);
      });
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn('Mermaid init error:', e);
    }
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initMermaid);
  } else {
    initMermaid();
  }
})();
"""


def build_mermaid_init_js() -> str:
    """Return the JavaScript snippet that initializes Mermaid diagrams."""
    return MERMAID_INIT_JS
The client script operates within an Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE) to avoid polluting global window namespaces. Because pymdownx.superfences wraps custom fence blocks inside <pre class="mermaid-raw"><code>...</code></pre>, standard Mermaid parsing fails because it expects raw diagram definitions directly inside the target container. The script resolves this by traversing document.querySelectorAll('pre.mermaid-raw > code'), assigning the inner text content of each <code> block directly to its parent <pre> node, clearing the intermediate element, and then executing mermaid.run({ querySelector: '.mermaid-raw' }).

docs.title: normalize_chapter_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: Executes deterministic, in-place link normalization across all generated markdown chapter contents. It inspects all internal cross-chapter hyperlinks ([anchor](target.md)), verifies whether targets point to valid chapter paths or simple file names, and replaces them with mathematically precise relative filesystem paths computed from the referencing file's directory to the target file's directory.

Parameters: * chapter_files (list[dict]): Mutable list of chapter file dictionaries, where each item must contain at least "filename" and "content".

docs.title: Phase 1: Canonical Filename Lookup and Ambiguity Resolution
docs.text:
# Build lookup: various path forms → canonical filename
    filename_lookup = {}
    ambiguous_basenames = set()
    for cf in chapter_files:
        fname = cf["filename"]  # e.g. "CoreService/AccountingService.cs.md"
        filename_lookup[fname] = fname
        basename = fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if basename in filename_lookup and filename_lookup[basename] != fname:
            ambiguous_basenames.add(basename)
        else:
            filename_lookup[basename] = fname

    # Remove ambiguous basenames (same name in different dirs)
    for ab in ambiguous_basenames:
        filename_lookup.pop(ab, None)
The first phase builds an index mapping both fully qualified relative filenames (e.g., services/auth.py.md) and plain basenames (e.g., auth.py.md) to canonical filenames. To guard against incorrect path rewrites in monorepos or multi-tiered directories containing identical filenames across distinct folders (e.g., api/v1/user.py.md vs. api/v2/user.py.md), collisions are tracked inside ambiguous_basenames. Any basename detected in more than one distinct subpath is permanently removed from the lookup table, requiring subsequent matches to resolve against fully qualified paths.

docs.title: Phase 2: Regex Matching and Relative Target Resolution
docs.text:
link_pattern = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)")
    fixed_count = 0

    for cf in chapter_files:
        current_dir = os.path.dirname(cf["filename"])  # e.g. "CoreService"

        def fix_link(match, _dir=current_dir):
            nonlocal fixed_count
            text, target, anchor = match.group(1), match.group(2), match.group(3) or ""
            if target.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                return match.group(0)
            # Try resolving the target as-is (LLM copied verbatim from index)
            canonical = filename_lookup.get(target)
            if not canonical:
                # Try resolving relative to current dir
                resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(_dir, target)).replace("\\", "/")
                canonical = filename_lookup.get(resolved)
            if canonical:
                correct_rel = os.path.relpath(canonical, _dir).replace("\\", "/") if _dir else canonical
                if correct_rel != target:
                    fixed_count += 1
                return f"[{text}]({correct_rel}{anchor})"
            return match.group(0)  # Unknown target — leave as-is

        cf["content"] = link_pattern.sub(fix_link, cf["content"])

    if fixed_count:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LINK NORMALIZATION | fixed {fixed_count} cross-chapter links", dest="LOG")
The second phase iterates through each chapter file, determining its enclosing directory via os.path.dirname(cf["filename"]). It compiles a regular expression r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)" to capture link text, .md link targets, and optional anchor tags. An inline closure, fix_link, bypasses HTTP/HTTPS URIs, resolves targets either directly or against current_dir via os.path.normpath, recalculates the relative traversal path using os.path.relpath, and normalizes path separators to forward slashes (/). If a target matches a canonical path and differs from the source link, the replacement is applied and the fix counter is incremented.

docs.title: write_mkdocs_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def write_mkdocs_output(output_path: str, prep_res: dict, chapter_files: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: The primary orchestration driver for exporting generated documentation into an MkDocs static site structure. It handles automated LLM navigation grouping (for API reference modes with large module counts), synthesizes mkdocs.yml, writes client-side Mermaid initialization assets, builds landing pages (docs/index.md and docs/api/index.md), persists navigation snippets, normalizes cross-document hyperlinks, and writes chapter Markdown files into disk subdirectories.

Parameters: * output_path (str): Base filesystem path where the documentation project is emitted. * prep_res (dict): Intermediate pipeline context dictionary containing mode flags, site configuration, project names, and raw navigation definitions. * chapter_files (list[dict]): List of generated chapter file structures containing module names, descriptions, filenames, and markdown content.

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Setup and Site Title Resolution
docs.text:
project_name = prep_res["project_name"]
    mode = prep_res["mode"]
    api_docs_path = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "api")
    os.makedirs(api_docs_path, exist_ok=True)

    mode_labels = {
        "tutorial": get("UI_MODE_TUTORIAL"),
        "advanced": get("UI_MODE_ADVANCED"),
        "sdk": get("UI_MODE_SDK"),
        "api-reference": get("UI_MODE_API_REF"),
    }
    site_title = f"{project_name} — {mode_labels.get(mode, 'Documentation')}"
    emit("COMBINE_FORMAT_MKDOCS", mode=mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation"))
    emit("COMBINE_CHAPTER_COUNT", count=len(chapter_files))
Initialization resolves localized mode labels (Tutorial, Advanced, SDK, or API Reference) through get(). It ensures the destination folder docs/api exists on disk via os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True) and emits UI events logging chapter counts and generation formats.

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM-Assisted Navigation Grouping
docs.text:
# --- LLM-Assisted Nav Grouping (api-reference only, 6+ modules) ---
    sections = None
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NAV GROUPING CHECK | mode={mode} | module_count={len(chapter_files)} | threshold=6", dest="LOG")
    if mode == "api-reference" and len(chapter_files) > 5:
        try:
            chapter_summaries = prep_res.get("chapter_summaries", [])
            module_entries = []
            for i, cf in enumerate(chapter_files):
                summary = chapter_summaries[i] if i < len(chapter_summaries) and chapter_summaries[i] else cf["description"]
                module_entries.append(f"- {cf['module_name']}: {summary}")
            module_list = "\n".join(module_entries)

            # Load grouping prompt template
            prompt_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", "common", "group_modules.md")
            with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                group_template = f.read()

            language = prep_res.get("language", "english")
            language_note = f"Section names MUST be in {language}." if language.lower() != "english" else ""

            group_prompt = group_template.format(
                project_name=project_name,
                module_count=len(chapter_files),
                module_list=module_list,
                directory_tree=prep_res.get("directory_tree", "N/A"),
                language_note=language_note,
            )

            emit("LLM_CALL_GROUPING", count=len(chapter_files))

            log_token_estimation("NavGrouping", group_prompt, prep_res.get("max_tokens", 100000))
            group_response = call_llm(group_prompt, use_cache=prep_res.get("use_cache", True), thinking_level=prep_res.get("thinking_level"))
            parsed = parse_yaml_response(group_response)
            sections = parsed.get("sections", parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None

            if sections:
                # Validate: ensure all modules are covered
                grouped_modules = collect_all_modules(sections)
                ungrouped = [cf["module_name"] for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] not in grouped_modules]
                if ungrouped:
                    sections.append({"name": get("UI_OTHER"), "modules": ungrouped})

                nav_lines = build_grouped_nav(sections, chapter_files, indent=4)
                nav_lines.insert(0, "    - api/index.md")
                nav_label = mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation")
                nav_snippet = f"nav:\n  - {nav_label}:\n" + "\n".join(nav_lines)
                emit("DONE_GROUPING", count=len(sections))
            else:
                emit("GROUP_EMPTY_FALLBACK")
                nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]

        except Exception as e:
            emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK", error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"LLM grouping failed: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
            sections = None
    else:
        nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
When running in api-reference mode with more than 5 modules, flat navigation becomes unwieldy. The system constructs an LLM prompt injecting module summaries and directory structures from prompts/common/group_modules.md. The model response is parsed via parse_yaml_response. A completeness check ensures no modules were dropped: any unassigned modules are collected into an Other (UI_OTHER) section. If parsing fails, exceptions are caught and the pipeline falls back to prep_res["nav_snippet"].

docs.title: write_standalone_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def write_standalone_output(output_path: str, prep_res: dict, chapter_files: list[dict], ui: dict) -> None:

Description: Emits generated documentation in standalone (non-MkDocs) format. This creates individual Markdown files in the output directory, outputs a top-level index.md, and compiles an all-in-one full_content.md file containing an anchored table of contents linked to every chapter for offline reading and monolithic viewing.

Parameters: * output_path (str): Target output directory. * prep_res (dict): Context dictionary containing index_content. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Collection of synthesized chapter records. * ui (dict): Localized UI label mapping containing at least "toc" and "chapter".

Example: 

# Standalone mode export invoked from CombineTutorial
write_standalone_output(
    output_path=output_dir,
    prep_res=preparation_state,
    chapter_files=chapters,
    ui={"toc": "Table of Contents", "chapter": "Chapter"}
)


def write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui):
    """Write standalone (non-MkDocs) output: index.md, chapters, full_content.md."""
    index_content = prep_res["index_content"]
    emit("COMBINE_FORMAT_STANDALONE")
    emit("COMBINE_CHAPTER_COUNT", count=len(chapter_files))

    # Write index.md
    index_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "index.md")
    with open(index_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(index_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=index_filepath)

    # Write chapter files
    for chapter_info in chapter_files:
        chapter_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, chapter_info["filename"])
        with open(chapter_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(chapter_info["content"])
        emit("FILE_WROTE", path=chapter_filepath)

    # Create full_content.md
    toc_lines = [f"# {ui['toc']}\n"]
    full_content_lines = []

    for i, chapter_info in enumerate(chapter_files):
        content = chapter_info["content"]
        title_line = content.split("\n", 1)[0]
        if title_line.startswith("# "):
            title = title_line[2:].strip()
        else:
            title = f"{ui['chapter']} {i + 1}"

        toc_lines.append(f"- [{title}](#chapter-{i + 1})")
        full_content_lines.append(f'<a id="chapter-{i + 1}"></a>\n')
        full_content_lines.append(content)
        full_content_lines.append("\n---\n")

    full_content = "\n".join(toc_lines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(full_content_lines)
    full_content_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "full_content.md")
    with open(full_content_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(full_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=full_content_filepath)
The function extracts the pre-built index_content from prep_res and writes it to index.md. It then writes each chapter file to output_path. Finally, it constructs full_content.md by parsing the first line of each chapter to extract its # title (falling back to a generic numbered title if missing), creating a table of contents list with Markdown anchor links, and concatenating all chapters separated by <a id="chapter-N"></a> anchors and horizontal divider rules (---).

docs.title: build_grouped_nav()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def build_grouped_nav(sections: list[dict], chapter_files: list[dict], indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:

Description: Recursively constructs lines of YAML navigation entries based on an LLM-derived hierarchical section tree. It handles arbitrary nesting depth through the children key. Within each leaf section, modules are matched against chapter_files by module_name. Modules residing in subdirectories are auto-sub-grouped by directory path without extra LLM calls, while root files remain flat.

Parameters: * sections (list[dict]): Hierarchical tree of section dictionaries. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Available chapter records to match against. * indent (int): Indentation spaces to prepend to YAML lines (defaults to 4).

Returns: * list[str]: Indented YAML lines representing the navigation tree.

def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"build_grouped_nav | building nav for {len(sections)} sections", dest="LOG")

    lines = []
    pad = " " * indent
    for section in sections:
        lines.append(f"{pad}- {yaml_str(section['name'])}:")
        if "children" in section:
            lines.extend(build_grouped_nav(section["children"], chapter_files, indent + 2))

        # Collect matched modules with directory info
        matched = []
        for mod_name in section.get("modules", []):
            match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
            if match:
                dir_path = os.path.dirname(match.get("original_path", "")) or ""
                matched.append((dir_path, mod_name, match))

        # Group by directory
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for dir_path, mod_name, match in matched:
            dir_groups[dir_path].append((mod_name, match))

        # Emit dir sub-layers for non-root dirs, flat for root files
        has_non_root = any(d for d in dir_groups)
        if has_non_root:
            for dir_path in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
                if dir_path:
                    # Non-root: add directory sub-layer with bare module names
                    lines.append(f"{pad}  - {yaml_str(dir_path)}:")
                    for mod_name, match in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        lines.append(f"{pad}    - {yaml_str(mod_name)}: {yaml_str('api/' + match['filename'])}")
                else:
                    # Root files: flat (no sub-layer)
                    for mod_name, match in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        lines.append(f"{pad}  - {yaml_str(mod_name)}: {yaml_str('api/' + match['filename'])}")
        else:
            # All root files → flat list
            for _dir_path, mod_name, match in matched:
                lines.append(f"{pad}  - {yaml_str(mod_name)}: {yaml_str('api/' + match['filename'])}")

    return lines
The helper formats indentation using pad = " " * indent and recursively processes nested sub-sections by passing indent + 2. It resolves module paths via defaultdict(list), checking if any module belongs to a non-root folder. If subdirectories are present, it injects a directory subsection header (- "dir_path":) with indented leaf entries pointing to api/{filename}. If all modules are top-level, it emits a flat list of module links.

docs.title: collect_all_modules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def collect_all_modules(sections: list[dict]) -> set[str]:

Description: Recursively traverses a hierarchical section tree, collecting every referenced module name into a flat Python set. This provides $O(1)$ membership testing to verify whether an LLM navigation plan has omitted any generated documentation chapters.

Parameters: * sections (list[dict]): The section tree structure containing modules lists and optional children lists.

Returns: * set[str]: Set of all unique module names present across the tree.

def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:
    """Recursively collect all module names referenced in a sections tree."""
    result = set()
    for section in sections:
        result.update(section.get("modules", []))
        if "children" in section:
            result.update(collect_all_modules(section["children"]))
    return result
The function initializes an empty set result and iterates over each section node. It performs an in-place update with section.get("modules", []), checks for the existence of children, and recursively invokes itself to traverse child branches. The consolidated set is returned to the caller to identify missing chapters.

docs.title: build_index_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def build_index_sections(lines: list[str], sections: list[dict], chapter_files: list[dict], level: int = 3) -> None:

Description: Recursively constructs the Markdown text of the index landing page (docs/api/index.md) from the section tree. For each section, it emits a Markdown heading scaled to the nesting depth ("#" * level), followed by a two-column Markdown table listing chapters and their descriptions.

Parameters: * lines (list[str]): Mutable accumulator list where Markdown lines are appended. * sections (list[dict]): Hierarchical tree of section definitions. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Collection of chapter objects for resolving metadata. * level (int): Markdown heading level for section titles (defaults to 3, e.g. ###).

def build_index_sections(lines, sections, chapter_files, level=3):
    """Recursively build index.md sections with module tables."""
    heading = "#" * level
    for section in sections:
        lines.append(f"{heading} {section['name']}")
        lines.append("")
        if section.get("modules"):
            lines.append(f"| {get('UI_TH_CHAPTER')} | {get('UI_TH_DESCRIPTION')} |")
            lines.append("|---------|-------------|")
            for mod_name in section["modules"]:
                match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
                if match:
                    display = mod_name
                    # Use description, but if it's the generic mapper description, extract from content
                    desc = match["description"]
                    if desc.startswith("Internal API reference"):
                        content_lines = match["content"].strip().split("\n")
                        for cl in content_lines:
                            cs = cl.strip()
                            if cs and not cs.startswith(("---", "#", "```", "title:", "sidebar_position:")):
                                desc = cs[:120]
                                break
                    lines.append(f"| [{display}]({match['filename']}) | {desc} |")
            lines.append("")
        for child in section.get("children", []):
            build_index_sections(lines, [child], chapter_files, level + 1)
For each module in a section, this helper resolves its display entry and description. If the description is a placeholder starting with "Internal API reference", it parses the module's actual markdown content, finds the first non-header, non-frontmatter, non-fence text line, and extracts the first 120 characters as an excerpt. It then recurses through section.get("children", []), incrementing level + 1 to maintain header hierarchy in Markdown.

docs.title: LLM Grouping Failures and Graceful Degradation
docs.text:
The automated grouping phase in write_mkdocs_output encapsulates network and parsing operations in an isolated try...except Exception block:

except Exception as e:
    emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK", error=e)
    emit_raw("ERROR", f"LLM grouping failed: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
    nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
    sections = None
If the LLM call times out, encounters rate limits, refuses the prompt, or outputs malformed YAML that fails in parse_yaml_response, the system captures the full exception traceback to diagnostics via emit_raw. It then emits a UI event (GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK), resets sections = None, and falls back to prep_res["nav_snippet"].

docs.title: Ambiguous Cross-Chapter Link Resolution
docs.text:
When normalizing cross-chapter links in normalize_chapter_links(), files in different directories may share the same basename (such as models.py.md in different services). The resolution engine detects collisions early:

basename = fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
if basename in filename_lookup and filename_lookup[basename] != fname:
    ambiguous_basenames.add(basename)
else:
    filename_lookup[basename] = fname

# Remove ambiguous basenames (same name in different dirs)
for ab in ambiguous_basenames:
    filename_lookup.pop(ab, None)
By removing colliding basenames from filename_lookup, ambiguous links are left unchanged rather than misdirected to arbitrary chapters.

docs.title: Defensive Filesystem and Asset Creation
docs.text:
All filesystem operations apply os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True) immediately before writing files, ensuring parent directories are created safely even in deep multi-directory configurations:

chapter_filepath = os.path.join(api_docs_path, chapter_info["filename"])
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(chapter_filepath), exist_ok=True)
with open(chapter_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(chapter_info["content"])

docs.title: output.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/output.py

Following the static-site generation and artifact serialization services documented in utils/mkdocs.py, the utils/output.py module provides the foundational telemetry, console formatting, and logging infrastructure utilized across the entire project. While mkdocs.py converts processed abstractions into persistent web documentation, output.py drives the interactive user experience, diagnostic logging, and localized CLI messaging for every stage of pipeline execution.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The output.py module acts as the centralized console presentation and filesystem logging subsystem for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder engine. It provides a structured mechanism to emit operational updates, warnings, errors, progress indicators, and debug traces across standard output (sys.stdout) and persistent run-specific log files. Terminal output is stylized using standard ANSI escape sequences mapped to semantic logging levels (PROGRESS, SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR, INFO, DEBUG, and FILE_WRITE).

A core architectural capability of the module is its dynamic internationalization (i18n) layer. Instead of hardcoding user-facing strings into pipeline routines, message templates are maintained in an external comma-separated values database (utils/strings.csv). Upon initialization, output.py loads strings for the requested target language, falling back gracefully to English if specific translations are absent. When untranslated keys are encountered in non-English execution modes, the module interfaces with utils/i18n.py to trigger automated LLM translations and persist the updated catalog back to disk.

The module also handles cross-platform stream encoding issues. On non-interactive or redirected Windows environments (such as CI/CD runners or background processes), standard output and error streams frequently default to legacy ANSI code pages (e.g., cp1252), resulting in UnicodeEncodeError exceptions when rendering multi-byte UTF-8 character sets. output.py proactively detects non-TTY streams and reconfigures them to standard UTF-8 with character replacement fallback strategies.

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def init(language: str = "english", use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None, debug: bool = False, auto_translate: bool = True) -> None

Description: Initializes the runtime state of the output subsystem. This method configures target language resolution, establishes the path to the localized string catalog (strings.csv), configures stream encodings for redirected execution environments, and loads all available message templates into the in-memory string registry. If auto_translate is enabled and missing translations are detected for a non-English language target, it automatically triggers translation synchronization via _auto_translate().

Parameters: * language (str): Target language name for CLI strings (e.g., "Vietnamese", "english"). Defaults to "english". * use_cache (bool): Determines whether LLM response caching is enabled during translation invocations. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None): Reasoning effort level passed to underlying LLM translation requests. Defaults to None. * debug (bool): Enables verbose console diagnostics and un-suppresses DEBUG-level output. Defaults to False. * auto_translate (bool): Flag controlling whether to invoke automated LLM string translation immediately. Upstream orchestrators like main() pass False to defer translation until credentials and preflights have completed. Defaults to True.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly; unhandled file system errors when accessing strings.csv are guarded internally.

Example: 

# Real initialization pattern from utils/output.py docstring:
init(
    language="english",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level=None,
    debug=False,
    auto_translate=True,
)

Implementation logic: 

def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):
    global _language, _lang_col, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level, _debug
    _language = language.capitalize()
    _lang_col = language.lower()
    _csv_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "strings.csv")
    _use_cache = use_cache
    _thinking_level = thinking_level
    _debug = debug
    _ensure_utf8_streams()
    _load_strings()
    if auto_translate:
        _auto_translate()
The initialization function mutates module-level configuration variables and establishes absolute paths relative to the current file location to ensure deterministic resolution regardless of the current working directory. It invokes _ensure_utf8_streams() prior to any file parsing to guarantee that console error emission mechanisms are stable. Once the catalog is populated via _load_strings(), it conditionally evaluates the auto_translate flag, delegating to the translation bridge if enabled.

docs.title: translate_missing_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def translate_missing_strings() -> None

Description: Performs on-demand translation of missing localization entries for the active target language. This function acts as a public decoupling hook designed for pipeline startup sequences where init(auto_translate=False) is executed prior to environment validation. Once authentication preflight checks (e.g., API key validation in utils/llm_config.py) confirm network and service readiness, translate_missing_strings() can be invoked safely without risking premature authentication crashes.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly; failures during downstream LLM translation are trapped within utils.i18n.

Example: 

# Invoked after authentication preflight succeeds:
translate_missing_strings()

Implementation logic: 

def translate_missing_strings():
    """Auto-translate strings missing for the configured language (LLM call); see init(auto_translate=False)."""
    _auto_translate()
This method delegates directly to the private helper _auto_translate(). It isolates external consumers from internal synchronization logic, maintaining clean separation between application configuration and network-backed internationalization routines.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit(key: str, suffix: str = "", **kwargs: object) -> None

Description: Emits a localized, template-driven message to configured output sinks (standard output, disk log file, or both). The function queries the loaded string registry using the provided key. If found, it interpolates dynamic variables supplied in kwargs, appends any optional suffix, applies ANSI color coding according to the entry's severity level, and routes the message according to its destination policy. If the key is not present in the catalog, a fallback notification is printed to standard output to prevent silent telemetry loss.

Parameters: * key (str): Symbolic identifier defined in utils/strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER"). * suffix (str): Optional plain text string appended to the formatted template output (e.g., token usage breakdowns). Defaults to "". * **kwargs (object): Arbitrary keyword arguments used for variable substitution within {placeholder} tokens in the template.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised; formatting errors and missing keys are handled gracefully.

Example: 

# Real usage from utils/output.py docstring:
emit("LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", chapter_num=1, name="flow")

Implementation logic: 

def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        # Fallback for unknown keys — print raw so nothing is silently lost
        print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
        return

    text = _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
    if suffix:
        text = text + suffix

    level = entry["level"]
    dest = entry["dest"]

    # D-prefixed destinations (DBOTH, DSTDOUT): debug-gated console output.
    # Without --debug, suppress console but always log. Preserves original color from LEVEL.
    if dest.startswith("D"):
        if _debug:
            dest = dest[1:]  # DBOTH → BOTH, DSTDOUT → STDOUT
        else:
            dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)
The dispatch mechanism evaluates whether the resolved destination incorporates a debug gate (prefixed with "D", such as "DBOTH" or "DSTDOUT"). When running without the --debug flag active, these destinations are rewritten to "LOG", suppressing terminal chatter while guaranteeing complete audit traces on disk. If the message destination includes terminal targets ("BOTH" or "STDOUT"), standard ANSI color prefixes and reset terminators are wrapped around the text before passing to Python's built-in print.

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit_raw(level: str, text: str, dest: str = "BOTH") -> None

Description: Renders and logs dynamic or structural text directly without consulting the localization catalog. This is the primary output function for un-templated content generated at runtime, such as file tree visualizations, markdown diffs, batch processing summaries, and horizontal dividing rules. It formats the output with appropriate ANSI color codes corresponding to the specified level and directs output to the selected destination sinks.

Parameters: * level (str): Severity or semantic styling identifier (e.g., "PROGRESS", "SUCCESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG"). * text (str): Pre-formatted string payload to output. * dest (str): Output target routing specifier. Accepts "BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG". Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Real usage from utils/output.py docstring:
emit_raw("WARNING", "Custom message")

Implementation logic: 

def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):
    # DEBUG-level: suppress console unless --debug is active
    if level == "DEBUG" and not _debug:
        dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)
emit_raw enforces an explicit safeguard for DEBUG-level records: if --debug is not enabled in the runtime configuration, the destination is automatically coerced to "LOG". Color styling is resolved dynamically via dictionary lookup against COLORS. If the resolved color string is non-empty, a trailing ANSI reset sequence (\033[0m) is appended to prevent terminal color leakage.

docs.title: is_debug()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def is_debug() -> bool

Description: Queries the active debug status configured during subsystem initialization. External modules use this predicate function to conditionally gate expensive string constructions, detailed abstract syntax tree dumps, or verbose telemetry operations.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * bool: True if the subsystem was initialized with debug=True, otherwise False.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Gating verbose diagnostic reporting:
if is_debug():
    emit_raw("DEBUG", "Tracing internal state...")

Implementation logic: 

def is_debug():
    """Return True when --debug is active (used to gate verbose diagnostics outside this module)."""
    return _debug
The method returns the boolean state of the module-scoped _debug variable. Because this flag is populated during init(), external callers can inspect CLI verbosity settings without directly accessing or modifying private module variables.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get(key: str, **kwargs: object) -> str

Description: Retrieves a translated, variable-interpolated string from the catalog without writing to standard output or the persistent log file. This method is used to obtain localized UI text, table headings, and section titles embedded directly into generated documentation files (such as index.md navigation headers generated by utils/mkdocs.py).

Parameters: * key (str): Symbolic identifier defined in strings.csv (e.g., "UI_TUTORIAL"). * **kwargs (object): Named parameters for template variable substitution.

Returns: * str: The translated text with interpolated keyword arguments. If the key is not found in the catalog, the raw key string is returned as a defensive fallback.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Real usage from utils/output.py docstring:
label = get("UI_TUTORIAL")

Implementation logic: 

def get(key, **kwargs):
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        return key  # Fallback: return the key itself
    return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
The retrieval routine performs an $O(1)$ dictionary lookup against the _strings catalog. If the requested key exists, it delegates formatting to _format_safe to substitute dynamic keyword parameters while guarding against interpolation syntax exceptions. If the key is absent, it returns the bare key string, ensuring downstream document builders can render placeholder content without crashing.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name: str = "project", mode: str = "tutorial") -> str

Description: Configures and initializes disk-based audit logging for the current pipeline run. The function ensures the target log directory exists, sanitizes the project and mode identifiers to create safe filenames, closes any previously active log file handle, and creates a timestamped log file. It also writes standard execution metadata headers into the log file.

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name of the repository or project under analysis. Defaults to "project". * mode (str): Active operational mode of the pipeline (e.g., "tutorial", "api-reference"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or normalized relative path to the newly opened log file (e.g., "logs/my_project_tutorial_20250101_120000.log").

Raises: * OSError: If the directory specified by LOG_DIR cannot be created or file creation fails due to filesystem permissions.

Example: 

# Configuring logging in main.py startup:
log_path = configure_logging(project_name="Codebase-Knowledge-Builder", mode="tutorial")

Implementation logic: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    global _log_file

    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_path = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Close any existing log file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()

    _log_file = open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8")  # noqa: SIM115

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    sep = "=" * 80
    emit_raw("INFO", sep, dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"Log file: {log_path}", dest="LOG")

    return log_path
Filename generation sanitizes input strings by replacing any non-alphanumeric character (excluding hyphens, underscores, and dots) with an underscore. The log stream is opened in append mode with explicit UTF-8 encoding. Immediately following initialization, standard audit metadata—including run mode, project name, timestamp, and delimiter bars—is written directly to the file stream via emit_raw(..., dest="LOG").

docs.title: shutdown()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def shutdown() -> None

Description: Flushes and cleanly closes the active log file handle, releasing operating system resources. This function should be called within a finally block at the entry point of the application (main.py) to guarantee that all pending disk buffers are flushed even if an unhandled exception terminates the pipeline.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Teardown handling in main entry point:
try:
    pass  # Pipeline execution
finally:
    shutdown()

Implementation logic: 

def shutdown():
    global _log_file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()
        _log_file = None
The routine verifies that _log_file is not None before invoking .close(). It subsequently resets _log_file to None, ensuring that subsequent calls to _write_log gracefully degrade to no-ops rather than raising errors on a closed file handle.

docs.title: _write_log()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _write_log(level: str, text: str) -> None

Description: Formats and writes a timestamped record to the active disk log file. If file-based logging has not been initialized via configure_logging(), the operation silently terminates without error. Written lines are formatted with microsecond precision truncated to milliseconds and flushed immediately to prevent buffer loss during system crashes.

Parameters: * level (str): Semantic severity string associated with the log record. * text (str): Formatted log message payload.

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If writing to the file descriptor fails at the operating system level.

Example: 

# Internal call site within emit():
_write_log(level, text)

Implementation logic: 

def _write_log(level, text):
    if _log_file is None:
        return

    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f")[:-3]
    _log_file.write(f"{ts} - {level} - {text}\n")
    _log_file.flush()
Timestamps are formatted according to the standard ISO-like structure YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm by slicing the last three characters off the microsecond string. Calling _log_file.flush() after every write operation guarantees that log entries are synchronized to the underlying storage device immediately, protecting execution traces against sudden process termination.

docs.title: _ensure_utf8_streams()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _ensure_utf8_streams() -> None

Description: Inspects standard output (sys.stdout) and standard error (sys.stderr) streams to identify non-UTF-8 encodings when running in non-interactive (piped or redirected) environments. On operating systems such as Windows, redirected streams often default to legacy code pages (e.g., cp1252), which fail to encode localized text (such as Vietnamese or CJK characters) and raise UnicodeEncodeError. This function reconfigures active streams to use UTF-8 with character replacement on failure.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Invoked internally during subsystem startup:
_ensure_utf8_streams()

Implementation logic: 

def _ensure_utf8_streams():
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        encoding = (getattr(stream, "encoding", "") or "").lower().replace("-", "")
        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure") and encoding != "utf8" and not stream.isatty():
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
The routine loops over both standard output and error descriptors. It normalizes the reported stream encoding string by stripping hyphens and converting to lowercase. If Python's stream reconfiguration interface (reconfigure) is supported, the stream encoding is not already UTF-8, and isatty() evaluates to False (indicating redirected output), it calls stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") to prevent runtime encoding failures.

docs.title: _format_safe()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _format_safe(template: str, kwargs: dict) -> str

Description: Applies standard Python string interpolation (template.format(**kwargs)) within an exception guard. If the template contains malformed format tokens, references positional indices that are missing, or encounters key errors during dictionary lookup, the function traps the error and returns the unformatted template verbatim.

Parameters: * template (str): Target string template containing {placeholder} tokens. * kwargs (dict): Keyword argument dictionary containing replacement values.

Returns: * str: Interpolated string result, or the raw template if substitution fails.

Raises: * No exceptions raised; KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError are intercepted.

Example: 

# Internal call site from get():
return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)

Implementation logic: 

def _format_safe(template, kwargs):
    try:
        return template.format(**kwargs)
    except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return template
This defensive helper protects logging execution paths from crashing when dynamic parameter dictionaries do not align with catalog templates. This situation can occur if upstream code passes an unexpected keyword argument set or an automated LLM translation inadvertently alters variable token syntax (e.g., mutating {path} to {file_path}).

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings() -> None

Description: Parses utils/strings.csv using csv.DictReader and populates the in-memory string catalog _strings. The parser strips whitespace, skips comments (lines starting with #) and empty keys, and resolves the target language string with fallback to English. It also tracks the total count of loaded keys versus translated keys for localization diagnostics.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If the CSV file cannot be opened due to filesystem permission constraints.

Example: 

# Invoked internally during init() and after auto-translation:
_load_strings()

Implementation logic: 

def _load_strings():
    global _strings
    _strings = {}

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    translated_count = 0
    total_count = 0

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue

            level = row.get("LEVEL", "INFO").strip()
            dest = row.get("DEST", "BOTH").strip()

            # Priority: language column → English fallback
            text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip()
            if text:
                translated_count += 1
            else:
                text = row.get("english", "").strip()

            total_count += 1
            _strings[key] = {"text": text, "level": level, "dest": dest}

    if _lang_col != "english" and translated_count == total_count:
        emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] {_language} — loaded {translated_count} strings from CSV")
The routine opens the CSV catalog utilizing utf-8-sig encoding, ensuring that Byte Order Marks (BOM) inserted by external editing tools (such as Microsoft Excel) are stripped cleanly. For each row, the helper resolves the active message string by first inspecting the configured language column (_lang_col); if empty, it falls back to the baseline "english" column. When a non-English catalog is completely translated, a success notification is emitted to standard output.

docs.title: _auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _auto_translate() -> None

Description: Triggers automated translation of untranslated string keys by delegating to utils.i18n.auto_translate. If auto_translate returns True (indicating that new translations were fetched via LLM inference and written to the CSV file on disk), this function invokes _load_strings() to refresh the in-memory catalog with the updated strings.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * Exceptions raised during remote inference or disk writes are caught and handled within the utils.i18n module.

Example: 

# Internal call site within translate_missing_strings():
_auto_translate()

Implementation logic: 

def _auto_translate():
    from utils.i18n import auto_translate

    if auto_translate(_lang_col, _language, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level):
        # Reload strings from the updated CSV so all translations are active
        _load_strings()
The helper uses a deferred import pattern (from utils.i18n import auto_translate) inside the function body. This prevents circular module dependencies between output.py and the LLM inference ecosystem (utils.call_llm $\rightarrow$ utils.output $\rightarrow$ utils.i18n). If new translations are committed to the file, _load_strings() is called immediately to synchronize the in-memory registry.

docs.title: ANSI Color Palette (COLORS)
docs.text:
The module maintains a mapping of semantic message classifications to terminal ANSI escape sequences.

Level Identifier Escape Sequence Target Display Color Semantic Usage Context "PROGRESS" "\033[96m" Cyan LLM API requests, active processing steps "SUCCESS" "\033[92m" Green Step completions, cache hits, successful exports "WARNING" "\033[93m" Yellow Rate warnings, truncation events, non-fatal errors "ERROR" "\033[91m" Red Execution failures, critical model refusals "INFO" "" Default Terminal Color Configuration parameters, file counts, standard labels "DEBUG" "\033[90m" Gray Skipped files, diagnostic token dumps "FILE_WRITE" "" Default Terminal Color File generation confirmations (- Wrote {path}) "UI" "" Default Terminal Color Reserved for markdown documentation rendering

docs.title: In-Memory String Entry (_strings Value Schema)
docs.text:
When strings.csv is parsed, each valid record is stored in the _strings dictionary using its STRING_KEY as the lookup key.

Field Name Type Description text str Message template string with optional {placeholder} tokens for parameter interpolation. level str Semantic severity identifier mapping into COLORS (e.g., "PROGRESS", "INFO"). dest str Routing sink specifier: "BOTH", "STDOUT", "LOG", "DBOTH", or "DSTDOUT". 
# Sample in-memory catalog entry:
{
    "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER": {
        "text": "[LLM] Writing Chapter {chapter_num}: {name}...",
        "level": "PROGRESS",
        "dest": "BOTH",
    }
}

docs.title: Localization File Schema (strings.csv)
docs.text:
The tabular CSV structure maintained on disk defining system-wide localized strings.

Column Header Required Description STRING_KEY Yes Unique string identifier (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", "UI_TUTORIAL"). Lines starting with # are ignored as comments. LEVEL Yes Semantic logging level specifying the ANSI color mapping (INFO, PROGRESS, WARNING, ERROR, DEBUG, FILE_WRITE, UI). DEST Yes Output destination routing (BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, DBOTH, DSTDOUT). english Yes Baseline canonical English translation and formatting template. <lang_col> No Dynamic columns representing additional target languages (e.g., vietnamese, japanese).

docs.title: Module Runtime State
docs.text:
The internal runtime configuration state maintained across the lifecycle of the process.

Variable Name Type Initial Value Description _strings dict[str, dict[str, str]] {} In-memory lookup registry mapping string keys to their configuration schemas. _language str "English" Display-formatted target language name (e.g., "Vietnamese"). _lang_col str "english" Lowercase column header name matching target languages in strings.csv. _log_file TextIOWrapper \| None None Active file descriptor for writing continuous disk logs. _csv_path str \| None None Absolute filesystem path resolving to utils/strings.csv. _use_cache bool True Determines if LLM translation calls should utilize persistent inference caches. _thinking_level str \| None None Reasoning effort budget allocated for automated translation inference. _debug bool False Global verbosity flag controlling DEBUG level and D* destination visibility.

docs.title: Persistent Disk Log Format
docs.text:
Disk log files generated by configure_logging() format output records as timestamped entries:

Segment Format Description Timestamp YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm Wall-clock execution time with millisecond precision. Level STRING The semantic level identifier associated with the message. Message STRING The plain text message payload (ANSI color codes are excluded). 
2025-05-18 14:32:01,102 - INFO - ================================================================================
2025-05-18 14:32:01,103 - INFO - RUN STARTED | project=knowledge_builder | mode=tutorial | timestamp=20250518_143201
2025-05-18 14:32:01,103 - INFO - Log file: logs/knowledge_builder_tutorial_20250518_143201.log
2025-05-18 14:32:02,450 - PROGRESS - [LLM] Writing Chapter 1: Architecture Overview...

docs.title: String Formatting Fault Isolation
docs.text: Variable substitution in user-facing strings is handled through _format_safe(). If a template defines invalid format tokens, references positional indices that are missing, or encounters mismatched dictionary keys, the resulting KeyError, IndexError, or ValueError is caught. Instead of propagating an unhandled exception that would crash an in-flight documentation build, _format_safe() returns the raw template string.

docs.title: Missing Catalog Keys
docs.text: If an emit(key) call requests a key that does not exist in strings.csv, output.py avoids raising a KeyError. It prints [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] directly to sys.stdout. Similarly, get(key) returns the raw key string. This approach ensures missing translation keys do not abort execution while surfacing clear visual notices to developers.

docs.title: Non-Interactive Windows Encoding Safeguards
docs.text: On Windows environments, non-TTY redirected streams (e.g., standard output redirected to a file or piped to another process) default to legacy ANSI code pages (such as Windows-1252). Emitting multi-byte UTF-8 characters under these conditions raises a terminal UnicodeEncodeError. _ensure_utf8_streams() detects non-TTY streams and reconfigures them using stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"). This ensures Unicode characters can be output safely, replacing un-encodable bytes with replacement characters rather than terminating the process.

docs.title: File Handle Lifecycle and Teardown
docs.text: To prevent file descriptor leaks and lost disk writes, configure_logging() explicitly closes any previously active log handle before opening a new one. The shutdown() function is designed to be invoked within finally blocks at the entry point of the application (main.py), ensuring that buffered output lines are flushed to disk even in the event of unexpected pipeline terminations.

  • utils/crawl_github_files.py — Ingestion crawler using output.py to stream remote download status and crawl metrics.
  • utils/crawl_local_files.py — Local directory traversal engine reporting ignored files and read progress via emit().
  • main.py — Primary application orchestrator managing the lifecycle of init(), configure_logging(), and shutdown().

docs.title: prompts.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/prompts.py

Following the console logging, terminal styling, and localized string management provided by output.py, the prompts.py module encapsulates prompt loading, inline prompt generation, and model response extraction. It decouples the synthesis pipeline's prompt lifecycle from model invocation drivers, providing unified filesystem loaders for Markdown prompt templates and robust parsing routines for model-generated YAML data structures and file indices.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The prompts.py module provides centralized prompt construction and response parsing utilities across the repository documentation pipeline. Upstream workflow graph nodes in nodes.py require structured communication with Large Language Models (LLMs) across multiple operational modes, including tutorial, advanced, api-reference, and sdk. This module abstracts prompt template locations on disk, ensures safe UTF-8 file reading with Byte Order Mark handling, dynamically generates specialized inline prompts, and extracts structured data from LLM text completions.

A critical design requirement of the response parsing layer is defense against silent failure modes caused by LLM output truncation. When model completions hit max token ceilings, partial YAML blocks can sometimes be parsed as incomplete data structures (such as truncated lists or dictionaries), leading to silently dropped files or corrupted chapter structures. The module prevents this by validating response objects for truncation sentinels (such as TruncatedResponse defined in llm_common.py) prior to YAML parsing, failing fast with explicit exceptions that prompt workflow nodes to retry.

docs.title: parse_file_index()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_file_index(idx_value) -> int | None:

Description: Extracts the first continuous sequence of numeric digits from an LLM-generated file index representation and converts it into an integer. LLM outputs referencing file indices frequently deviate from strict numeric formats, producing annotated strings such as "3 # path/to/file.py", range indicators such as "0-3", or standard integers. This function applies a regular expression match to isolate the leading integer value, returning None if no numeric characters exist.

Parameters: * idx_value (Any): The raw input representation from the LLM, which can be an integer, string, or mixed object.

Returns: * int | None: The first parsed integer index, or None if no numeric digits are detected.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly; unparseable non-digit representations safely return None.

Example: 

def parse_file_index(idx_value):
    """Extract the first integer from an LLM-returned file index value.

    Handles multiple formats the LLM may produce:
    - Plain int: 3
    - Annotated string: "3 # path/to/file.py"
    - Range notation: "0-3" → returns first number only (caller handles ranges)

    Returns:
        int or None if no digits found.
    """
    nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(idx_value))
    return int(nums[0]) if nums else None

Under the hood, parse_file_index() coerces idx_value to a string using str(idx_value) before running re.findall(r"\d+", ...). This design accommodates heterogeneous types produced by YAML deserialization, such as native Python integers, floats, or raw strings. If multiple numeric segments exist (such as range notations like "0-3" or annotated lines like "12 # src/utils/token.py:44"), it deliberately selects the first integer group nums[0]. Downstream callers in nodes.py handle higher-level range expansion or index validation against the repository's file list.

docs.title: load_prompt_template()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None) -> str:

Description: Locates and loads a Markdown prompt template file from the repository's prompts/ directory hierarchy. The function resolves the target subdirectory based on explicit execution modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk, or common) with backward-compatible fallback behavior for legacy boolean flags. It reads the file using the utf-8-sig encoding to eliminate Byte Order Marks and emits an operational debug trace to the disk audit log.

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base name of the Markdown template file without the .md extension (e.g., "identify_abstractions", "draft_chapters"). * advanced_mode (bool, optional): Legacy fallback flag used when mode is None. If True, resolves to the "advanced" directory; otherwise defaults to "tutorial". Defaults to False. * mode (str | None, optional): The execution mode string specifying the target subdirectory inside prompts/. Overrides advanced_mode when provided. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The decoded text content of the target Markdown template file.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the resolved template path does not exist on disk. * OSError: If the filesystem encounters an I/O error while reading the file.

Example: 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        content = f.read()
    from utils.output import emit_raw

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"load_prompt_template | loaded '{template_name}.md' from prompts/{prompt_dir}/", dest="LOG")
    return content

The function computes the absolute root path of the project using os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), navigating two levels up from utils/ to ensure path resolution remains invariant regardless of the current working directory. Opening with utf-8-sig guarantees that Markdown templates authored or modified across different operating systems—specifically Windows text editors that introduce a UTF-8 BOM—do not inject hidden zero-width non-breaking spaces (\ufeff) into the prompt payload. The logging invocation uses a deferred local import (from utils.output import emit_raw) with dest="LOG", routing prompt loading traces strictly to file logs without polluting interactive console output.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response) -> Any:

Description: Extracts, strips, and deserializes a YAML document enclosed within triple-backtick Markdown fences (```yaml ... ```) from an LLM completion response. Prior to extraction, it checks for a truncated attribute on the response object; if detected, it aborts execution immediately by raising a ValueError. This protects upstream pipeline nodes from parsing incomplete YAML payloads that could silently drop classes, modules, or chapter mappings.

Parameters: * response (str | Any): The raw string response from the LLM or an instance of a string subclass (such as TruncatedResponse from llm_common.py).

Returns: * Any: The deserialized Python data structure (typically a list or dict) produced by yaml.safe_load.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the response was flagged as truncated (getattr(response, "truncated", False) is True), if the response lacks the ```yaml code block delimiter, or if yaml.safe_load fails to parse the extracted string.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    # A reply cut off at max tokens (llm_common.TruncatedResponse) can still contain a parseable
    # fenced prefix that silently drops items — raise so the node retries instead.
    if getattr(response, "truncated", False):
        raise ValueError("LLM response was truncated before the YAML block completed")
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

The method isolates the YAML block by performing sequential string splits: splitting on "```yaml" to isolate the opening fence, selecting index 1, splitting on "```" to strip trailing text, and taking index 0. Wrapping the parsing logic in a broad try-except block guarantees that formatting irregularities—such as missing closing backticks, unclosed quotes, invalid indentation, or an absent ```yaml delimiter—are consistently re-raised as ValueError instances containing the underlying exception message. This exception model signals the calling graph node in nodes.py that retry escalation or model re-prompting is required.

docs.title: build_code_file_filter_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:

Description: Constructs a specialized, self-contained prompt string used by the DeterministicFileMapper node in api-reference mode. The prompt instructs the LLM to analyze a formatted codebase file listing and filter out non-code assets (such as UI markups, build manifests, configuration files, and static assets), returning exclusively the numeric indices of files containing functional source code, classes, and APIs.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The name or identifier of the project being documented. * file_listing (str): A pre-formatted string of indexed repository files (typically formatted as index-path pairs, such as "0: src/main.py\n1: config.json").

Returns: * str: The complete prompt payload formatted with system instructions, exclusion constraints, and a few-shot YAML schema example.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    """Build the prompt for DeterministicFileMapper to filter non-code files.

    Used in api-reference mode to identify which files are actual code modules
    (APIs, functions, classes, business logic) vs. UI layouts, configs, assets.
    """
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:\n\n"
        f"{file_listing}\n\n"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.\n"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices that should be documented as code modules.\n\n"
        f"```yaml\n- 0\n- 1\n- 3\n```"
    )

The constructed prompt enforces strict categorical exclusions directly in the natural language contract, explicitly listing extensions and file classes that must be omitted (.xaml, .storyboard, .html, .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini, .csproj, .sln). The prompt terminates with a few-shot example instructing the model to wrap its output in a fenced ```yaml block containing an array of integers. This strict output framing guarantees compatibility with downstream processing by parse_yaml_response().

docs.title: build_chapter_summary_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:

Description: Constructs a structured prompt instructing the model to synthesize a technical brief of an already generated chapter. This brief is fed into the context of subsequent chapter generation passes, maintaining architectural continuity across the documentation set. The prompt enforces a uniform summary structure spanning four distinct technical dimensions: scope and responsibility, key technical elements, implementation patterns and architecture, and system integration and dependencies.

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): The 1-based numerical index of the chapter being summarized. * abstraction_name (str): The title, architectural concept, or module name of the chapter. * chapter_content (str): The complete Markdown source code of the drafted chapter. * language (str, optional): The target natural language for the output summary. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: The assembled prompt payload ready for submission to the LLM.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly.

Example: 

def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:
    """Build the prompt for generating a technical summary of a written chapter.

    Used after each chapter is generated to create a concise technical summary
    for cross-chapter context. The summary is fed into subsequent chapters'
    prompts so the LLM maintains coherence across the full document.

    The summary captures 4 technical dimensions with 3-5 sentences each:
    1. Component scope & responsibility
    2. Key classes/services/functions and their roles
    3. Implementation patterns & architectural decisions
    4. Inter-component interfaces & dependencies
    """
    lang_instruction = f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )

The prompt construction logic conditionally prepends an internationalization instruction (lang_instruction) when language differs from "english". It explicitly requires that each of the four numbered dimensions contains between 3 and 5 concise sentences, constraining the LLM from generating overly verbose prose that could exhaust the token budget of subsequent chapter prompts. Appending Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name} alongside the raw Markdown ensures that the model preserves domain terminology and component identifiers accurately.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements focused error validation centered around LLM output safety and filesystem access:

  • Truncation Detection (ValueError): In parse_yaml_response(), the function checks for response truncation via getattr(response, "truncated", False). When an upstream provider driver flags that output was cut off mid-stream due to max token limits (such as TruncatedResponse in llm_common.py), the function immediately raises a ValueError("LLM response was truncated before the YAML block completed"). This prevents partial YAML lists from passing as valid completions, which would silently omit files or pipeline entities.
  • Malformed YAML Extraction (ValueError): In parse_yaml_response(), missing ```yaml code fences or invalid syntax inside the block raises ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e. The original parsing or splitting exception is chained using from e to preserve diagnostic stack traces for debugging.
  • Missing Prompt Templates (FileNotFoundError): If load_prompt_template() attempts to read a non-existent template file, Python's native FileNotFoundError propagates to the caller, highlighting missing template files across mode directories (prompts/advanced/, prompts/tutorial/, prompts/api-reference/, prompts/sdk/).
  • Defensive Index Extraction: parse_file_index() treats malformed, non-numeric, or missing index representations defensively, returning None instead of throwing IndexError or ValueError.
